modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.auth
modules.summary: Sign-in, sign-up and the account, as code (``docs/auth-harmonization.md`` §8 in ``Eifi1/ui-kit``).

links.heading: 8. What the kits add, what stays app-side

members.name: ABSENT_ACCOUNT_SECRET_BYTES
members.doc: The random bytes behind the dummy hash's password (keksdose ``secrets.token_urlsafe(32)``).

members.name: ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES
members.doc: The same, in the minutes the apps' settings hold (``access_token_expire_minutes``).

members.name: ACCESS_TOKEN_LIFETIME
members.doc:
The session's two lifetimes, the defaults of each app's settings (§6.2, §10.3).
keksdose and Kurvenschmiede run these; kastlan keeps 15 minutes of access until its
per-request check exists.

members.name: ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE
members.doc:
The ``type`` claim of each JWT; every consumer discriminates on it, so a refresh
token is never accepted as an access token, nor a challenge as either.

members.name: AUTH_ERROR_DETAIL
members.signature:
AUTH_ERROR_DETAIL: Mapping[AuthErrorCode, str] = {
    AuthErrorCode.INVALID_CREDENTIALS: "Invalid credentials",
    AuthErrorCode.REGISTRATION_CLOSED: "Registration is by invitation only",
    AuthErrorCode.EMAIL_TAKEN: "Email already registered",
    AuthErrorCode.INVITATION_INVALID: "This invitation is not valid",
    AuthErrorCode.INVITATION_EXPIRED: "This invitation has expired",
    AuthErrorCode.TOKEN_INVALID: "This link is invalid or has expired",
    AuthErrorCode.TOKEN_EXPIRED: "This link has expired",
    # Kurvenschmiede's ``TokenRefusal.ENDED`` (``auth_service.py:187``).
    AuthErrorCode.SESSION_ENDED: "This session has ended. Please sign in again.",
}
members.doc:
The English ``detail`` of each code, keksdose's words where it had them. The pages
show the kit's own text for the code; this is for logs and API clients.

members.name: AUTH_ERROR_STATUS
members.signature:
AUTH_ERROR_STATUS: Mapping[AuthErrorCode, int] = {
    AuthErrorCode.INVALID_CREDENTIALS: 401,
    AuthErrorCode.REGISTRATION_CLOSED: 403,
    AuthErrorCode.EMAIL_TAKEN: 409,
    AuthErrorCode.INVITATION_INVALID: 400,
    AuthErrorCode.INVITATION_EXPIRED: 400,
    AuthErrorCode.TOKEN_INVALID: 400,
    AuthErrorCode.TOKEN_EXPIRED: 400,
    AuthErrorCode.SESSION_ENDED: 401,
}
members.doc:
Each code's status. The token codes are ``400`` as keksdose answers a bad reset or
verification link today; the page tells them apart by ``code``, not by status. A
refresh's refusal is ``401``, never ``403``: the three apps' refresh routes already
answer so (auth §11.1).

members.name: CHALLENGE_LIFETIMES
members.doc:
How long a challenge lasts (keksdose): five minutes to copy a code out of an app that
is already open; ten to invent, type and confirm a password.

members.name: CHALLENGE_PER_IP
members.doc:
``/auth/login/2fa`` and ``/auth/login/set-password``, per IP (keksdose
``_challenge_ip_limiter``): a six-digit code behind an open endpoint is 10^6 guesses.

members.name: CHALLENGE_PER_SUBJECT
members.doc:
The same two, per challenge subject — the window a header cannot re-key (keksdose
``_challenge_subject_limiter``).

members.name: CONTRAST_MODES
members.doc:
The contrast modes in the settings card's order (text-size §10.6). ``"system"`` is one
of them, because the PATCH rule refuses an explicit ``null``: without it, somebody who
picked "More" could never go back to following the device.

members.name: DEFAULT_LOCALE
members.doc:
What a new account is written to in when the form did not say: the UI's German, the
kit's fallback language (i18n H7).

members.name: EMAIL_CHANGE_TOKEN_KIND
members.doc: The email change's kind, by the name the user-admin contract gives it (§7).

members.name: EMAIL_CHANGE_TTL
members.doc:
An email change's confirmation link, mailed to the NEW address (user-admin §6.2). As
long as a verification link, because it proves the same thing — that the mailbox is
theirs — and the address does not change until it is redeemed.

members.name: FAMILY_NAME_FIRST
members.doc: The languages that write the family name first (§3.2): Hungarian with a space…

members.name: FAMILY_NAME_FIRST_NO_SPACE
members.doc: …and Chinese without one.

members.name: INVITE_TTL
members.doc: An invitation (keksdose ``budget_share_service.INVITE_TTL``, §4.4).

members.name: LOCALE_PATTERN
members.doc:
A locale tag as the UI sends it — ``de-CH``, ``en``, ``zh-Hans`` (keksdose
``ProfileUpdateRequest.locale``). Not a list of shipped languages: an app narrows it.

members.name: LOGIN_FAILURES_FREE
members.doc: Failures per address that cost nothing: a person mistyping a password a few times.

members.name: LOGIN_FAILURE_BASE_DELAY
members.doc: The delay after the first failure past the free ones, doubling with each further one…

members.name: LOGIN_FAILURE_MAX_DELAY
members.doc: …up to this, in seconds. The owner under attack waits at most this long, never more.

members.name: LOGIN_FAILURE_WINDOW_SECONDS
members.doc: How long a failure is remembered.

members.name: LOGIN_PER_IP
members.doc:
``/auth/login`` and the passkey finish, per IP — the hard limit, charged BEFORE the
password check so a shed request costs no bcrypt (keksdose ``_login_ip_limiter``).

members.name: MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH
members.doc: RFC 5321's path limit, less the angle brackets.

members.name: MAX_NAME_LENGTH
members.doc:
First and last name, after trimming (§3.1): the old ``display_name`` limit, so a
migrated name fits.

members.name: MAX_PASSWORD_BYTES
members.doc:
bcrypt hashes at most 72 BYTES, and bcrypt 5 RAISES past it in both the hash and the
check (keksdose ``infrastructure/security.py`` ``BCRYPT_MAX_PASSWORD_BYTES``).

members.name: MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH
members.doc: The one hard rule a NEW password has (keksdose feedback #124); any checklist is advisory.

members.name: ONE_TIME_TOKEN_BYTES
members.doc: Entropy of a one-time token's random part; ``token_urlsafe(32)`` is 43 characters.

members.name: ONE_TIME_TOKEN_TTLS
members.doc: Each kind's lifetime.

members.name: PROFILE_CLAIMS
members.doc: What an access token must not carry (§6.2): the profile is read from ``/auth/me``.

members.name: PROFILE_NOT_NULLABLE
members.doc:
The fields of :class:`ProfileUpdate` that a PATCH may leave out but never null. The
text size and the contrast are among them (text-size §10.6): their ``null`` means only
"never chosen", which a person cannot choose — "System" is a value of its own.

members.name: REGISTER_PER_IP
members.doc:
``/auth/register``, per IP: the other endpoint that hashes (Kurvenschmiede
``REGISTRATION_ATTEMPTS``).

members.name: RESERVED_CLAIMS
members.doc: The claims a builder sets itself; ``extra`` may not override them.

members.name: RESET_PER_IP
members.doc:
``/auth/password-reset/request``: 10 an hour per IP asking, 3 an hour per address
asked about (keksdose, kastlan). Two windows, because neither covers the other: the
first bounds one client trying address after address, the second keeps a victim's
inbox quiet when the requests come from everywhere. The second is keyed by the
SUBMITTED address, whether or not it has an account, so it is no existence oracle.

members.name: RESET_TTL
members.doc: A password-reset link (keksdose ``password_reset_service.TOKEN_TTL``).

members.name: TAG_SEPARATOR
members.doc: What stands between a local part and its tag (RFC 5233 sub-addressing).

members.name: TEXT_SIZES
members.doc:
The text sizes in the settings card's order (text-size §10.6) — the kit's
``TextSizeSetting`` offers the same three.

members.name: VERIFICATION_RESEND_PER_RECIPIENT
members.doc:
``/auth/resend-verification``, per RECIPIENT address, not per IP (keksdose
``_resend_email_limiter``): what it protects is that inbox and the sender's reputation.

members.name: VERIFY_TTL
members.doc: An email-verification link (keksdose ``settings.email_verification_ttl_hours = 48``).

members.name: AuthError
members.doc:
A coded refusal: ``status_code`` and ``code`` from :class:`AuthErrorCode`.

``AuthError(AuthErrorCode.EMAIL_TAKEN)`` is a 409 with the code's English detail; pass
``detail`` to say more. A ``ValueError`` like every kit refusal, and registered in
:data:`~eifi1_server_kit.errors.CONTRACT_ERRORS`, so an app-wide ``ValueError`` → 400
handler does not swallow its status.

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(code: AuthErrorCode, detail: str | None = None) -> None

members.name: AuthErrorCode
members.doc: The ``code`` of a refusal (§5.2). A ``StrEnum``, so ``str(code)`` is the wire value.

members.name: AuthLimiters
members.doc:
Every budget of the signed-out routes, built once per app.

``login`` (per IP), ``login_failures`` (per address, a delay — see
:class:`LoginFailureThrottle`), ``challenge`` (per IP) and ``challenge_subject`` (per
user id of the challenge token) for the 2FA and set-password steps, ``register`` (per
IP), ``reset_ip`` and ``reset_address`` for the reset request, and
``verification_resend`` (per recipient). Charge an IP window with ``hit`` and answer a
non-``None`` result with ``429`` and ``Retry-After``
(:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.limiter.retry_after_header`); charge it BEFORE any hashing,
so a shed request costs no bcrypt. Key every address window by
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.normalise_email` of what was submitted.

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(*, login: Budget = LOGIN_PER_IP, challenge: Budget = CHALLENGE_PER_IP, challenge_subject: Budget = CHALLENGE_PER_SUBJECT, register: Budget = REGISTER_PER_IP, reset_ip: Budget = RESET_PER_IP, reset_address: Budget = RESET_PER_ADDRESS, verification_resend: Budget = VERIFICATION_RESEND_PER_RECIPIENT, login_failures: LoginFailureThrottle | None = None, clock: Clock = time.monotonic) -> None

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Empty every window — the test seam.

members.name: Budget
members.doc: At most ``max_hits`` per key in any ``window_seconds``.

members.name: ChallengeKind
members.doc: The ``type`` of a sign-in challenge token (keksdose ``infrastructure/security.py``).

members.name: ContrastMode
members.doc:
A contrast mode as stored on the account (text-size §2.4, §10.6). ``"system"`` follows
the device's ``prefers-contrast``; it is a stored value, not the absence of one.

members.name: Email
members.signature:
Email = Annotated[
    str,
    BeforeValidator(_normalised),
    Field(max_length=MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH),
    AfterValidator(_plausible_email),
]
members.doc:
An address as it comes in: trimmed, lower-cased (a ``+tag`` kept), then checked for
shape — every entry normalises (§3.1).

members.name: ExistingPassword
members.doc:
An EXISTING password presented for checking: no minimum (the account may predate the
rule), the same ceiling — an over-long one could not have been set (keksdose
``ExistingPassword``).

members.name: LocaleTag
members.doc: A locale tag (:data:`LOCALE_PATTERN`).

members.name: LoginFailureThrottle
members.doc:
Failed sign-ins per address: counted, and answered with a delay, never a lockout.

Per request to ``/auth/login``, with the SUBMITTED address — whether or not it has an
account, so an unknown address and a known one cost the same (§5.2's "one error, in
the same time")::

    await asyncio.sleep(limiters.login_failures.delay(payload.email))
    user = await authenticate(...)
    if user is None:
        limiters.login_failures.record_failure(payload.email)
        raise AuthError(AuthErrorCode.INVALID_CREDENTIALS)
    limiters.login_failures.clear(payload.email)

**Wait BEFORE checking the password**, for every attempt on that address — not only
after a failure. A delay on failures alone is visible as one: an attacker gives up
on each answer after a few milliseconds and reads silence as "wrong". Waiting first
holds the right answer back exactly as long as the wrong one.

What it does not do: bound a botnet. Parallel requests each wait, and no
per-address rule can stop them without becoming the lockout this avoids — the IP
window is the hard limit. Addresses are normalised here, so ``Ada@Example.com`` and
``ada@example.com`` count together.

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(*, free: int = LOGIN_FAILURES_FREE, base_delay: float = LOGIN_FAILURE_BASE_DELAY, max_delay: float = LOGIN_FAILURE_MAX_DELAY, window_seconds: float = LOGIN_FAILURE_WINDOW_SECONDS, clock: Clock = time.monotonic) -> None

methods.name: delay
methods.doc: Seconds to wait before answering this attempt on ``email``.

methods.name: record_failure
methods.doc: Count a failed attempt: an unknown address, a wrong password, a deactivated account.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc:
A successful sign-in forgets the address's failures, so the owner's own typos
stop costing them once they are in.

members.name: LoginRequest
members.doc: ``POST /auth/login {email, password}`` (§5.1; keksdose ``UserLogin``).

members.name: MintedToken
members.doc: A fresh one-time token: ``raw`` goes into the mail, once; ``digest`` into the table.

members.name: NewPassword
members.doc:
A NEW password: 8 characters at least, 72 bytes at most — a clean 422 where a password
is SET, because truncating would let two passwords open one account (keksdose
``schemas/auth.py`` ``NewPassword``).

members.name: OneTimeTokenKind
members.doc:
What a one-time token is FOR — the ``kind`` column of an app's token table, and the
``kind`` its mail is logged under (:meth:`eifi1_server_kit.mail.Mailer.send`).

Every kind follows the same recipe (:func:`mint`, :func:`hash_token`,
:func:`is_expired`) at its own lifetime, :data:`ONE_TIME_TOKEN_TTLS`.

members.name: PasswordChangeChallenge
members.doc:
The sign-in passed; the account must choose a new password before it gets a
session (§5.1; keksdose ``PasswordChangeChallengeResponse``) →
``POST /auth/login/set-password``.

A DIFFERENT discriminator from :class:`TwoFactorChallenge` on purpose: a client
narrows the ``/auth/login`` union on the field's name. App fields ride along in a
subclass — keksdose's ``encrypted`` — and the kit's form passes them through.

members.name: PersonName
members.doc: A first or last name: 1–120 characters after trimming, any script (§3.1).

members.name: ProfileUpdate
members.doc:
``PATCH /auth/me {first_name?, last_name?, locale?, text_size?, contrast?}`` (§6.1;
Kurvenschmiede ``ProfileUpdate``; ``docs/text-size-harmonization.md`` §6, §10.6).

Every field optional, so the language picker writes the locale alone, and the text-size
and contrast cards write theirs alone (a pick writes the device and the account). Unknown fields
are refused (``extra="forbid"``): the obvious next field somebody sends is ``role``
or ``email``, and a schema that silently ignored it would read as having accepted it.
An explicit ``null`` is refused too — a name cannot be cleared, and
``model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`` would otherwise carry it onto a NOT NULL column.
Write it with :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.settings.apply_patch` and
:data:`PROFILE_NOT_NULLABLE` (settings §6.1).

**The locale, from the app's languages** (settings §6.2): set :attr:`offered_locales`
in a subclass — or build the class with
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.settings.profile_update_model` — and the locale goes through
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.settings.canonical_locale`: ``de_ch`` is stored as ``de-CH``,
``de`` as the offered German, and a language the app doesn't offer is a 422. Unset,
only the tag's shape is checked, as before.

fields.name: text_size
fields.doc: One of :data:`TEXT_SIZES`; left out keeps the account's, ``null`` is refused.

fields.name: contrast
fields.doc: One of :data:`CONTRAST_MODES`; left out keeps the account's, ``null`` is refused.

fields.name: offered_locales
fields.doc:
The app's languages in its menu's order (``("de-CH", "en", "fr", "it")``); ``None``
checks the tag's shape only (:data:`LOCALE_PATTERN`).

members.name: RefreshRequest
members.doc:
``POST /auth/refresh {refresh_token}`` (auth §6.2, §11; keksdose, kastlan and
Kurvenschmiede ``RefreshRequest``, field for field).

The token is plain text, with no length rule: an empty or malformed one is the
route's ``401 {code: "session_ended"}``, never a 422. ui-kit's
``attachSessionRefresh`` reads a 422 as a client fault that a sign-out would not mend
(transient), so a 422 here would leave a device that holds a broken token signed in,
refreshing at every request. What the route answers is
:mod:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.tokens`' "Refreshing a session".

members.name: RegisterRequest
members.doc:
``POST /auth/register`` (§4.2; keksdose ``UserCreate``).

``{email, password, first_name, last_name, locale, invite_token?}`` plus the app's
fields in its subclass (kastlan's company, keksdose's currency). Unknown fields are
refused: a role or a company id sent by a client is a 422, not silently dropped —
they come from the invitation or the app's default, never from the form (§4.3).

fields.name: invite_token
fields.doc:
``/register?invite=<token>`` (§4.4); its mail address must accept ``email``
(:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.invitation_accepts`).

members.name: RegistrationDecision
members.doc: What :func:`registration_decision` answers.

members.name: TextSize
members.doc:
A text size as stored on the account (``docs/text-size-harmonization.md`` §2.1,
§10.6): 100, 125 and 150 % of the browser's own font size.

members.name: TokenResponse
members.doc:
A session (§5.1; keksdose ``TokenResponse``): ``{access_token, refresh_token,
token_type, user, expires_at}``.

``refresh_token`` is ``None`` for a session that cannot be renewed — the demo
(``docs/landing-demo-harmonization.md`` §5.3), whose access token lives to the demo
account's end. ``expires_at`` says when the access token ends; the demo MUST send it,
because the client's countdown and its end page run from it and the client never
decodes the JWT (§5.3). ``user`` is the app's :class:`UserResponse` subclass —
``TokenResponse[MyUserResponse]`` — and ``Any`` unparametrised. An app that boots
offline reads the user from here, so it carries ``name_incomplete`` too (§3.3).

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc:
When the access token ends, ISO-8601 in UTC: set for a demo session
(:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.demo.demo_expires_at`); optional for any other.

members.name: TwoFactorChallenge
members.doc:
The password was right; the second factor is next (§5.1; keksdose
``TwoFactorChallengeResponse``) → ``POST /auth/login/2fa {challenge_token, code}``.

members.name: UserResponse
members.doc:
``GET /auth/me`` (§6.1): the core every app answers; subclass to add its own.

``display_name`` and ``name_incomplete`` are DERIVED and read-only: computed from
``first_name`` / ``last_name`` on every serialisation, never accepted as input. The
display name is written in the user's own ``locale`` — this is the user reading about
themselves; the kit formats from first and last name on screen, in the reader's
language, and uses ``display_name`` only as a fallback (§3.2).

``role`` is the app's vocabulary; narrow it to the app's enum in the subclass.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: As stored — already normalised; not re-validated on the way out.

fields.name: last_name
fields.doc: May be ``""`` on a migrated account until the name is completed (§3.3).

fields.name: demo_expires_at
fields.doc:
When a demo account ends, ISO-8601 in UTC (landing-demo §5.3): ``created_at`` plus
the maximum age, :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.demo.demo_expires_at`. ``None`` for a real
account. The ORM row rarely has it, so the app passes it — a property on its model
read through ``from_attributes``, or ``model_copy(update=…)``.

fields.name: text_size
fields.doc:
The account's text size (text-size §6, §10.6); ``None`` = never chosen, so a device
without its own choice uses Normal. The app's column, read through
``from_attributes``; an app without the column yet answers ``None``.

fields.name: contrast
fields.doc:
The account's contrast mode (text-size §6, §10.6); ``None`` = never chosen, which
reads as ``"system"``.

methods.name: display_name
methods.doc: The name in the user's language (:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.full_name`).

methods.name: name_incomplete
methods.doc: Either part empty — the app shows ``CompleteNameDialog`` after sign-in (§3.3).

methods.name: name_completion_exempt
methods.doc:
Override to exempt an account from completing its name — keksdose's demo
session (``return self.is_demo``, §3.3).

members.name: UtcDateTime
members.doc:
An instant on the wire, always ISO-8601 in UTC (``2026-10-08T09:00:00Z``): the client
counts down to it (landing-demo §5.3), so it must never be a local time without an
offset, which a browser would read in ITS zone.

members.name: absent_account_check
members.signature: absent_account_check[H](hash_password: Callable[[str], H], verify_password: Callable[[str, H], object], *, cost: Callable[[], Hashable] | None = None) -> Callable[[str], bool]
members.doc:
A check for the address with no account: the same work a real check does, and
``False``, always. Built from the app's own two functions::

    check_absent = absent_account_check(hash_password, verify_password)
    ...
    user = await get_user_by_email(session, email)
    if user is None:
        check_absent(password)  # False, after one verify against the dummy hash
        return None
    password_ok = verify_password(password, user.password_hash)

Four rules, which the three apps each kept in their own way (KS S3):

* the dummy is the hash of a **random** secret (:data:`ABSENT_ACCOUNT_SECRET_BYTES`,
  keksdose's), never a string in a source file (kastlan's
  ``"kastlan-no-such-account"``), which a seed or a fixture could one day make
  somebody's password (Kurvenschmiede: "so it can never be mistaken for a
  credential");
* it is built **lazily**, at the first unknown address, so it carries the cost
  ``hash_password`` hashes at then, not at import — keksdose's suite lowers bcrypt's
  rounds once it has started. ``cost`` is the app's cost, read at every call
  (``cost=lambda: get_settings().bcrypt_rounds``, Kurvenschmiede's): when it changes
  the dummy is built again, so a dummy at a cost the real rows aren't checked at can't
  bring the difference back. Without it, the dummy is built once;
* it goes through the app's **own** ``verify_password``, so whatever that refuses
  without hashing — a password past bcrypt's 72 bytes — is refused here without
  hashing too: a short-circuit on one path only is the same oracle in a narrower
  doorway;
* it answers **False**, whatever the password, so it can stand where the real check
  stands.

Two threads at the first unknown address may each build a dummy; the last one stays,
and both are random. The returned callable holds one dummy at a time.

members.name: access_claims
members.signature: access_claims(sub: int | str, *, now: datetime, lifetime: timedelta = ACCESS_TOKEN_LIFETIME, extra: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]
members.doc:
The payload of an access token (keksdose ``auth_service.issue_access_token``).

``{sub, type: "access", iat, exp, **extra}``. ``iat`` is ``now`` with its fraction of
a second; ``exp`` is whole seconds. ``extra`` is what the app needs to authorise —
keksdose's ``role``, kastlan's ``company_id``, ``roles`` and ``sid`` — and may not set
the four claims above, nor a name, an email or a locale (:data:`PROFILE_CLAIMS`).

members.name: addresses_for_reset
members.doc:
The addresses a password-reset request looks up, in order (§4.5).

The submitted address first; if it finds no account, its tagged variant — a user who
took the tag at sign-up and forgot it still gets the link. The mail goes to the
account's OWN address (the tagged one), and the answer is ``204`` either way.

members.name: challenge_claims
members.signature: challenge_claims(sub: int | str, kind: ChallengeKind, *, now: datetime) -> dict[str, Any]
members.doc:
The payload of a sign-in challenge token, at its kind's lifetime (keksdose
``create_2fa_challenge_token`` / ``create_password_change_challenge_token``).

Single-purpose through its ``type``: ``get_current_user`` and ``/auth/refresh`` refuse
it, and each challenge endpoint accepts only its own kind.

members.name: env_list_match
members.signature: env_list_match(email: str, env_list: Iterable[str]) -> bool | None
members.doc:
``on_env_list`` for :func:`registration_decision`: ``None`` when no list is set,
else whether the normalised address is on it.

members.name: erasure_identifiers
members.signature: erasure_identifiers(email: str | None, first: str | None, last: str | None, old_display_name: str | None = None) -> list[str]
members.doc:
A person's own strings, for :func:`eifi1_server_kit.feedback.anonymise_feedback`'s
``identifiers`` (§8, §10.6).

The email, the old ``display_name`` (what a stamp written before the switch holds),
and the full name in every order :func:`full_name` writes it — "First Last",
"Last First", and zh's "LastFirst" — because the feedback stamp is frozen in its
AUTHOR's language. **Never a bare first or last name**: redacting "Mai" or "Bank"
on its own would shred a report that mentions the month or the bank. With a part
missing, the full-name forms are left out; the old display name covers a migrated
account.

De-duplicated case-insensitively and ordered LONGEST FIRST, because
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.scrub_text` replaces needles one after another: an
old display name "Ada Lovelace" replaced before "Ada Lovelace-Byron" would leave
"[erased]-Byron" behind.

members.name: first_name_of
members.signature: first_name_of(first: str | None, last: str | None) -> str | None
members.doc:
The name other people see (feedback §9.5): ``first`` trimmed when ``last`` is not
blank, otherwise ``None``.

**No first-word guessing**: "王小明", "Dr. Anna Muster" and "Muster, Anna" all break it.
An account whose old display name moved whole into ``first_name`` (keksdose 0114,
Kurvenschmiede) is :func:`name_incomplete` and shows no name until it completes it;
``None`` is drawn as "A user", the same as an erased author.

members.name: full_name
members.signature: full_name(first: str | None, last: str | None, locale: str | None) -> str
members.doc:
A person's name in the order of ``locale``'s language (§3.2).

"First Last" in de-CH, en, fr, it and es (and any language not listed); "Last First"
in hu; "LastFirst" with no space in zh — but only for a name written in CJK script in
both parts: a zh reader sees "Ada Lovelace" as written, never "LovelaceAda". Both
parts are trimmed; an empty part leaves the other alone, so a migrated account whose
``last_name`` is still empty shows its old display name as it was.

Whose language: the READER's on screen (the kit formats there; the API's
``display_name`` is a fallback), the RECIPIENT's in a mail or a push, the AUTHOR's in
a copy frozen when it was written — the feedback stamp (§3.2, §10.6).

members.name: hash_token
members.doc:
The SHA-256 hex digest a one-time token is stored and looked up by (64 characters;
keksdose ``password_reset_service.hash_token``).

members.name: invitation_accepts
members.signature: invitation_accepts(invited: str, registered: str, tag: str) -> bool
members.doc:
May ``registered`` redeem an invitation for ``invited``? (§4.5)

The exact address, or the same local part with the app's own tag on the same domain
— ``you@example.com`` accepts ``you+kastlan@example.com`` for kastlan — and nothing
else: not another tag, not another domain, not the untagged address of a tagged
invitation. Both sides are normalised first.

members.name: is_expired
members.signature: is_expired(issued_at: datetime, ttl: timedelta, now: datetime) -> bool
members.doc:
Has a token issued at ``issued_at`` with lifetime ``ttl`` run out at ``now``?

Expired AT the boundary, as keksdose's ``expires_at <= utcnow()``. Naive datetimes
are read as UTC.

members.name: login_failure_delay
members.signature: login_failure_delay(failures: int, *, free: int = LOGIN_FAILURES_FREE, base: float = LOGIN_FAILURE_BASE_DELAY, cap: float = LOGIN_FAILURE_MAX_DELAY) -> float
members.doc:
Seconds to hold a sign-in for an address with ``failures`` failures in the window.

``0`` for the first ``free``; then ``base``, doubling per failure, never above
``cap``. With the defaults: five free, then 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 30 seconds.

members.name: mint
members.doc:
A fresh one-time token and its digest: ``raw, digest = mint()``.

``prefix`` is optional — letters or digits ending in ``_`` — for an app that wants to
tell its tokens apart where they are pasted; keksdose's links carry none.

members.name: name_incomplete
members.signature: name_incomplete(first: str | None, last: str | None, *, is_demo: bool = False) -> bool
members.doc:
``/auth/me``'s ``name_incomplete`` (§3.3): either part empty after trimming.

A demo session never counts as incomplete (keksdose's anonymous demo has nobody to
ask), so ``is_demo=True`` is always ``False``.

members.name: normalise_email
members.doc:
``raw`` trimmed and lower-cased — and nothing else (§3.1, §4.5).

Never strips a ``+tag`` and never folds dots: the tagged address is the identity the
user signs in with, and a provider's own aliasing rules are not ours to guess.

members.name: parse_env_list
members.doc:
The bootstrap list from an environment variable: addresses separated by commas
and/or whitespace, normalised (keksdose ``auth_service._registration_allowlist``).

members.name: refresh_claims
members.signature: refresh_claims(sub: int | str, *, now: datetime, lifetime: timedelta = REFRESH_TOKEN_LIFETIME, extra: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]
members.doc:
The payload of a refresh token (keksdose ``auth_service.issue_refresh_token``).

``{sub, type: "refresh", iat, exp, **extra}``. The ``iat`` is what makes a stateless
session revocable at all: a reset or a password change stamps
``sessions_invalid_before``, and :func:`token_is_revoked` compares the two. It keeps
its fraction of a second because with whole seconds a user who resets and signs
straight back in gets a token stamped in the cut-off's second, and the check throws
the brand-new session away; rounding the other way lets an old session survive by up
to a second.

members.name: registration_decision
members.signature: registration_decision(*, is_first_user: bool, on_env_list: bool | None, has_valid_invitation: bool) -> RegistrationDecision
members.doc:
May this address register, and as what? (§4.3, §2.12)

* **The first account ever** becomes the admin — unless the app has an environment
  list (``on_env_list`` is not ``None``) that does not name it. That is the list's one
  job now: who may claim a fresh deployment, so a stranger who finds it first
  cannot. ``None`` means the app has no list, and the first registration is open, as
  in keksdose today. Build the argument with :func:`env_list_match`.
* **After that**, only a valid invitation lets anyone in — an allow-list entry is an
  invitation, so the app passes ``True`` for one. The environment list grants
  nothing any more.
* Everyone else: :attr:`RegistrationDecision.CLOSED`, answered as
  ``AuthError(AuthErrorCode.REGISTRATION_CLOSED)``.

The role and the associations never come from the form: from the invitation, the
allow-list row, or the app's default (§4.3).

members.name: tagged_variant
members.signature: tagged_variant(email: str, tag: str) -> str | None
members.doc:
``you@example.com`` → ``you+<tag>@example.com``, normalised; ``None`` when there is
nothing to offer (keksdose ``email-tag.ts`` ``taggedEmail``, §4.5).

``None`` when the address already carries a ``+`` — their own scheme wins, and
stacking two would be wrong — or is not complete enough to split. ``tag`` is the
app's name; anything but letters, digits, ``.``, ``_`` and ``-`` is a
:class:`ValueError` (a programming error, not a user's).

members.name: token_is_revoked
members.signature: token_is_revoked(claims_iat: object, sessions_invalid_before: datetime | None) -> bool
members.doc:
Was this token — access or refresh — minted at or before the account's cut-off?
(keksdose ``auth_service.token_is_revoked``, Kurvenschmiede's line for line.)

Call it with ``claims.get("iat")`` on EVERY request (``get_current_user``) and on
refresh: ending only the refresh chain leaves a tab with an access token signed in
for the rest of its lifetime.

* No cut-off: never revoked.
* The comparison is exact, to the microsecond: a token minted after the cut-off in
  the same second survives — the user who resets and signs straight back in — and
  one minted at the cut-off itself does not.
* Fails CLOSED on a token with no ``iat``, or one that is not a number: only an
  account that has had a cut-off gets this far, so "I cannot tell when this was
  issued" has to mean "before". The cost is one extra sign-in for a stale tab.

Not a query: the caller has loaded the user to authenticate at all, and the cut-off
is a column on it. A naive cut-off (SQLite) is read as UTC.

members.name: verified_by_invitation
members.doc:
Does registering through this invitation prove the mailbox? Only for the exact
invited address (§4.3, §10.7).

The token reached ``you@x``, which says nothing about whether ``you+app@x`` is
delivered — not every server implements sub-addressing — so a tagged registration
starts unverified and is sent its own verification mail (Kurvenschmiede's point).

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.user_admin
modules.summary: User administration and the account's own settings, as code (``docs/user-admin-harmonization.md`` §7 in ``Eifi1/ui-kit``).

links.heading: 7. What the kits add, what stays app-side

members.name: ACCOUNT_ERROR_DETAIL
members.signature:
ACCOUNT_ERROR_DETAIL: Mapping[AccountErrorCode, str] = {
    AccountErrorCode.LAST_ADMIN: "This would leave no active admin",
    AccountErrorCode.SELF_ACTION: "You cannot do this to your own account",
    AccountErrorCode.OTHER_COMPANIES: "This account belongs to other companies too",
    AccountErrorCode.HOUSEHOLD_HAS_MEMBERS: "The household still has other members",
    AccountErrorCode.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED: "This action needs an explicit confirmation",
    AccountErrorCode.CONFIRMATION_MISMATCH: "The typed address does not match the account",
    AccountErrorCode.PASSWORD_INCORRECT: "The current password is not correct",
}
members.doc:
The English ``detail`` of each code, for logs and API clients; the pages show the
kit's own text for the code. None of them echoes an address.

members.name: ACCOUNT_ERROR_STATUS
members.doc:
Each code's status: ``409``, see the module docstring — except ``password_incorrect``,
a ``400`` so no client reads it as an ended session.

members.name: BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS
members.doc:
How long a copy survives in the database backups and the deleted-files store after
the erasure: the shared Cloud SQL instance's 7 daily backups and 7-day point-in-time
recovery, and the uploads bucket's 7-day soft delete (§6.4, keksdose's production
figures).

members.name: CONFIRMATION_LEVELS
members.signature:
CONFIRMATION_LEVELS: Mapping[AdminAction, ConfirmationLevel] = {
    AdminAction.DEACTIVATE: ConfirmationLevel.TYPE_EMAIL,
    AdminAction.REACTIVATE: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.ROLE: ConfirmationLevel.ACKNOWLEDGE,
    AdminAction.MEMBERSHIP_REMOVE: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRE: ConfirmationLevel.ACKNOWLEDGE,
    AdminAction.PASSWORD_CHANGE_WITHDRAW: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.MAIL_VERIFICATION: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.MAIL_RESET: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.REVIEWER: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.INVITE: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.INVITE_RESEND: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.INVITE_REVOKE: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.TRANSFER: ConfirmationLevel.TYPE_EMAIL,
    AdminAction.DELETION_REQUEST: ConfirmationLevel.TYPE_EMAIL,
    AdminAction.DELETION_CANCEL: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.ERASE: ConfirmationLevel.TYPE_EMAIL,
    AdminAction.PLAN: ConfirmationLevel.ACKNOWLEDGE,
    AdminAction.GROUP_CREATE: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.GROUP_RENAME: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.GROUP_DELETE: ConfirmationLevel.ACKNOWLEDGE,
    AdminAction.MEMBERSHIP_ADD: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    AdminAction.MEMBERSHIP_ROLE: ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
}
members.doc:
The contract's level per action (§4.2). ``type_email``: deactivate, erase (the
operator's "erase now"), transfer — and the user's own deletion request, whose body
carries the typed address (§6.4). ``acknowledge``: force a password change, change a
role, change a plan (billing §6), delete a group (§11.2 decision 5: what goes with it
is what nobody can see afterwards). Everything else: ``none``. No group's action is
``type_email``: a group has no address to type.

members.name: DEFAULT_DELETION_DAYS
members.doc:
The window before the erasure (§2.1): the user's time to change their mind, the
admins' to hand shared work over (Kurvenschmiede), the guests' to export a shared
budget (keksdose).

members.name: DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE
members.doc:
One page of the list, and the most one request may ask for (keksdose): the pager makes
the size visible, the cap stops a hand-written ``?limit=100000``.

members.name: DEFAULT_ROSTER_SORT
members.doc:
No sort asked: the newest account first — on an install that is growing, the row you
came to look at is the one that just arrived (keksdose).

members.name: DETAIL_MAX_BYTES
members.doc: The most a detail weighs as JSON — ids and counts, not a payload.

members.name: DETAIL_MAX_DEPTH
members.doc:
How many objects and lists may enclose a value, ``detail`` itself included:
``{"counts": {"projects": 3}}`` encloses the 3 in two, ``{"before": {"roles":
["ADMIN"]}}`` the role in three.

members.name: DETAIL_TOKEN_MAX_LENGTH
members.doc: The longest string a detail holds: a role, a locale, an ISO timestamp (32), a kind.

members.name: EXPORT_FORMAT
members.doc: The envelope's ``format``: what a reader checks before it trusts the rest.

members.name: EXPORT_PER_USER
members.doc: Once a minute per account (§6.5): an export reads every table the user touches.

members.name: EXPORT_VERSION
members.doc:
The envelope's ``version``; it changes only when the ENVELOPE does, not when an app
adds a field to ``account`` or ``data``.

members.name: FACT_SUFFIXES
members.signature:
FACT_SUFFIXES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        "at",
        "on",
        "until",
        "date",
        "count",
        "enabled",
        "required",
        "fingerprint",
        "epoch",
        "kind",
        "type",
        # 0.5.1 (keksdose): `api_tokens_revoked`, `sessions_valid` are facts about a secret,
        # not the secret — keksdose had renamed them to `*_count` to get past the check.
        "revoked",
        "valid",
        # 0.10 (keksdose): notifications' `digest_cadence` (the kit's own DigestFields, in
        # every export by notifications §3.9) says how often the digest goes, not a digest.
        "cadence",
    }
)
members.doc:
A key's last word that says it holds a FACT about a secret — when, whether, how many,
which one — and not the secret.

members.name: LIKE_ESCAPE
members.doc:
The escape character :func:`area_like_patterns` uses. Name it in the query
(SQLAlchemy ``column.like(pattern, escape=LIKE_ESCAPE)``, SQL ``LIKE … ESCAPE '\'``):
PostgreSQL defaults to it, SQLite has no default.

members.name: LOG_RETENTION_DAYS
members.doc: How long the server logs keep a line (Cloud Logging's ``_Default`` bucket, §6.4).

members.name: MAIL_BACKEND_CONSOLE
members.doc:
The mail backend whose answers may carry a link (§4.1, §5): nothing leaves the
machine, so the admin is the only way the link reaches anyone.

members.name: MAX_NOTE_LENGTH
members.doc: An invitation's note (kastlan's ``String(255)``).

members.name: MAX_REVIEWER_ENTRIES
members.doc: Locales and areas in one reviewer grant (keksdose ``AdminReviewerRequest``).

members.name: MAX_ROLE_LENGTH
members.doc: A role value as an app writes it (``ADMIN``, ``PROPERTY_MANAGER``).

members.name: MAX_SEARCH_LENGTH
members.doc: The search box's longest query (keksdose ``Query(max_length=200)``).

members.name: NEVER_EXPORT
members.signature:
NEVER_EXPORT: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "the password hash",
    "TOTP secrets and backup-code digests",
    "every token and token hash: refresh, API, reset, verification, invitation, email change, translation review",
    "passkey credential ids and public keys (a passkey leaves as its name, created and last used)",
    "push endpoints and their keys (an endpoint is a capability URL)",
    "all E2EE material: key wraps with their Argon2 parameters and salts, recovery verifiers "
    "(at most a public-key fingerprint and the key epoch)",
    "other people's addresses and data: other team members, kastlan's invitees, others' work shared with the user "
    "(a reference at most)",
    "a company's records in kastlan: the company is their controller",
)
members.doc:
What no app's export holds, whatever it chooses for ``data`` (§6.5) — documentation;
:func:`assert_no_secrets` catches the secrets among them.

members.name: SECRET_KEY_TERMS
members.doc:
Words that make a key a secret's (§6.5 "never leaves"): the password and its hash,
TOTP secrets and backup-code digests, every token and token hash, passkey credential
ids and public keys, push endpoints and their keys, and the E2EE material — key wraps,
salts, nonces, recovery verifiers. Multi-word terms match as consecutive words.

members.name: SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS
members.signature:
SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS: tuple[re.Pattern[str], ...] = (
    re.compile(r"^\$2[abxy]?\$\d{2}\$"),  # bcrypt
    re.compile(r"^\$argon2(id|i|d)\$"),  # Argon2
    re.compile(r"^\$scrypt\$|^\$7\$"),  # scrypt
    re.compile(r"^(\$pbkdf2|pbkdf2[_:$])", re.IGNORECASE),  # PBKDF2 (passlib, Django)
    re.compile(r"^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$"),  # a JWT
    re.compile(r"^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$"),  # a SHA-256 digest: the kit's one-time-token hash
    re.compile(r"[?&](token|invite|code|key)=", re.IGNORECASE),  # a link that carries one
    # 0.5.1 (keksdose): a Web Push subscription's endpoint is a capability URL — anyone
    # holding it can push to the device — and it may sit under a harmless key.
    re.compile(
        r"^https://(fcm\.googleapis\.com|updates\.push\.services\.mozilla\.com"
        r"|[a-z0-9.-]*\.push\.apple\.com|[a-z0-9.-]*\.notify\.windows\.com)/",
        re.IGNORECASE,
    ),
)
members.doc: Shapes no export and no audit detail holds legitimately.

members.name: SECRET_WHOLE_KEYS
members.doc:
Keys that are a secret only as the WHOLE key: a push subscription's
``{"p256dh": …, "auth": …}``, and a bare ``key``.

members.name: SORT_KEYS
members.doc:
The sort keys every app's list takes (§3.1). An app adds its own columns' keys
(keksdose's ``plan``, ``privacy``) through ``parse_roster_query(sort_keys=…)``.

members.name: STATE_TOKENS
members.doc:
The ``state`` vocabulary (§3.1): keksdose's tokens (``admin``, ``reviewer``,
``verified``, ``unverified``, ``deactivated``, ``never_logged_in``) and the contract's
new ones. ``invited`` is a user row that has not completed its sign-up (kastlan's
interim invite); ``deletion_scheduled`` has ``deletion_requested_at`` set (§6.4).
keksdose's ``allowlisted`` is its own, added through ``accepted_states``.

members.name: SUMMARY_ACTIVE_ADMINS
members.doc:
The :class:`UserListResponse` ``summary`` key with the count of active admins — what
the roster's last-admin lock reads (§4.1).

members.name: AccountError
members.doc:
A coded refusal: ``status_code`` and ``code`` from :class:`AccountErrorCode`.

``AccountError(AccountErrorCode.LAST_ADMIN)`` is a 409 with the code's English detail;
pass ``detail`` to say more. ``extra`` adds JSON fields to the answer for a refusal
that names something the page shows — kastlan's per-company last-admin check answers
``AccountError(AccountErrorCode.LAST_ADMIN, extra={"companies": ["Example AG"]})`` →
``{"detail": …, "code": "last_admin", "companies": ["Example AG"]}`` (§6.4). It may
not set ``detail`` or ``code``.

A ``ValueError`` like every kit refusal, and registered in
:data:`~eifi1_server_kit.errors.CONTRACT_ERRORS`, so an app-wide ``ValueError`` → 400
handler does not swallow its status.

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(code: AccountErrorCode, detail: str | None = None, *, extra: Mapping[str, object] | None = None) -> None

members.name: AccountErrorCode
members.doc: The ``code`` of a refusal. A ``StrEnum``, so ``str(code)`` is the wire value.

members.name: ActionConfirmation
members.doc:
The confirmation a request carries (§4.2): ``acknowledged`` for the ``acknowledge``
level, ``confirm_email`` — the target's address, typed — for ``type_email``. Also the
whole body of ``POST /admin/users/{id}/password-change``.

members.name: ActiveChange
members.doc:
``POST /admin/users/{id}/active {active, confirm_email?}`` (§4.1). Deactivating
types the address; reactivating needs nothing and also clears a pending deletion.

members.name: AdminAction
members.doc:
What an ``admin_actions`` row records (§4.3). A ``StrEnum``: ``str(action)`` is the
stored value.

members.name: AdminActionRow
members.doc:
One row of ``GET /admin/actions?limit=&offset=&target=``, newest first (§4.3): the
table's columns, plus the actor and the group joined for display.

``actor_id`` is ``None`` for the erasure job; ``target_user_id`` for an invitation and
after an erasure, when ``target_email`` is scrubbed too. ``company_id`` is kastlan's.
``target_group_id`` (0.8, §11.3) is the group a ``group_*`` row is about, or a
``membership_*`` or invitation row happened in; ui-kit's log takes ``target_group`` as
the entry's ``target`` for the first and as its ``group`` for the second (§11.4). The
``group_delete`` row's ``target_group_name`` is not a field of its own: it is read
back through ``target_group``. The group is not a filter: ``?target=`` stays a
person's.

fields.name: action
fields.doc:
An :class:`AdminAction`, or the app's own action as a string (0.5.1; keksdose's
``plan`` was one until 0.6 made it :attr:`AdminAction.PLAN`):
:func:`admin_action_record` takes both, so the row does too.

members.name: AdminUserRow
members.doc:
One row of ``GET /admin/users`` (§3.2): the auth contract's ``UserResponse`` core —
with its derived ``display_name`` and ``name_incomplete`` — plus what the admin page
shows. Reads an ORM row (``from_attributes``).

``extra`` holds the app's own columns: keksdose's plan and key custody,
Kurvenschmiede's owned counts; kastlan's companies only in the PLATFORM list — a
company's list never names another company (§3.2). Attributes and counts, never
content (keksdose's roster rule).

fields.name: email
fields.doc: As stored — already normalised; not re-validated on the way out.

fields.name: last_name
fields.doc: May be ``""`` on a migrated account until the name is completed (§3.3).

fields.name: demo_expires_at
fields.doc:
When a demo account ends, ISO-8601 in UTC (landing-demo §5.3): ``created_at`` plus
the maximum age, :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.demo.demo_expires_at`. ``None`` for a real
account. The ORM row rarely has it, so the app passes it — a property on its model
read through ``from_attributes``, or ``model_copy(update=…)``.

fields.name: text_size
fields.doc:
The account's text size (text-size §6, §10.6); ``None`` = never chosen, so a device
without its own choice uses Normal. The app's column, read through
``from_attributes``; an app without the column yet answers ``None``.

fields.name: contrast
fields.doc:
The account's contrast mode (text-size §6, §10.6); ``None`` = never chosen, which
reads as ``"system"``.

fields.name: last_login_at
fields.doc:
``None``: never signed in (or not since the column shipped) — "never", not "0
days ago". kastlan's comes from its session rows, account-wide (§3.2).

fields.name: password_change_required_at
fields.doc:
An admin required a new password; the next sign-in answers
``password_change_required`` (§4.1).

fields.name: deletion_requested_at
fields.doc: The user asked to delete the account (§6.4); the account is deactivated.

fields.name: deletion_scheduled_at
fields.doc: When the erasure runs; ``None`` in ``operator`` mode, where an operator erases.

fields.name: translation_review_locales
fields.doc: The reviewer scope (``[]`` = none; an admin reviews everything without one).

fields.name: translation_review_areas
fields.doc: …limited to these areas; ``None`` = every area.

members.name: AuditDetailError
members.doc:
A ``detail`` that could carry content or a secret — a programming error in the app,
caught by its tests, never a user's (no ``status_code``).

members.name: ConfirmationLevel
members.doc: How much the admin says before an action runs (§4.2; keksdose ``Confirmation``).

methods.name: rank
methods.doc: ``0`` / ``1`` / ``2``: the order a stronger level outranks a weaker one in.

members.name: DeletionMode
members.doc: Who erases a deleted account, and when — a per-app setting (§6.4).

members.name: DeletionRequest
members.doc:
``POST /auth/me/deletion {password, confirm_email}`` (§6.4): the password, and the
account's own address typed — check it with
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.user_admin.require_confirmation` at
``confirmation_level(AdminAction.DELETION_REQUEST)``.

members.name: EmailChangeConfirm
members.doc:
``POST /auth/me/email/confirm {token}`` (§6.2): switches the address, sets
``email_verified_at``, keeps the sessions.

members.name: EmailChangeRequest
members.doc:
``POST /auth/me/email {new_email, password}`` (§6.2). The password again, because
the address is the identity. The new address is normalised (a ``+tag`` stays) and
must be free — ``email_taken`` otherwise. Nothing changes until the link mailed to
it (:data:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.EMAIL_CHANGE_TTL`) is confirmed.

members.name: ExportSecretError
members.doc:
The export holds something that looks like a secret; ``paths`` names each one
(``account.passkeys[0].public_key``).

members.name: GroupRef
members.doc:
A group a row names (§11.4): a Kurvenschmiede team, a kastlan company, a keksdose
budget. Joined by the app as :class:`PersonRef` is, from the live group — else, for
a group that no longer exists, from its ``group_delete`` row's ``target_group_name``
(decision 6); kastlan's from ``company_id``. ``name`` ``None``: nothing left to say,
and the page reads "a deleted team".

members.name: InvitationCreate
members.doc:
``POST /admin/invitations {email, role, scope?, note?, locale}`` (§5).

The address is normalised like every entry; the kit's form suggests no ``+tag`` — it
is someone else's address. ``scope`` is the app's: a Kurvenschmiede team, ``None``
for registration; kastlan's company comes from the admin's own, never from the body.
``locale`` is the invitee's language, which the mail is written in.

members.name: InvitationRow
members.doc:
One row of ``GET /admin/invitations`` (§5): ``{id, email, role, scope, note,
locale, invited_by, created_at, expires_at, status, link?}``.

``link`` appears ONCE — in the answer to the create and to a resend, while mail goes
to the console — never in the list: the token is stored hashed and cannot be shown
again. ``role`` is ``None`` for kastlan's sign-up invitations.

members.name: InvitationStatus
members.doc: Where an invitation stands (§5).

members.name: MailKind
members.doc: Which account mail an admin (re)sends (§4.1).

methods.name: action
methods.doc: The ``admin_actions`` row it is logged as.

members.name: MailRequest
members.doc:
``POST /admin/users/{id}/mail {kind}`` (§4.1). ``none`` by the contract; keksdose
raises the reset mail's level for an account a password key opens, so the
confirmation fields ride along.

members.name: MailResult
members.doc:
The answer to a mail action: ``{sent, mail_backend, link?}`` (§4.1).

``sent=false`` is a 200, not an error: the mail is best effort and the admin can do
nothing about a provider being down (keksdose). ``link`` only while mail goes to the
console — the shown-once rule of invitations — and a ``link`` with any other backend
is refused here, so a production answer can never hand an admin someone's reset
link.

members.name: PersonRef
members.doc:
Who someone is, for a row that names them: the inviter, an action's actor. Names
are formatted on the page, in the reader's order. Every field may be empty — an
erased account leaves nothing to show (§4.3).

members.name: RetentionNote
members.doc:
The numbers the deletion mail states (§6.4), as placeholders for
:meth:`~eifi1_server_kit.mail.MailText.render`.

members.name: ReviewerUpdate
members.doc:
``PUT /admin/users/{id}/reviewer {locales, areas}`` (§4.1; keksdose
``AdminReviewerRequest``): the reviewer role and its scope in one write. ``[]``
locales takes the role away; ``areas`` ``None`` or ``[]`` is every area. Check both
against the app's vocabulary with
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.translation_review.normalize_locales` and
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.translation_review.normalize_areas`.

members.name: RoleChange
members.doc:
``POST /admin/users/{id}/role {role}`` (§4.1) — ``acknowledge``. Narrow ``role``
to the app's enum in a subclass.

members.name: RolesChange
members.doc:
kastlan's ``PUT /admin/users/{id}/roles {roles}`` for the current company (§4.1):
at least one, de-duplicated in order. Removing every role is "Remove from company",
its own request.

members.name: RosterQueryError
members.doc:
A malformed user-list query: an unknown sort key, state or role, a page out of
range (→ 422).

members.name: RosterSort
members.doc: One sort key and its direction.

members.name: UserListQuery
members.doc:
A parsed ``GET /admin/users`` query — build it with :func:`parse_roster_query`.

Field names are the wire's: ``role`` and ``state`` hold the tokens asked for (OR-ed
within each, AND-ed between them), empty for "no filter".

fields.name: q
fields.doc: Trimmed; ``None`` when blank.

methods.name: search_pattern
methods.doc:
``q`` as a ``LIKE`` pattern — ``%q%``, its own ``%`` and ``_`` escaped with
:data:`~eifi1_server_kit.translation_review.LIKE_ESCAPE` — or ``None`` without a
search.

``q`` searches the first name, the last name, both orders together, and the
email (auth §10.6), case-insensitively::

    if (pattern := query.search_pattern) is not None:
        full = User.first_name + " " + User.last_name
        reverse = User.last_name + " " + User.first_name
        stmt = stmt.where(or_(*(c.ilike(pattern, escape=LIKE_ESCAPE) for c in
                                (User.email, User.first_name, User.last_name, full, reverse))))

members.name: UserListResponse
members.doc:
``GET /admin/users`` (§3.1): ``{users, total, mail_backend, summary?, levels?}``.

``total`` counts the rows matching the filter across every page — what the pager
counts against. ``summary`` (keksdose's) describes the whole install and does NOT
follow the filter; its ``active_admins`` key (:data:`SUMMARY_ACTIVE_ADMINS`) is the
count every roster needs for the last-admin lock, sent by kastlan and Kurvenschmiede
alike. ``mail_backend`` says whether the mail actions really send
(:data:`MAIL_BACKEND_CONSOLE` = they log). ``levels`` maps an action (an
:class:`AdminAction` value, or the app's own) to the :class:`ConfirmationLevel` the
server will demand (§4.2), so the page renders the right confirmation before the
first request instead of learning it from a refusal (kastlan's and Kurvenschmiede's
shape, 2026-10-07). ``UserListResponse[MyRow]`` types the rows.

members.name: admin_action_record
members.signature: admin_action_record(action: AdminAction | str, *, actor_id: int | None, target_user_id: int | None, target_email: str | None, detail: Mapping[str, object] | None = None, company_id: int | None = None, target_group_id: int | None = None, target_group_name: str | None = None, now: datetime) -> dict[str, Any]
members.doc:
The fields of one ``admin_actions`` row (§4.3), for the app's model:
``AdminActionModel(**record)``.

``{"at", "actor_id", "action", "target_user_id", "target_email", "detail"}`` — plus
``"company_id"``, ``"target_group_id"`` and ``"target_group_name"`` each only when it
is given (kastlan's company admins; Kurvenschmiede's groups), so a table without the
column takes the record as it is. No ``id``: the database assigns it.

* ``action`` — an :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.user_admin.AdminAction` or its value,
  stored as the plain string — or the app's own action (``"reseed_demo"``), kept as
  written, as :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.user_admin.AdminActionRow` reads it back
  (0.5.1). An empty or blank action is a :class:`ValueError`.
* ``actor_id`` — who acted; ``None`` for the erasure job (its ``erase`` and
  Kurvenschmiede's day-30 ``transfer``). A ``deletion_request`` names the user
  themselves (§6.4).
* ``target_user_id`` — ``None`` for an invitation to an address with no account.
  After an erasure the app nulls it and scrubs ``target_email``; the row stays.
* ``target_email`` — the address as it was at the time, normalised; kept so an
  invitation's row names its invitee.
* ``detail`` — checked by :func:`audit_detail`.
* ``target_group_id`` — the group the row is about (``group_*``) or happened in
  (``membership_*``, ``invite``, ``invite_resend``, ``invite_revoke``) (§11.3).
  kastlan passes none: its ``company_id`` already names the company, and it fills the
  read's group from that.
* ``target_group_name`` — the name a group had, on its ``group_delete`` row only, and
  with its ``target_group_id`` (decision 6); anywhere else a :class:`ValueError`. Kept
  as written: the log reads it back for a group that no longer exists.
* ``now`` — stored as given, so an app with naive UTC columns (kastlan) passes a
  naive one.

members.name: assert_no_secrets
members.doc:
Refuse an export that holds what looks like a secret: an
:class:`ExportSecretError` naming every path (:func:`secret_paths`). Run it in the
app's test over a fully populated account's export.

members.name: audit_detail
members.signature: audit_detail(detail: Mapping[str, object] | None) -> dict[str, Any]
members.doc:
``detail`` checked and made JSON-ready (see the module docstring), or an
:class:`AuditDetailError`. ``None`` is ``{}``.

members.name: confirm_email_matches
members.signature: confirm_email_matches(target_email: str, typed: str | None) -> bool
members.doc:
Is ``typed`` the target's address? Both normalised
(:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.normalise_email`: trimmed, lower-cased, a ``+tag``
kept), so case and stray spaces never fail a confirmation and nothing else passes.
Nothing typed is never a match.

members.name: confirmation_level
members.signature: confirmation_level(action: AdminAction | str, *, at_least: ConfirmationLevel | str = ConfirmationLevel.NONE) -> ConfirmationLevel
members.doc:
The confirmation ``action`` needs: the contract's level (:data:`CONFIRMATION_LEVELS`),
or ``at_least`` when that is stronger.

The contract's level is a FLOOR. An app may ask for more, never less — keksdose
raises the reset mail and the forced password change to ``type_email`` for an account
whose encryption key a password opens (``admin_user_actions_service
.required_confirmation``)::

    level = kit.confirmation_level(
        kit.AdminAction.PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRE,
        at_least=kit.ConfirmationLevel.TYPE_EMAIL if ctx.has_password_wrap else kit.ConfirmationLevel.NONE,
    )

An unknown action or level is a :class:`ValueError`.

members.name: deletion_due
members.signature: deletion_due(requested_at: datetime | None, days: int, now: datetime, *, scheduled_at: datetime | None = None) -> bool
members.doc:
Is an account whose deletion was requested at ``requested_at`` due for erasure at
``now``, ``days`` later? Due AT the boundary, as a token expires (§6.4).

``None`` — no request, or one an admin cancelled — is never due. Pass the row's
``scheduled_at`` too, and the erasure waits for BOTH: a window shortened in the
settings after the request never erases before the date the mail promised. Naive
datetimes are read as UTC.

members.name: deletion_mail_retention_note
members.signature: deletion_mail_retention_note(*, backup_days: int = BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS, log_days: int = LOG_RETENTION_DAYS) -> RetentionNote
members.doc:
What the deletion mail says may outlive the erasure (§6.4, §9.5), as
``{backup_days, log_days}`` for the mail's placeholders.

The words are the app's; the contract's English is "copies in database backups and
deleted files age out within {backup_days} days of the erasure, server logs within
{log_days}". The defaults are the shared production figures; an app on other
infrastructure passes its own::

    texts.render(link=link, date=erase_on, **kit.deletion_mail_retention_note())

members.name: deletion_schedule
members.signature: deletion_schedule(now: datetime, mode: DeletionMode | str, days: int = DEFAULT_DELETION_DAYS) -> datetime | None
members.doc:
``deletion_scheduled_at`` for a request made at ``now``: ``now + days`` in
``after_days`` mode, ``None`` in ``operator`` mode (no date is promised). The
datetime keeps ``now``'s form, naive or aware, for the app's column.

members.name: export_envelope
members.signature: export_envelope(app: str, account: Mapping[str, Any], data: Mapping[str, Any], now: datetime, *, version: int = EXPORT_VERSION) -> dict[str, Any]
members.doc:
``{"format": "eifi1-account-export", "version": 1, "app", "exported_at", "account",
"data"}`` (§6.5).

``app`` is the app's name (``keksdose``); ``exported_at`` is ``now`` as an ISO 8601
string in UTC (a naive ``now`` is read as UTC). ``account`` and ``data`` are copied
in as given — JSON-ready, which the app's encoder (FastAPI's ``jsonable_encoder``)
sees to for dates.

members.name: export_filename
members.doc:
``keksdose-account-2026-10-07.json``: the download's name, for
``Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=…``.

members.name: invitation_status
members.signature: invitation_status(*, expires_at: datetime, now: datetime, accepted_at: datetime | None = None, revoked_at: datetime | None = None) -> InvitationStatus
members.doc:
An invitation's status from its columns: accepted, then revoked, then expired (AT
``expires_at``, as :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.is_expired`), else open. Naive
datetimes are read as UTC.

members.name: looks_secret
members.doc:
Whether the leaf ``key: value`` looks like a secret: its value's shape, or its
key's name unless the value cannot carry one (a boolean, ``None``, ``""``, ``[]``).

For a list of scalars, call it per item with the list's key.

members.name: looks_secret_key
members.doc:
Whether a key's NAME says it holds a secret (see the module docstring). A key that
ends in a fact word (:data:`FACT_SUFFIXES`) does not.

members.name: looks_secret_value
members.doc:
Whether a string has a secret's SHAPE (:data:`SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS`); anything
else is ``False``.

members.name: parse_roster_query
members.signature: parse_roster_query(*, limit: int = DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE, offset: int = 0, sort: str | None = None, q: str | None = None, role: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, state: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, sort_keys: Collection[str] = SORT_KEYS, accepted_states: Collection[str] = STATE_TOKENS, roles: Collection[str] | None = None) -> UserListQuery
members.doc:
The query of ``GET /admin/users`` (§3.1), parsed and checked, or a
:class:`RosterQueryError` (422).

Take the raw query parameters as the route gets them and hand them over::

    @router.get("/admin/users")
    async def list_users(limit: int = 25, offset: int = 0, sort: str | None = None,
                         q: str | None = None,
                         role: Annotated[list[str] | None, Query()] = None,
                         state: Annotated[list[str] | None, Query()] = None):
        query = kit.parse_roster_query(limit=limit, offset=offset, sort=sort, q=q,
                                       role=role, state=state, roles=[r.value for r in Role])

* ``sort_keys`` — the keys the app sorts by: :data:`SORT_KEYS`, plus its own columns'.
* ``accepted_states`` — the app's state vocabulary: :data:`STATE_TOKENS`, narrowed to
  the states it has, or widened with its own.
* ``roles`` — the app's role values; ``None`` takes any role token unchecked.

members.name: parse_sort
members.signature: parse_sort(raw: str | None, *, keys: Collection[str] = SORT_KEYS) -> tuple[RosterSort, ...]
members.doc:
``"-last_login,name"`` → ``(RosterSort("last_login", True), RosterSort("name", False))``.

``-key`` and ``key.desc`` sort descending, ``key`` and ``key.asc`` ascending. Nothing
asked: :data:`DEFAULT_ROSTER_SORT`. An unknown key, an unknown direction, both a ``-``
and a suffix, or a key twice is a :class:`RosterQueryError` naming it — two
directions for one key have no sensible reading (keksdose ``sorting.parse_sort``).

members.name: parse_tokens
members.signature: parse_tokens(raw: str | Iterable[str] | None, accepted: Collection[str], *, what: str) -> tuple[str, ...]
members.doc:
The tokens of a filter — comma-separated or repeated — de-duplicated in the order
asked, every one in ``accepted``; an unknown one is a :class:`RosterQueryError`
naming it and what is accepted.

members.name: refuse_last_admin
members.signature: refuse_last_admin(*, target_is_admin: bool, active_admins: int, change_removes_admin: bool) -> None
members.doc:
Refuse an action that would leave no active admin: ``409 {code: "last_admin"}``
(§4.1, §6.4; Kurvenschmiede ``_refuse_if_last_admin``).

* ``target_is_admin`` — the target IS an active admin now, so it is one of
  ``active_admins``. A deactivated admin is not: switching it off again removes
  nobody.
* ``active_admins`` — the active admins in the scope the rule guards, the target
  included: the instance in keksdose and Kurvenschmiede, the company in kastlan (and
  per company, for a request that touches several).
* ``change_removes_admin`` — the action leaves the target no longer an active admin:
  deactivating, a role change away from admin, a deletion request (keksdose: "covers
  deactivation AND the self-deletion request"), kastlan's removal from a company.

kastlan's **one-person company** is always its own last admin; there the deletion
request is accepted and flags the company for the operator (§6.4), so the app does
not call this for it. Naming the companies in kastlan's answer is
``AccountError(AccountErrorCode.LAST_ADMIN, extra={"companies": [...]})``.

members.name: refuse_self
members.signature: refuse_self(actor_id: int | str, target_id: int | str) -> None
members.doc:
Refuse an admin acting on their own account: ``409 {code: "self_action"}`` (§4.1).

Call it where the contract says "never yourself": deactivating, and a role change that
takes your own admin role away. Kurvenschmiede's reason: deactivating yourself is the
last admin's lock-out one click sooner, and nobody is left on the page to undo it.
Not for the actions that are fine on yourself (resending your own mail).

members.name: require_confirmation
members.signature: require_confirmation(level: ConfirmationLevel | str, *, target_email: str | None, acknowledged: bool = False, confirm_email: str | None = None) -> None
members.doc:
Refuse a request that lacks the confirmation ``level`` asks for (§4.2; keksdose
``assert_confirmed``).

* ``none`` — passes.
* ``acknowledge`` — the request's ``acknowledged`` is true, or it carries the
  target's typed address (the stronger confirmation covers the weaker one).
* ``type_email`` — the request carries the target's address
  (:func:`confirm_email_matches`); ``acknowledged`` alone is not enough.

Nothing given: ``409 {code: "confirmation_required"}``. A typed address that is not
the target's: ``409 {code: "confirmation_mismatch"}`` — the page keeps the dialog open
and says the address is wrong, rather than asking again from scratch.

``target_email=None`` is a group (0.8, §11.8; KS 10), which has no address: ``none``
passes; ``acknowledge`` passes on ``acknowledged`` alone, since no typed address can
match, and is ``confirmation_required`` without it; ``type_email`` is a
:class:`ValueError` — a programming error, as no level table gives a group's action
``type_email``. kastlan's company plan change may pass ``None`` in place of ``""``.

members.name: secret_paths
members.doc:
Every path in ``obj`` whose leaf looks like a secret
(:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.user_admin.looks_secret`), in document order; ``[]`` when
none does.

Objects and lists are walked into, so a container named like a secret is judged by
what it holds: ``api_tokens: [{"name": …, "scopes": …}]`` passes, ``api_tokens:
[{"token_hash": …}]`` does not. ``allow`` names keys skipped wherever they occur,
with everything under them — for a field the heuristic flags wrongly.

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.settings
modules.summary: Settings on the server: one rule for every settings body, and the account's language.
modules.doc:
Settings on the server: one rule for every settings body, and the account's language.

``docs/settings-harmonization.md`` §6 in ``Eifi1/ui-kit``. Two things every app's settings
endpoints share; the endpoints themselves, their models and their columns stay in the app.

**One PATCH rule** (§6.1). Every settings write body — ``PATCH /auth/me``, kastlan's
``PATCH /company/settings``, keksdose's ``PUT /push/settings`` and ``/push/preferences`` —
follows the same five rules, whatever its verb: the rule is about the BODY, so keksdose's
push writes stay PUT and still follow it.

1. an omitted field keeps its value;
2. an explicit ``null`` clears a nullable field — back to "not set", or to the field's
   default;
3. an explicit ``null`` on a field that can't be empty is a 422, never a silent skip;
4. unknown fields are a 422 (``extra="forbid"``), so a typo is not a silent no-op;
5. the answer is the whole resource after the change, so the client replaces its copy
   instead of merging.

:func:`apply_patch` is rules 1–3 over a Pydantic model's ``model_fields_set`` — the one
place that tells "left out" from "sent as null" — and refuses a model that would break
rule 4. Rule 5 is the endpoint's ``response_model``. The three apps each had their own
reading of ``null`` before (keksdose's push preferences dropped it, its push settings
kept the old cadence, kastlan skipped it on a required field, Kurvenschmiede refused it),
which is why it is code now and not a convention.

**The account's language** (§6.2). The account holds ONE ``locale``, canonical, from the
app's offered languages: :func:`canonical_locale` replaces keksdose's
``canonical_locale``, kastlan's ``normalize_lang`` and Kurvenschmiede's ``LanguageIn``.
:func:`parse_accept_language` reads a browser's header for a mail to someone without an
account; for everyone with one, mails and pushes use the account's locale and the server
never guesses from the request. ``ProfileUpdate`` takes the app's offered languages through
its ``offered_locales`` knob, or :func:`profile_update_model` builds that class in one call.

members.name: PATCH_NULL_CODE
members.doc: The ``code`` of :class:`PatchNullError`, named after ``apply_patch``'s ``not_nullable``.

members.name: PatchNullError
members.doc:
An explicit ``null`` on a field that can't be empty (§6.1 rule 3) → ``422``.

``{"detail": "first_name cannot be null; leave it out to keep it", "code":
"not_nullable", "fields": ["first_name"]}`` through
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.errors.install_contract_error_handlers`. Every refused field is
named, in the model's order. A ``ValueError`` like every kit refusal, so an app-wide
``ValueError`` → 400 handler cannot swallow its status.

members.name: apply_patch
members.signature: apply_patch(obj: object | None, update: BaseModel, *, not_nullable: Iterable[str], defaults: Mapping[str, object] | None = None, skip: Iterable[str] = ()) -> dict[str, object]
members.doc:
Write a settings body onto ``obj`` under §6.1's rules 1–3; the fields written.

For a PATCH and a PUT body alike — the rule is about the body, not the verb::

    changes = apply_patch(user, payload, not_nullable=PROFILE_NOT_NULLABLE)

* **Only the fields the client sent** are written (``update.model_fields_set``):
  a field left out keeps its value (rule 1), even where the model's default is
  ``None``. That is the whole difference from ``model_dump()``, which cannot tell "left
  out" from "sent as null".
* **A null clears** (rule 2): it is written as ``None`` — or as ``defaults[name]``,
  for a field whose "not set" is a value (keksdose's push preferences: ``null`` resets
  a type to its default).
* **A null on a ``not_nullable`` field** is a :class:`PatchNullError` (rule 3, 422),
  raised before ANYTHING is written, so a refused body never leaves ``obj`` half
  changed. ``not_nullable`` is required on purpose: an empty one says "every field may
  be cleared" out loud, and a forgotten one would otherwise reach the database as a
  ``NOT NULL`` violation — a 500.
* **A ``skip`` field is the caller's to write**: rule 3 still checks it — a null on it
  is refused with the others, before anything is written — but it is neither written
  nor answered. That is how a field with rules of its own reaches its own code:
  notifications' ``types`` goes through
  :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.notifications.apply_switches_patch`
  (``skip=SETTINGS_SKIP``).

``obj`` is an ORM row or any object (``setattr``), or a mutable mapping (item
assignment). Values are written as validated: a nested model stays a model, so dump it
first for a JSON column. Answers ``{name: value}`` for every field written, in the
model's order — for the app's audit or its "did the locale change" check.

**``obj=None`` when every field is skipped**: a body whose fields all have their own
code (notifications' settings in an app with no push and no digest: ``types`` alone)
has nothing to write onto. Rule 3 is still checked; nothing is written, and the answer
is ``{}``::

    apply_patch(None, body, not_nullable=SETTINGS_SKIP, skip=SETTINGS_SKIP)

Programming errors, raised as :class:`TypeError` / :class:`ValueError` so a test meets
them on the first call: a model that doesn't forbid unknown fields (rule 4 — without
``extra="forbid"`` a typo would be a silent no-op), and a ``not_nullable``, ``defaults``
or ``skip`` name that is no field of the model (a typo there would switch the guard off
without a word), or one name in both ``not_nullable`` and ``defaults``, or in both
``skip`` and ``defaults`` (a skipped field is not written, so it has no default here),
or ``obj=None`` with a field that is not skipped (a :class:`TypeError` whatever the
body sent: a write onto nothing would be lost).

members.name: canonical_locale
members.signature: canonical_locale(tag: str | None, offered: Sequence[str]) -> str | None
members.doc:
The app's own spelling of ``tag`` from ``offered``, or ``None`` (§6.2).

* **Case and ``_`` normalised**: ``de_ch`` and ``DE-ch`` are ``de-CH``, ``EN`` is
  ``en``; the answer is the offered tag exactly as the app writes it, because every
  client compares the stored string to its own language code.
* **An offered tag matches exactly**; otherwise **the language's offered tag**: ``de``,
  ``de-DE`` and Kurvenschmiede's retired ``de-informal`` are all the offered ``de-CH``
  (there is one German), ``fr-CH`` is ``fr``. With two offered tags of one language,
  the first in ``offered`` wins.
* **Anything else is** ``None``: a language the app does not offer, an empty value, or
  a string that is no language tag at all. ``PATCH /auth/me`` answers it with a 422
  (``ProfileUpdate.offered_locales``); a reader of a stored value falls back to the
  app's default.

``offered`` is the app's languages in its menu's order — kastlan's ``UI_LANGUAGES``,
Kurvenschmiede's seven codes. Lifted from keksdose ``domain/server_text.py``
(``canonical_locale``), kastlan ``domain/i18n.py`` (``normalize_lang``) and
Kurvenschmiede ``domain/languages.py`` (``LanguageIn``), which each did half of this.

members.name: parse_accept_language
members.signature: parse_accept_language(header: str | None, offered: Sequence[str]) -> str | None
members.doc:
The best offered locale in an ``Accept-Language`` header, by q-value; else ``None``.

For a mail to somebody WITHOUT an account — an invitation, a reset for an unknown
address answered the same way (§6.2). Somebody with an account gets the account's
locale: the server never guesses from the request then.

Every entry is read through :func:`canonical_locale`, so ``de-DE`` finds the offered
``de-CH``. The highest ``q`` wins and, at equal ``q``, the earlier entry (kastlan
``parse_accept_language``); ``q=0`` means "not this one", and an entry with a malformed
``q`` or the wildcard ``*`` is skipped — ``None`` then lets the caller use its default.

members.name: profile_update_model
members.doc:
``ProfileUpdate`` for the app's languages, in one call (settings §7.2)::

    ProfileUpdate = profile_update_model(("de-CH", "en", "fr", "it"))

A subclass of :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.ProfileUpdate` with ``offered_locales``
set: everything it already did stays (unknown fields and nulls refused, names trimmed),
and the locale goes through :func:`canonical_locale` — ``de_ch`` is stored as ``de-CH``,
and a language the app doesn't offer is a 422. Kurvenschmiede's ``LanguageIn`` override
and kastlan's own check go.

**An app that adds fields subclasses instead** and sets the knob — mypy takes no
function's result as a base class::

    class ProfileUpdate(kit.ProfileUpdate):
        offered_locales = LANGUAGES
        reporting_currency: CurrencyCode | None = None

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.demo
modules.summary: The demo: a throwaway account that lets a visitor try the app before an invitation.
modules.doc:
The demo: a throwaway account that lets a visitor try the app before an invitation.

``docs/landing-demo-harmonization.md`` §5–§7 in ``Eifi1/ui-kit``. Layer 1, like the rest of
the kit: the settings, the gate's order, the refusals and their codes, the address and the
dates — no database, no app ``User``, no route. The demo data and its seeder, the access
mechanics (keksdose's RLS and viewer share, kastlan's company ADMIN and read-only
transaction, Kurvenschmiede's grants and sandbox), the reap's row list and the refusal at
each route stay in each app (§7.3). kastlan's demo backend settles the gate's order and
the read-only recipe; keksdose's names the settings.

* :class:`DemoSettings` — the five settings of §6.1, for the app's ``Settings`` to inherit;
  the switch is OFF by default;
* :class:`DemoGate` — ``POST /auth/demo-session``'s checks in §5.1's order, around the
  app's three callbacks (reap, count the live users, is the demo data there);
* :class:`DemoError` and :class:`DemoErrorCode` — the six refusals of §6.2, answered
  ``{detail, code}`` (and ``Retry-After``) by
  :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.errors.install_contract_error_handlers`;
* :func:`demo_write_allowed` — layer 1 of model R's read-only (§6.3); :func:`refuse_demo`
  — the never-list of §6.4;
* :func:`demo_address`, :func:`is_demo_address`, :func:`demo_password` — the throwaway
  user (§5.1); :func:`demo_expires_at`, :func:`stale_cutoff` — its one lifetime (§5.3,
  §5.7).

The per-IP window keys on :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.limiter.client_ip`, counted from the
right of ``X-Forwarded-For`` (§5.1).

:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.name_incomplete` or each demo is asked to complete it

The subdomain of the app's own domain that demo addresses live on. It has no MX record
and no routing rule, so nothing sent to it can reach anyone (§5.1).
