3. **load** the payer's row — by ``event.payer_ref`` first (the checkout's custom data,
   :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.checkout_custom_data`), else by the provider's
   subscription id. **Never by the customer id** (§15.2.11): one Paddle customer per
   e-mail address serves every app and every company a person pays for, so it would
   land one payer's event on another's row. None → :attr:`~DispatchOutcome.NO_PAYER`;
4. **the ordering guard** (§5): a snapshot older than the row's
   ``updated_from_event_at`` → :attr:`~DispatchOutcome.STALE`. A notice never moves
   the mark, so a late notice cannot hide a newer state;
5. **another subscription** that would not keep the payer in good standing →
   :attr:`~DispatchOutcome.OTHER_SUBSCRIPTION`; one that would (the payer subscribed
   again) takes the row's link;
6. **a free grant** (§12.11, :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.grant_holds`) → apply only
   the link and the dates, :attr:`~DispatchOutcome.GRANT_HOLDS`. Pass ``launch`` — the
   settings' ``billing_launch_at`` — so a beta row stored without an end stops
   holding at the launch plus 12 months (§3.2); without it such a row holds for good,
   as in 0.6.0;
7. otherwise **apply** :func:`row_changes`, with the plan from ``plan_for_price``
   (:meth:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingSettings.billing_plan_for_price`). A price
   the settings don't know is 503 ``billing_not_configured``: nothing is kept, and the
   provider's retry applies the event once the setting is there;
8. **mark processed**, except for ``NO_PAYER``.

``apply(event, row, changes)`` writes the changes — and may send the app's notice for
the kind. It raises :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.PoisonEventError` for an event it
can never apply (answered 2xx and logged); any other exception rolls the transaction
back and answers 5xx, so the provider retries (:func:`webhook_answer`).

members.name: effective_comped_until
members.signature: effective_comped_until(row: SubscriptionRow, launch: datetime | None) -> datetime | None
members.doc:
When the row's free grant ends, as the kit reads it (§3.2, §2.4): what a banner's
"free until …" and the overview show, and what :func:`grant_holds` and
:func:`in_good_standing` compare with.

* The row's ``comped_until`` where it has one: an explicit end always wins, over the
  launch too.
* A BETA row (``source`` ``beta``) without one: :func:`beta_comped_until` of
  ``launch``, the settings' ``billing_launch_at``. The apps' beta migrations and every
  registration before Marcel names the launch date write the row without that date;
  read as "no end", it would be free for good. The kit resolves it at READ time
  instead of having the app write it back, because the launch date may still move: a
  moved date then needs no data change (Kurvenschmiede's 0.32 report).
* Otherwise ``None``, no end: an operator's grant without one (``source`` ``manual``,
  the operator's own admin accounts, §12.8) — and a beta row while ``launch`` is
  ``None``, as in 0.6.0.

``launch`` is a required argument that may be ``None``:
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingSettings` switches on with the provider and
its two secrets, NOT the launch date, so a deployment with billing on may still lack
one. Pass ``settings.billing_launch_at`` as it is. Naive in, naive out, like
:func:`beta_comped_until`.

members.name: grant_holds
members.signature: grant_holds(row: SubscriptionRow, now: datetime, *, launch: datetime | None = None) -> bool
members.doc:
Is a free grant running — ``comped`` before its end, or without one?

While it is, a provider event does not overwrite the row (§12.11): an operator's grant
— or the beta's — beats the provider, and the provider's state applies from the
grant's end on (:func:`in_good_standing`). The end is
:func:`effective_comped_until`: ``comped_until``, else for a beta row the launch plus
12 months — given ``launch``, the settings' ``billing_launch_at``. Without ``launch`` a
beta row stored without an end holds without one, as in 0.6.0.

members.name: in_good_standing
members.signature: in_good_standing(row: SubscriptionRow | None, now: datetime, *, retry_grace: timedelta | None = None, launch: datetime | None = None) -> bool
members.doc:
May the payer's data change at ``now``? §3.3, with §12.7 and §12.11.

* **No row: always** (§12.7) — demo users, the demo's system account, ownerless items
  such as keksdose's preview budget. They are never gated and never counted. Every real
  payer has a row (§12.12), so ``None`` means one of these, never "forgotten".

  **This FAILS OPEN when the row is there but hidden.** With row-level security on the
  subscription table, a guest's request — keksdose's guest in the owner's budget,
  kastlan's staff of another company — reads the PAYER's row back as nothing, and a
  lapsed owner's data stays writable through every guest (keksdose's 0.32 report).
  Read the payer's row with the RLS bypass, as the webhook does (§12.20), or, where a
  row must exist — any payer, §12.12 — treat a missing one as an error rather than
  pass ``None`` here.
* ``active`` — yes; but a subscription set to cancel at its period's end is out once
  that end has passed, even before the provider's final event arrives (it may be late;
  a cancelled period cannot renew).
* ``trialing`` — the cardless trial (``source`` ``trial``) before ``trial_ends_at``, or
  while it is empty: a pure guest's row waits for their first owned item to start it
  (§12.9). A provider's own trial counts as ``active``.
* ``comped`` — before its end, or without one; after it, while the provider's paid
  period runs (``current_period_end``): a payer who subscribed during the grant —
  whose provider events left the grant in place (§12.11) — is in good standing from
  the grant's end on, as the provider says. The end is
  :func:`effective_comped_until`: ``comped_until``, else for a beta row stored without
  one the launch plus 12 months, given ``launch`` (the settings'
  ``billing_launch_at``); without ``launch`` such a row has no end, as in 0.6.0.
* ``past_due`` — yes: the provider retries, and moves it on when it gives up (Paddle to
  ``canceled`` or ``paused``).
  With ``retry_grace``, also no later than ``current_period_end`` plus the grace — a
  backstop for a provider event that never arrived.
* ``canceled``, ``expired`` — no.

Billing switched off means everyone is in good standing (§4):
:meth:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingSettings.billing_standing` asks the switch
first, and passes its ``billing_launch_at`` as ``launch``. An unknown ``status`` is a
:class:`ValueError`.

members.name: is_beta
members.signature: is_beta(invitation_created_at: datetime | None, launch: datetime) -> bool
members.doc:
Does a payer registering now count as beta (§12.10)? Yes when their invitation was
CREATED before the launch, even if it is accepted after — the last week's invitees get
12 months, not 30 days. No invitation (open registration after launch): no.

The payers who exist when billing goes on are beta by the migration (§3.2), which needs
no question.

members.name: map_paddle_event
members.doc:
A Paddle Billing notification as a :class:`NormalisedEvent`; ``None`` for an event
billing doesn't use; :class:`PoisonEventError` for a body it cannot read.

The envelope is ``{event_id, event_type, occurred_at, notification_id, data}``, and a
subscription event's ``data`` the whole subscription: ``id``, ``status``,
``customer_id``, ``items[].price.id``, ``current_billing_period.ends_at`` (``null``
once cancelled — ``canceled_at`` then), ``scheduled_change.action``, ``custom_data``.

members.name: minor_to_decimal
members.signature: minor_to_decimal(amount: int, currency: BillingCurrency | str) -> Decimal
members.doc:
``amount`` minor units of ``currency`` as an exact :class:`~decimal.Decimal`:
``minor_to_decimal(990, "CHF") == Decimal("9.90")``.

Exact by construction — the exponent of :data:`CURRENCY_EXPONENTS` shifts the integer,
no float is ever involved (§4). A ``float`` or a ``bool`` amount is a
:class:`TypeError`; a currency not in the table is a :class:`ValueError`, never a
guessed exponent.

members.name: normalize_plan
members.doc:
A plan code as stored and sent: trimmed and lowercase (§3.1, §12.16).

Codes become lowercase by a data migration, and **reads compare case-insensitively**:
keksdose's ``admin_actions`` history keeps its uppercase ``FREE`` / ``PRO``, and this
reads them as ``free`` / ``pro``. Not a code — empty, too long (32), or anything but
letters, digits, ``_`` and ``-`` after a letter — is a :class:`ValueError`, so inside a
Pydantic model it is a 422. Whether the code is one of the app's plans is the
catalogue's question (:func:`plan_catalogue`), not this one's.

members.name: paddle_environment_of
members.doc:
The environment a Paddle API key's prefix names — ``pdl_sdbx_apikey_…`` is the
sandbox, ``pdl_live_apikey_…`` live — or ``None`` for a key without one: a legacy key
(from before 2025-05-06, 50 random characters), which needs ``billing_environment``
set.

members.name: paddle_locale
members.doc:
The kit's locale → Paddle's checkout locale, as ui-kit's ``paddleLocale``:
``de-CH`` → ``de``, ``zh`` → ``zh-Hans``, ``hu`` → ``en`` (Paddle has no Hungarian),
the others as they are. Any tag is read as the kit reads it (``de-AT`` and ``de`` are
the one German, ``zh-TW`` the one Chinese); one the kit doesn't ship is English.
:class:`PaddleClient` sends it as a hosted checkout's ``locale``.

members.name: parse_webhook_event
members.signature: parse_webhook_event(provider: BillingProvider | str, raw_body: bytes, *, app: str | None = None) -> NormalisedEvent | None
members.doc:
The raw body of ``provider``'s webhook as a :class:`NormalisedEvent` — after its
signature passed — or ``None`` for an event billing doesn't use (answer 2xx). A body
that cannot be read is a :class:`PoisonEventError` (answer 2xx and log).

``app`` is the settings' ``billing_app`` (§14.3); pass it::

    event = parse_webhook_event("paddle", raw, app=settings.billing_app)

Given, it keeps this app's events only: **another app's event** (``custom_data.app``
differs) **and an untagged one are ``None``** — answered 200, never recorded or
dispatched, and logged (the untagged at WARNING; the other apps' at INFO, since on one
account they are two thirds of the traffic). An untagged event is never matched by the
provider's customer id: one person may be one Paddle customer across the apps, and the
payer references (``user:<id>``) repeat between keksdose and Kurvenschmiede. Every
checkout from 0.7 on carries the tag, which Paddle copies to the subscription and its
later events. ``None``: every event, as before 0.7.

members.name: plan_catalogue
members.doc:
The app's plans as one read-only mapping, code → plan, in ``sort`` order (§3.1).

Look a plan up with the code normalised: ``PLANS.get(normalize_plan(code))``. Refused,
as :class:`ValueError`, on the first import: no plans, two plans with one code, and
plans that name different dimensions — a ``budget`` beside a ``budgets`` would leave
one plan without a limit there.

members.name: plan_switch_preview
members.signature: plan_switch_preview(answer: ProviderSwitchPreview, plan: PlanSpec, usage: Mapping[str, int], *, interval: BillingInterval | str) -> PlanSwitchPreview
members.doc:
The route's answer (§15.2.10): the provider's ``answer`` for a switch to ``plan``
per ``interval``, with the payer's ``usage`` and the dimensions it exceeds on the new
plan (:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.dimensions_over_limit`).

members.name: plans_out
provider_subscription_runs
members.doc:
Whether a provider subscription runs for ``row`` as of ``now`` (§14.6, §15.2.10):
the one rule :func:`require_new_checkout` and :func:`require_plan_switch` refuse by,
and :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingOverview`'s ``switching`` — true, a plan
pick is a plan switch; false, a checkout. :func:`require_new_checkout` names the rule.

members.name: refuse_billing_read_only
members.doc:
Refuse a write at the app's own choke point while the payer is not in good standing:
402 ``billing_read_only``, naming ``what`` for the log (§3.3, §12.2)::

    refuse_billing_read_only(settings.billing_standing(owner_row, now), "a new budget")

The detail never names the payer's status or the payer (§12.6): a guest in a lapsed
owner's budget reads it too, and learns only that the budget is read-only for now.

members.name: require_new_checkout
members.doc:
Refuse a checkout while a provider subscription runs (§14.6): 409
``billing_already_subscribed``. A second checkout would be a second subscription,
charged twice; plan changes go through the provider's customer portal, and the page
that gets the 409 points there. Call it in ``POST /billing/checkout`` before the
transaction is created.

A subscription runs when the row has the provider's subscription id and it isn't set
to cancel at its period's end, and:

* the row's ``source`` is ``provider``: its status is ``active``, ``trialing`` or
  ``past_due``;
* any other source — a payer who bought while a grant held (§12.11): the webhook
  wrote the subscription's link, period end and cancellation but kept the grant's
  ``comped`` status and source, so the provider's period running past ``now`` is what
  says it runs.

A subscription already set to cancel at its period's end never blocks: the payer may
subscribe again, to another plan. A plan change while one runs is the plan switch
(:func:`require_plan_switch`).

members.name: require_plan_switch
members.doc:
Refuse a plan switch while no provider subscription runs (§15.2.10): 409
``billing_not_subscribed`` — the inverse of :func:`require_new_checkout`, by the same
rule, so exactly one of the two passes for any row. The page offers the checkout
instead. A subscription set to cancel at its period's end doesn't run here either: the
payer subscribes again, to the plan they want, through a checkout.

members.name: resume_after_withdrawal
members.signature: async resume_after_withdrawal(row: SubscriptionRow, client: BillingProviderClient, now: datetime | None = None) -> ResumeOutcome | None
members.doc:
Undo the cancellation a deletion request scheduled, when the account comes back
(§12.37, §14.8): an operator's reactivation that cancels a pending deletion, or a
person's own withdrawal where the app has one. The provider's
:meth:`~BillingProviderClient.remove_scheduled_cancel` — Paddle's ``PATCH
/subscriptions/{id} {"scheduled_change": null}``: the subscription stays ``active``,
and the row follows through the ``subscription.updated`` event it sends.

**Only the cancellation the deletion made:** call it only when the request's audit
detail recorded ``"cancelled"`` for this row (:func:`cancel_for_deletion`). A payer who
had cancelled in the portal before asking to leave (the request answered ``None``)
isn't subscribed again. That audit is the check, not the row's
``cancel_at_period_end``: :func:`cancel_for_deletion` doesn't set it — only Paddle's
``subscription.updated`` does, which may not have arrived yet, and never arrives with
billing switched off (the webhook answers 404) — so the row may still read "not
cancelled" while Paddle has the cancellation scheduled. Removing nothing is harmless:
the provider is asked whenever the subscription hasn't ended.

* ``None``: nothing to undo — no ``provider_subscription_id``, the subscription
  ``canceled`` or ``expired``, its period over at ``now`` (default: the current time),
  or Paddle answering that it has ended. A subscription cancelled at once (it was
  paused) or past its period can't be reinstated (Paddle: a cancelled subscription
  "can't be reinstated"); the payer subscribes again through a new checkout.
* ``"resumed"``, or ``"failed"``: it **never raises**. A failure is logged at ERROR —
  "remove the scheduled cancellation by hand" — and goes into the reactivation's audit
  detail (``provider_resume``).

members.name: row_changes
members.signature: row_changes(event: NormalisedEvent, *, grant_holds: bool = False, plan_code: str | None = None) -> dict[str, object]
members.doc:
The columns of the payer's row (§3.2) that ``event`` sets, by name — what
:func:`dispatch` hands the app's ``apply``::

    for name, value in changes.items():
        setattr(row, name, value)

* Always ``provider``, and the provider's ``provider_customer_id`` and
  ``provider_subscription_id`` where the event names them — the link the portal and a
  deletion's cancellation need (§12.23).
* A snapshot also sets ``current_period_end``, ``cancel_at_period_end`` and
  ``provider_price_id`` (the price it pays, §15.2.10) where it carries them, and
  ``updated_from_event_at`` (the ordering guard's mark) — under a grant too, so a plan
  switch under a grant still shows that it landed (the overview's ``paid``).
* Unless a grant holds, a snapshot then sets ``status``, ``source`` (``provider``) and,
  given ``plan_code``, the plan. While a grant holds those stay as the grant set them,
  and :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.in_good_standing` reads the provider's paid
  period once the grant ends (§12.11).

Datetimes are aware, in UTC: an app with naive columns (kastlan) strips the zone.
``status``, ``source`` and ``provider`` are the kit's ``StrEnum`` members
(:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.SubscriptionStatus`,
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.SubscriptionSource`,
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingProvider`), not plain strings: a ``str``
subclass, so they compare equal to their string values and a string column stores
them as those values — an app that writes ``.value`` instead sees no difference.

members.name: sold_plan
members.signature: sold_plan(catalogue: Mapping[str, PlanSpec], request: CheckoutRequest, *, sold: Collection[str] | None = None) -> PlanSpec
members.doc:
The plan a checkout asks for (§14.2), or 422 ``billing_plan_not_sold``: a plan the
catalogue doesn't have, one outside ``sold`` (keksdose's ``SOLD``: the plans on sale,
where the catalogue keeps retired ones for the rows still on them), or a currency and
interval the plan has no price for (a free plan has none). kastlan answered 503 here;
the price id missing from the settings for a combination that IS sold stays 503
``billing_not_configured`` (:meth:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingSettings.billing_price_id`).

members.name: switch_price
members.signature: switch_price(catalogue: Mapping[str, PlanSpec], row: SubscriptionRow, request: PlanSwitchRequest, settings: BillingSettings, *, sold: Collection[str] | None = None) -> str
members.doc:
The provider's price id a plan switch asks for (§15.2.10): ``request``'s plan per
its interval, in the currency the row pays (its ``provider_price_id`` as the settings
name it — a switch keeps the subscription's currency).

* 422 ``billing_plan_not_sold``: a plan the catalogue doesn't have, one outside
  ``sold`` (a payer on a plan no longer sold keeps it until switching away, but never
  switches to one), or one without a price for that currency and interval;
* 409 ``billing_plan_unchanged``: the price the row pays now;
* 503 ``billing_not_configured``: the row has no ``provider_price_id`` yet (no
  snapshot has written it: a row from before 0.12 until its next
  ``subscription.updated``) or one the settings don't name, or the settings lack the
  current price id for a combination that IS sold
  (:meth:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingSettings.billing_price_id`).

Call it after :func:`require_plan_switch`.

members.name: trial_ends_at
members.doc:
When a trial started at ``now`` ends: 30 days on (§2.7, :data:`TRIAL_LENGTH`).

Set where the payer is created (§12.12) — except for keksdose's pure guest, whose row is
created with an empty ``trial_ends_at`` and given one at their first OWNED item
(§12.9). Naive in, naive out.

members.name: verify_paddle_signature
members.signature: verify_paddle_signature(raw_body: bytes, header: str | None, secret: str, *, now: float | None = None, tolerance: float = PADDLE_SIGNATURE_TOLERANCE) -> None
members.doc:
Check a Paddle Billing webhook's ``Paddle-Signature``, or raise 400
``invalid_signature``.

The header is ``;``-separated ``key=value`` pairs: one ``ts`` (Unix seconds) and at
least one ``h1``; unknown keys are ignored, so a future scheme beside ``h1`` doesn't
break the check. The signed payload is ``ts``, a colon, and the raw body; any ``h1``
that matches passes (secret rotation). ``now`` is Unix seconds, the current time by
default; ``ts`` further than ``tolerance`` seconds from it is refused as a replay.

members.name: verify_webhook_signature
members.signature: verify_webhook_signature(provider: BillingProvider | str, raw_body: bytes, headers: Mapping[str, str], secret: str, *, now: float | None = None, tolerance: float = PADDLE_SIGNATURE_TOLERANCE) -> None
members.doc:
Check the signature of a webhook from ``provider``, reading its header from
``headers`` (§5)::

    settings.require_billing_enabled()                  # 404 billing_disabled
    raw = await request.body()
    verify_webhook_signature(
        BillingProvider.PADDLE, raw, request.headers, settings.billing_webhook_key(),
        tolerance=settings.billing_signature_tolerance,
    )

``now`` and ``tolerance`` are Paddle's (:func:`verify_paddle_signature`); pass the
settings' ``billing_signature_tolerance``, so a deployment widens it in its
environment — or call
:meth:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingSettings.verify_billing_webhook`, which does
(§14.2). An unknown provider — ``"lemonsqueezy"`` since 0.8 — is a :class:`ValueError`.

members.name: webhook_answer
members.doc:
The answer policy (§5): what the webhook route answers for what happened.

* ``None`` — an event billing doesn't use — and every :class:`DispatchOutcome`: 200.
  Paddle asks for a 200; anything else is retried. So is a
  :class:`DuplicateEventError` that reaches the route (a store that raises it at the
  commit): the event is in the table, a retry would only find it there.
* :attr:`DispatchOutcome.NO_PAYER` and a
  :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.PoisonEventError`: 200 and logged — a retry would
  bring the same bytes (keksdose's Pub/Sub rule).
* A :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingError`: its own status — 400 for a bad
  signature, 404 with billing off, 503 for a missing setting (retried) — logged, but
  for the 404.
* Anything else is transient: 500 and logged, so the provider retries (Paddle 60 times
  over 3 days).

Log the result's type and message, never the body: it carries the buyer's details.

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.jobs
modules.summary: The scheduler's calls: a route no account is behind, opened by ``X-Jobs-Token``.
modules.doc:
The scheduler's calls: a route no account is behind, opened by ``X-Jobs-Token``.

``docs/billing-harmonization.md`` §14.7 in ``Eifi1/ui-kit``: a daily job — the trial and
grant end notices, and kastlan's every daily job — is ``POST /api/v1/ops/…``, called by a
Cloud Scheduler HTTP job. No account is behind the call, so there is no session and no
role: the caller proves it is the job with **a header, never a query parameter** (Cloud
Run's request log records the URL with its query), compared **in constant time** with the
app's ``<APP>_JOBS_TOKEN`` secret. Missing, wrong, or no token set: **401**, one answer for
all three; the last is logged too, because then the operator has something to do.

kastlan (``adapters/api/ops_router.py:35``) and Kurvenschmiede
(``adapters/api/ops_router.py:39``) each wrote that dependency; this is it once (round
0.34 S5). keksdose runs its jobs in-process and has no token route.

members.name: JOBS_TOKEN_HEADER
members.doc: The header the scheduler sends the token in (Cloud Scheduler's ``--headers``).

members.name: JobsSettings
members.doc:
The token setting, for the app's settings to INHERIT, so each reads its own
variable (``KASTLAN_JOBS_TOKEN``, ``KURVENSCHMIEDE_JOBS_TOKEN``)::

    class Settings(BaseSettings, DemoSettings, BillingSettings, JobsSettings):
        model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="KASTLAN_")

fields.name: jobs_token
fields.doc:
The scheduler's token: Secret Manager in production, never a deploy literal. Unset —
or blank, as an ``.env`` template leaves it — every token route answers 401.

members.name: JobsTokenError
members.doc:
The call isn't the scheduler's (→ 401): ``X-Jobs-Token`` missing or wrong, or no
token set. One answer for the three, as kastlan's ``AuthError`` and Kurvenschmiede's
``HTTPException`` gave it; answered through
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.errors.install_contract_error_handlers`.

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(detail: str = f'A valid {JOBS_TOKEN_HEADER} is required') -> None

members.name: check_jobs_token
members.signature: check_jobs_token(presented: str | None, expected: SecretStr | str | None) -> None
members.doc:
Refuse unless ``presented`` — the request's ``X-Jobs-Token`` — is the app's token:
:class:`JobsTokenError` (401) for a missing or wrong one, and for no token set (logged
at WARNING: the operator's to fix). ``expected`` is the setting as the app holds it,
a ``SecretStr`` (kastlan) or text (Kurvenschmiede's ``str = ""``); blank is unset.

:func:`hmac.compare_digest` on BYTES: two ``str`` with a non-ASCII character raise
``TypeError`` there, which an unauthenticated caller could turn into a 500 at will.

members.name: require_jobs_token
members.signature: require_jobs_token(token: Callable[[], SecretStr | str | None]) -> Callable[[Request], None]
members.doc:
The FastAPI dependency for a token route, reading the app's token through ``token``
at every call — so a test that sets the setting is heard::

    @router.post(
        "/ops/jobs/{name}",
        dependencies=[Depends(require_jobs_token(lambda: settings.jobs_token))],
    )

It reads ``X-Jobs-Token`` from the request (Starlette's ``Request``, which FastAPI
hands a dependency; the kit doesn't import FastAPI) and calls
:func:`check_jobs_token`. So the header is not a parameter in the app's OpenAPI
schema — nobody but the scheduler calls these routes.

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.mail
modules.summary: Outbound account mail: the words per language, one layout, two transports.
modules.doc: Outbound account mail: the words per language, one layout, two transports. ``docs/auth-harmonization.md`` §8 in ``Eifi1/ui-kit``. Lifted from keksdose ``backend/keksdose/infrastructure/email.py`` and ``domain/server_text.py`` and from Kurvenschmiede ``infrastructure/email.py`` (``MailText``), which agree on everything here; kastlan built its own on the same shape. * **The words are the app's.** A mail's texts are a table per language of :class:`MailText` rows — the subject and the five parts :func:`render_message` lays out — and :func:`pick` chooses the row for the recipient's locale. Which mails exist and what they say stays in each app (§8 "App-side: the texts of the mails"). * **One layout, escaped at the boundary** (:func:`render_message`): a greeting is built from a person's name, and a name is free text, so an account called ``Reset here`` must not put that anchor into the app's own mail. * **A whole HTML document**, with the language and a title: Outlook junked a fully authenticated Kurvenschmiede reset mail (SCL 5 — a new domain on shared sending IPs), and a bare fragment with no ```` and no ```` is one more mark against a mail. :func:`render_mail` picks the row AND its language in one call. * **A ``Reply-To``** (:class:`ResendClient`'s ``reply_to``): the mails come from a ``noreply@`` address, and a reply must reach a person. Each app's ``*_EMAIL_REPLY_TO`` setting defaults to ``support@<its domain>`` (:func:`support_address`), which Cloudflare Email Routing forwards on all three domains. * **Two transports behind one protocol** (:class:`Mailer`): :class:`ResendClient` for production — the ``mail`` extra (``eifi1-server-kit[mail]``, httpx) — and :class:`ConsoleMailer` for a fresh checkout, which logs the message, link and all. **Sending never raises**: a sign-up must not fail because a provider is down, and every link can be asked for again. ``send`` answers whether the mail went; the caller decides who is told. * **A word for every mail** — the ``kind`` it is sent and logged under, which an operator greps three apps' logs for: a mail with a one-time link by its token's :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.OneTimeTokenKind`, billing's notices by :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingNoticeKind`, and the account notices with no token by :class:`AccountNoticeKind`. * **A notification mail** (``docs/notifications-harmonization.md`` §3.6) is sent under its notification type's id and carries RFC 8058's one-click unsubscribe: :func:`list_unsubscribe_headers` on :attr:`MailMessage.headers`, and a footer line linking the app's unsubscribe page (:class:`MailUnsubscribe`, which :func:`render_mail` lays out and turns into the headers). Account mail and billing's notices carry none: the recipient asked for them, and has no switch to turn them off. One a job sends is owed until it went (§9.4): it carries :attr:`MailMessage.idempotency_key` from :meth:`~eifi1_server_kit.notifications.MailMarker.idempotency_key`, so two runs on one day send it once.

links.heading: 8. What the kits add, what stays app-side

members.name: FALLBACK_LOCALES
members.doc:
Where :func:`pick` goes when the recipient's language has no row: the UI's German —
the apps' home language and the kit's fallback (i18n H7) — then English.

members.name: RESEND_ENDPOINT
members.doc: Resend's send endpoint (keksdose, Kurvenschmiede, kastlan).

members.name: SUPPORT_LOCAL_PART
members.doc: The local part :func:`support_address` puts on the sender's domain.

members.name: TIMEOUT_SECONDS
members.doc: Per attempt (keksdose ``TIMEOUT_SECONDS``).

members.name: AccountNoticeKind
members.doc:
The account mails that carry no one-time token, as the ``kind`` they are sent and
logged under (KS S5): each TELLS an address something rather than asking it to prove
anything, so :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.OneTimeTokenKind` has no word for them.
Not ``MailKind``, which is :mod:`~eifi1_server_kit.user_admin`'s word for the mail an
admin sends again. None has a switch or an unsubscribe link: they are about the
account itself.

The user-admin contract requires the first two of every app with an email change and
an account deletion; the third is Kurvenschmiede's, for its admin transfer of work
(notifications §9.3)::

    await mailer.send(user.email, message, kind=AccountNoticeKind.ACCOUNT_DELETION)

members.name: ConsoleMailer
members.doc:
The development transport: log the mail, link included, instead of sending it.

A fresh checkout needs no credentials — you verify an account by reading the backend
log (keksdose's default). kastlan logs at ``WARNING`` so the line shows under its
default level; pass ``level``. Never in production: the link in the log is a
credential.

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(*, level: int = logging.INFO, log: logging.Logger = logger) -> None

methods.name: send
methods.signature: async send(to: str, message: MailMessage, *, kind: str = 'other') -> bool

members.name: MailMessage
members.doc:
One mail, ready to send: ``html`` may be ``None`` for a plain-text mail (kastlan).

``headers`` are extra mail headers — a notification mail's
:func:`list_unsubscribe_headers` — which :class:`ResendClient` sends as Resend's
``headers`` object and an SMTP transport sets on its message. A :class:`ValueError` for
a name that is no header name, or a line break in a value.

``idempotency_key`` is the send's own ``Idempotency-Key`` — a request header to the
provider, not a mail header — for a mail a job may send again (notifications §9.4,
:meth:`~eifi1_server_kit.notifications.MailMarker.idempotency_key`)::

    message = replace(message, idempotency_key=marker.idempotency_key(today))

:class:`ResendClient` sends it on both tries; ``None`` (account mail) is a random key
per send. :class:`ConsoleMailer` ignores it. A :class:`ValueError` unless it is 1–256
characters of printable ASCII with no space: Resend refuses a longer one, and it is
one header line.

members.name: MailText
members.doc:
One mail's words in one language (Kurvenschmiede ``MailText``).

Keep a table per mail — ``{"de-CH": MailText(…), "en": MailText(…), …}`` — and render
the recipient's row with :func:`render_mail`, which picks it and knows its language;
or choose it with :func:`pick_entry` and call :meth:`render`. Any part may hold
``{placeholders}`` (``{name}``, ``{hours}``), filled by :meth:`render`.

methods.name: render
methods.signature: render(*, link: str, lang: str, unsubscribe: MailUnsubscribe | None = None, **values: object) -> MailMessage
methods.doc:
The mail with ``values`` filled in and the layout of :func:`render_message`;
``lang`` is the language this row is written in (its key in the table), so no
template may use a ``{lang}`` or ``{unsubscribe}`` placeholder.

``str.format`` runs on the TEMPLATE only, so braces in a person's name are text,
never a format field; the name is HTML-escaped by the layout. A literal brace in a
template is doubled (``{{``).

``unsubscribe`` makes it a notification mail: the footer line, and
:attr:`MailMessage.headers` from its ``one_click``. Its ``label`` is used as
written, never formatted.

members.name: MailUnsubscribe
members.doc:
A notification mail's way out (notifications §3.6), for :func:`render_mail`.

``label`` is the footer line, in the recipient's language: why the mail came and what
the link does ("You get this because e-mails about shared projects are on. Stop
them"). ``page`` is the app's signed-out ``/unsubscribe?token=…`` page, which offers
"Stop these e-mails" and "Stop all"; ``one_click`` the ``POST
/notifications/unsubscribe/{token}`` URL for :func:`list_unsubscribe_headers`, or
``None`` where the app's base URL isn't https (a development server): RFC 8058 takes
https only, so such a mail has the footer line and no headers. A :class:`ValueError`
for a ``page`` that isn't http(s) or a ``one_click`` that isn't https.

methods.name: headers
methods.doc: :func:`list_unsubscribe_headers` for :attr:`one_click`, or ``None``.

members.name: Mailer
members.doc: What sends a mail: :class:`ResendClient`, :class:`ConsoleMailer`, or a test's fake.

methods.name: send
methods.signature: async send(to: str, message: MailMessage, *, kind: str = 'other') -> bool
methods.doc:
Send one mail; whether it went out. Never raises.

``kind`` is what the mail is FOR — a small enum fit for a log line or a metric
label, which the recipient's address never is: a
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.OneTimeTokenKind` (``verification``,
``password_reset``, ``invitation``, ``email_change``), an
:class:`AccountNoticeKind` (``email_change_notice``, ``account_deletion``,
``work_transferred_notice``), a
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingNoticeKind`, or — for a notification mail —
its notification type's id (``share_granted``; notifications §3.6). An app whose own
``send`` takes a narrower kind widens it to its registry's ids.

members.name: ResendClient
members.doc:
One POST to Resend's HTTP API per mail (keksdose, Kurvenschmiede ``send_email``).

``api_key`` and ``from_address`` are injected — the app's settings, never read here;
``from_address`` must be on a domain verified with Resend. ``reply_to`` is where a
reply goes — the app's ``*_EMAIL_REPLY_TO`` setting, by default
``support_address(from_address)``; ``None`` or empty sends none. ``client`` is an
``httpx.AsyncClient`` the app owns and closes (tests pass one with a
``MockTransport``); without it each send opens and closes its own.

**At most one retry**, and only where a second attempt can help: a transport error (no
connection, a timeout) or an answer of ``429`` / ``5xx``. A ``4xx`` — a bad key, an
unverified sender — fails at once. Both attempts carry the same ``Idempotency-Key``, so
a first attempt that did reach Resend before the timeout is not sent twice: the
message's :attr:`~MailMessage.idempotency_key` where it has one (a job's notification
mail, notifications §9.4), else a random ``{kind}-{uuid}``. No queue, no delivery
tracking: a handful of mails, each awaited by somebody at the app.

**Resend's idempotency** (its docs, 2026-10-14): a key is kept 24 hours; the same key
with the same body answers the first request's answer, and nothing is sent again; a
``409`` is the same key while its first request is still in progress
(``concurrent_idempotent_requests``) or with another body
(``invalid_idempotent_request``). A ``409`` is "not sent" here and not retried: the
request that holds the key has the mail, and a job's next run tries again under the
next day's key.

The log lines name the ``kind`` and Resend's answer, never the recipient.

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(*, api_key: str, from_address: str, timeout: float = TIMEOUT_SECONDS, retry_delay: float = 0.5, endpoint: str = RESEND_ENDPOINT, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None, reply_to: str | None = None) -> None

methods.name: send
methods.signature: async send(to: str, message: MailMessage, *, kind: str = 'other') -> bool
methods.doc: Send ``message`` to ``to``; whether Resend accepted it. Never raises.

members.name: list_unsubscribe_headers
members.doc:
RFC 8058's two headers for a notification mail (notifications §3.6)::

    List-Unsubscribe: <https://app.example/api/v1/notifications/unsubscribe/v1.…>
    List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click

``url`` is the app's ``POST /notifications/unsubscribe/{token}``, which a mail client
calls with no cookie and no page in between. A :class:`ValueError` unless it is
``https://`` (RFC 8058 takes nothing else) in printable ASCII with no space, ``<``,
``>`` or ``,`` — anything that would end the header's ``<…>``.

members.name: pick
members.signature: pick[T](locale: str | None, texts: Mapping[str, T], *, fallback: Sequence[str] = FALLBACK_LOCALES) -> T
members.doc:
The row of ``texts`` for ``locale``, through a fallback chain (keksdose
``server_text.pick``, Kurvenschmiede ``languages.language_of``).

``texts`` may be keyed by full tags (Kurvenschmiede: ``de-CH``, ``en``, …) or by bare
languages (keksdose: ``de``, ``en``, …); case does not matter. The chain: the exact
tag, then its language (``fr-CH`` → ``fr``, and ``de`` finds a ``de-CH`` row), then
``fallback`` — ``de-CH`` → ``de`` → ``en`` — so an unknown or missing locale reads
German, as it does on every other surface. A table with none of them is a
:class:`KeyError`: a programming error a unit test that renders every row catches.
:func:`pick_entry` also answers the key it chose.

members.name: pick_entry
members.signature: pick_entry[T](locale: str | None, texts: Mapping[str, T], *, fallback: Sequence[str] = FALLBACK_LOCALES) -> tuple[str, T]
members.doc:
``(key, row)``: the row :func:`pick` chooses and the key it is under in ``texts``,
as written there — the language the mail is actually written in, which is not the
recipient's when the chain fell back. :func:`render_mail` puts it in ``<html lang>``.

members.name: render_mail
members.signature: render_mail(locale: str | None, texts: Mapping[str, MailText], *, link: str, fallback: Sequence[str] = FALLBACK_LOCALES, unsubscribe: MailUnsubscribe | None = None, **values: object) -> MailMessage
members.doc:
The recipient's mail from a table: :func:`pick_entry` for ``locale``, then
:meth:`MailText.render` with the row's own language in ``<html lang>``::

    message = render_mail(user.locale, RESET_TEXTS, link=link, name=greeting, hours=1)

A notification mail passes ``unsubscribe`` (:class:`MailUnsubscribe`, its label picked
for the same ``locale``): the footer line and the ``List-Unsubscribe`` headers::

    message = render_mail(user.locale, SHARED_TEXTS, link=link, actor=name, unsubscribe=way_out)
    await mailer.send(user.email, message, kind="share_granted")

members.name: render_message
members.signature: render_message(*, subject: str, lang: str, intro: str, body: str, cta: str, link: str, outro: str, unsubscribe: MailUnsubscribe | None = None) -> tuple[str, str]
members.doc:
``(html, text)`` for a transactional mail: greeting, one paragraph, one link, footer
(keksdose ``infrastructure/email.py:50``).

The one place a mail's layout is decided; the callers own the words. ``html`` is a
WHOLE document — ``<!doctype html><html lang="{lang}"><head><meta charset="utf-8">
<title>{subject}</title></head><body>…</body></html>`` — because a bare fragment is one
more mark against a mail with a spam filter (Kurvenschmiede's Outlook finding).
``lang`` is the language the words are in (``de-CH``, ``en``; :func:`pick_entry`'s
key), ``subject`` the mail's subject.

**Escaped here**, not by each caller: ``intro`` is built from a name, and a name may
hold markup; the subject may hold one too. The plain-text half is not markup and stays
exactly as written.

``link`` must be ``http(s)``; it is server-built from the app's base URL and a token
the server minted. Unlike keksdose it is escaped inside the ``href`` too: ``&`` in
an attribute IS ``&`` to every HTML parser, so a query string survives, and a link can
no longer close the attribute.

The plain text's link line is ``{cta}: {link}``, typeset for ``lang``: French takes a
no-break space before the colon (``Choisir : https://…``), every other language
none.

``unsubscribe`` (a notification mail, :class:`MailUnsubscribe`) adds a last line after
the footer, linking its ``page``: escaped and typeset like the action line —
``{label}: {page}`` in the text half.

members.name: support_address
members.signature: support_address(from_address: str, *, local: str = SUPPORT_LOCAL_PART) -> str
members.doc:
``support@<the sender's domain>``: the default of each app's ``*_EMAIL_REPLY_TO``
setting. ``"Kurvenschmiede <noreply@kurvenschmiede.app>"`` →
``"support@kurvenschmiede.app"``. Cloudflare Email Routing forwards ``support@`` on all
three apps' domains (2026-10-07); the mails come from ``noreply@``, which nobody
reads.

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.notifications

members.name: DEFAULT_ZONE
members.doc:
The zone for an account that has none, or one ``zoneinfo`` no longer knows (decision 6):
the zone both billing notices are already written in.

members.name: DIGEST_CADENCES
members.doc: Every :data:`DigestCadence`, the default first.

members.name: DIGEST_LATE_DAYS
members.doc:
How many days after the period's first local day a digest is still due (decision 5): a
Tuesday digest after a missed Monday is right, its content is the view as of that day.

members.name: INBOX_RETENTION
members.doc: How long an inbox row is kept (keksdose ``RETENTION_DAYS = 90``).

members.name: MAIL_EVENT_PATTERN
members.doc:
An event key: 1–64 letters, digits and ``:._-``, a letter or digit first. It fits the
marker's ``event VARCHAR(64)``.

members.name: MAIL_LATE_DAYS
members.doc:
How many days after its event's day a job's notification mail is still owed (decision
5): billing's and the digest's grace (``NOTICE_LATE_LIMIT``, ``DIGEST_LATE_DAYS``).

members.name: MAIL_MARKER_RETENTION
members.doc: How long the app keeps a marker (decision 6); the job that sends deletes older ones.

members.name: PUSH_MAX_FAILURES
members.doc:
Failures in a row after which the daily job deletes a device (keksdose
``push_max_failures``). Every success resets the count.

members.name: PUSH_PAYLOAD_LIMIT
members.doc:
The encoded payload's ceiling in bytes. Web Push carries about 4 KB once encrypted; 3 KB
of JSON leaves room for the encryption's overhead.

members.name: PUSH_TEST_TYPE
members.doc: The payload's ``data.type`` for a test push, the account's own and an admin's alike.

members.name: PUSH_TIMEOUT
members.doc: Seconds one send may take before it counts as failed (keksdose ``push_timeout_seconds``).

members.name: PUSH_TTL
members.doc:
Seconds a push service keeps a message for a device that is offline (keksdose
``push_ttl_seconds``): a day.

members.name: QUIET_HOURS_PATTERN
members.doc: A quiet-hours bound: local ``HH:MM``, 00:00–23:59 (keksdose ``schemas/push.py:106-107``).

members.name: SETTINGS_NOT_NULLABLE
members.doc:
``apply_patch``'s ``not_nullable`` for a body with :class:`DigestUpdate` (§3.2 rule 3):
``types: null`` and ``digest_cadence: null`` are a 422 ``not_nullable``. Without a
digest, ``("types",)`` — :data:`SETTINGS_SKIP`.

members.name: SETTINGS_SKIP
members.doc:
``apply_patch``'s ``skip``: ``types`` is checked for a null there and written by the app
from :func:`apply_switches_patch`.

members.name: TYPE_ID_PATTERN
members.doc:
A type id: lower case, digits and ``_``, 2–40 characters, starting with a letter — it
fits keksdose's ``notification_preferences.notification_type String(40)``.

members.name: Delivery
members.doc:
What to do for one recipient: write an inbox row, push to their devices, send the
mail. :attr:`NONE` is nothing at all.

fields.name: NONE
fields.doc: Nothing: no inbox row, no push, no mail.

members.name: DigestCadence
members.doc: How often the digest goes: on Monday, or on the 1st, in the account's zone.

members.name: DigestFields
members.doc: The digest's cadence, where the app has a digest type (§2.5).

members.name: DigestUpdate
members.doc: The cadence in the ``PATCH``; ``null`` is refused (:data:`SETTINGS_NOT_NULLABLE`).

members.name: InboxItem
members.doc: One inbox row as the bell lists it.

fields.name: notification_type
fields.doc: The type id, so the page can pick an icon.

fields.name: url
fields.doc: A path in the app, or ``None``.

members.name: InboxMarkRead
members.doc:
``POST /notifications/inbox/read``: these rows, or with ``ids`` ``null`` or left out,
the whole inbox.

members.name: InboxMarkReadResponse
members.doc: How many rows the call marked read.

members.name: InboxResponse
members.doc: A page of the inbox, newest first.

fields.name: unread_count
fields.doc: Every unread row of the account (the badge), not just this page's.

members.name: MailMarker
members.doc:
One recipient's mail for one event, sent (decision 6): the row the app writes, and
the source of the send's ``Idempotency-Key`` (§9.4)::

    marker = MailMarker(user.id, "invoices_overdue", mail_event(company.id, day))
    if not mail_due(day, today, sent=marker in markers):
        continue
    message = replace(message, idempotency_key=marker.idempotency_key(today))
    if await mailer.send(user.email, message, kind=marker.type_id):
        ...  # INSERT (user_id, type_id, event, sent_at) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; commit

A :class:`ValueError` for a ``type_id`` outside
:data:`~eifi1_server_kit.notifications.TYPE_ID_PATTERN`, an ``event`` outside
:data:`MAIL_EVENT_PATTERN`, or a string ``user_id`` with a colon, a space or nothing
in it (a number or a UUID is right).

methods.name: idempotency_key
methods.doc:
``<type>:<event>:<user_id>:<YYYY-MM-DD>`` for the try on ``day`` (decision 7)::

    MailMarker(17, "invoices_overdue", "42:2026-10-13").idempotency_key(date(2026, 10, 14))
    # "invoices_overdue:42:2026-10-13:17:2026-10-14"

Two runs on one day send one mail: Resend answers the second from the first (it
keeps a key 24 hours). The next day's try is a new key, so a count that changed in
between is no conflict at Resend. At most 181 characters, within Resend's 256. A
:class:`TypeError` for a ``datetime``.

members.name: NotificationError
members.doc:
Base class of every notifications refusal; each subclass sets ``status_code``,
``code`` and its English ``detail`` (for logs and API clients — the kit's pages show
their own words for the code). Pass ``detail`` to say more.

members.name: NotificationSettingsResponse
members.doc:
``GET /notifications/settings`` and the ``PATCH``'s answer (rule 5): every type the
account can receive, in the registry's order (:func:`resolve_switches`). Add
:class:`QuietHoursFields` and :class:`DigestFields` as the app has them.

members.name: NotificationSettingsUpdate
members.doc:
``PATCH /notifications/settings`` (§3.2), checked against the app's registry.

Set :attr:`registry` in the subclass, as ``ProfileUpdate.offered_locales`` is set
(settings §7.2); a class without it is a :class:`TypeError` on its first validation.
A type the registry doesn't know, or an ``app`` / ``email`` switch on a type that
doesn't offer it, is a validation error (422). A type the registry knows but this
account doesn't receive is :func:`apply_switches_patch`'s
:class:`~.errors.NotificationTypeError`. Unknown fields are a 422.

fields.name: types
fields.doc:
``{type id: {"app"?, "email"?} | null}``; a type left out keeps, a type's ``null``
resets both switches. ``"types": null`` is refused through ``apply_patch``.

fields.name: registry
fields.doc: The app's whole registry; the account's narrowing is :func:`apply_switches_patch`'s.

members.name: NotificationType
members.doc:
One notification type (§3.1)::

    NotificationType("support_chat", app=True, quiet=False)  # keksdose
    NotificationType("feedback_answered", app=None, email=True)  # Kurvenschmiede

A :class:`ValueError` for an id outside :data:`TYPE_ID_PATTERN`, or a type with
neither channel.

fields.name: id
fields.doc:
The id the switches, the inbox rows, the payload's ``data.type`` and the
unsubscribe token carry (``support_chat``).

fields.name: app
fields.doc: The "in the app" default (inbox and push); ``None``: the app has no such channel.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: The e-mail default; ``None``: the type sends no mail.

fields.name: quiet
fields.doc:
Quiet hours hold its push (§2.4). ``False`` for what a person sends — a share, a
support reply, an announcement — and ``True`` for what the machine sends.

members.name: NotificationTypeError
members.doc:
A ``PATCH /notifications/settings`` naming a type this account doesn't receive (§3.2
rule 4): 422 ``{"detail": …, "code": "notification_type_not_received", "types":
[...]}``. Raised by :func:`~.resource.apply_switches_patch` before anything is written;
a type no registry knows is refused earlier, by the update model.

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(type_ids: Iterable[str], detail: str | None = None) -> None

members.name: NotificationTypes
members.doc:
The app's registry: its types, in its order (§3.1)::

    TYPES = NotificationTypes(
        NotificationType("invoices_overdue", app=False, email=False),
        NotificationType("dunnings_pending", app=False),
    )

A :class:`ValueError` for an id declared twice. ``iter`` and ``len`` go over the
types in order, ``"digest" in TYPES`` asks for an id, ``TYPES["digest"]`` answers its
type (a :class:`KeyError` for an unknown one), :attr:`ids` the ids in order, and
:meth:`receivable` narrows it to what one account can receive.

methods.name: ids
methods.doc: Every id, in the registry's order.

methods.name: receivable
methods.doc:
The types one account can receive, in the same order: the account's narrowing.

kastlan's two types go to an account that is staff in any of its companies (roles
are per company); a tenant receives neither, so its ``GET`` lists none and a
``PATCH`` naming one is a 422::

    types = TYPES.receivable(lambda _type: is_staff_anywhere)

members.name: PushData
members.doc: The payload's ``data``: where a click goes, and the notification's type.

fields.name: url
fields.doc:
A path in the app (``/support``), opened by the service worker on the app's origin;
never ``//``, a backslash or a scheme.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: The type id, or :data:`PUSH_TEST_TYPE` for a test push.

members.name: PushDeviceResponse
members.doc:
One of the caller's devices in ``GET /notifications/devices``, oldest first. The
owner gets the whole endpoint, to mark "this device" (keksdose ``schemas/push.py:128-139``).

members.name: PushEndpointTakenError
members.doc:
``POST /notifications/devices`` with an endpoint another account holds (§3.5): 409.

Refused, never moved to this account: the server can't prove the caller holds the
endpoint, and moving it would let one account redirect another's notifications. The
client unsubscribes and registers a fresh endpoint (keksdose
``domain/services/push_service.py:62-153``).

members.name: PushKeyResponse
members.doc: ``GET /notifications/push-key``: the VAPID public key; ``""`` when push is off.

members.name: PushOutcome
members.doc: What one send's answer means for the device's row (§2.7).

members.name: PushPayload
members.doc:
What the service worker receives: ``{title, body, tag, data: {url, type}}``.

``tag`` is one per event: a repeat of the same event replaces the earlier notification
(``digest:2026-W42``), distinct events don't (``support:<uuid>``). Send
:meth:`encode`'s bytes.

methods.name: encode
methods.doc:
The payload as compact UTF-8 JSON of at most ``limit`` bytes.

A body that doesn't fit is cut, and ends in "…", at the longest length that fits; a
:class:`ValueError` when even an empty body doesn't — a title or a tag too long for
a push.

members.name: PushSubscriptionIn
members.doc:
``POST /notifications/devices``: the browser's ``PushSubscription.toJSON()`` and a
label to tell devices apart (keksdose ``schemas/push.py:16-22``). Registering is the
switch: an upsert by endpoint for the same account, a 409 for another's.

Its other fields (``expirationTime``) are ignored, as the browser sends them. The
endpoint is an https URL — a push service's — so no row ever points the server's
sends at a plain-http address.

fields.name: user_agent
fields.doc: ``navigator.userAgent``, for the device list.

members.name: PushSubscriptionKeys
members.doc: The two keys a payload is encrypted for (``PushSubscription.toJSON().keys``).

members.name: PushTestResponse
members.doc: ``POST /notifications/test``: how many devices took the test push.

members.name: PushUnregisterIn
members.doc:
``POST /notifications/devices/unregister {endpoint}``: the caller's own device, by
its endpoint in the body — never in a URL. Silent when there is none.

members.name: QuietHoursFields
members.doc: The quiet hours and the zone, where the app has push (§3.2, §3.4).

fields.name: quiet_hours_start
fields.doc: Local ``HH:MM``; with ``quiet_hours_end``, the window — which may cross midnight.

fields.name: timezone
fields.doc: An IANA name; ``null`` is the app's zone, ``Europe/Zurich`` (decision 6).

members.name: QuietHoursUpdate
members.doc:
The quiet hours and the zone in the ``PATCH``: ``HH:MM`` bounds, an IANA zone
``zoneinfo`` knows; ``null`` clears each.

members.name: StoredSwitches
members.doc:
What the app stores for one type: a switch the person set, or ``None`` — unset,
read as the type's default by :func:`resolve_switches`. A type with no row is
``StoredSwitches()``.

members.name: TypeSwitches
members.doc:
One type in the ``GET``: each switch as it applies, ``null`` where the type doesn't
offer the channel (Kurvenschmiede: ``{"app": null, "email": true}``).

fields.name: app
fields.doc: The "in the app" switch (inbox and push); ``None``: the app has no such channel.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: The e-mail switch; ``None``: the type sends no mail.

members.name: TypeSwitchesPatch
members.doc:
One type in the ``PATCH``: a switch left out keeps, ``null`` resets it to the type's
default. Unknown fields are a 422.

members.name: UnsubscribeClaim
members.doc:
What a valid token names: the account (as text — the app reads its own id type)
and the type whose e-mail to turn off.

members.name: UnsubscribeTokenError
members.doc:
An unsubscribe link whose token doesn't verify — tampered, cut, signed with another
secret, or of another version (§3.6): 400. A valid token always answers 200, also for
a switch already off or an account that is gone, so the answer reveals nothing.

members.name: apply_switches_patch
members.signature: apply_switches_patch(types: NotificationTypes, stored: Mapping[str, StoredSwitches], patch: Mapping[str, TypeSwitchesPatch | None] | None) -> dict[str, StoredSwitches]
members.doc:
The new stored value of each type the body names, in the registry's order (§3.2
rules 1–2): a type's ``null`` unsets both switches, a switch's ``null`` that one, a
switch left out keeps its stored value. The app writes what this answers.

``types`` is the account's registry (:meth:`~.registry.NotificationTypes.receivable`);
a type it doesn't hold is a :class:`~.errors.NotificationTypeError` (422,
``notification_type_not_received``), raised before anything is answered. ``patch`` is
the body's ``types``; ``None`` (left out) names nothing.

members.name: digest_due
members.signature: digest_due(cadence: DigestCadence, zone: tzinfo, now: datetime, *, sent: str | None, late_days: int = DIGEST_LATE_DAYS) -> str | None
members.doc:
The period key while the digest is due, else ``None`` (§3.4).

Due while ``sent`` — the key the app stored when it last sent one — is not this
period's, and the local date (``now`` in ``zone``) is no more than ``late_days`` days
into the period: Monday to Thursday for a week, the 1st to the 4th for a month. Store
the answer as the new ``sent`` in the transaction that writes the digest's inbox row,
whether or not quiet hours let the push go: a marker set on the push would write a new
row every day of the grace. An app with no inbox stores it once the mail's send
answered ``True``, so a failed send is tried again the next day of the grace (§9.2
decision 9). ``now`` is aware.

members.name: digest_period
members.doc:
The period ``day`` belongs to: its ISO week, ``2026-W42`` (on the ISO year, so
2027-01-01 is ``2026-W53``), or its month, ``2026-10``. At most 8 characters, so the
marker fits ``VARCHAR(16)``.

members.name: digest_tag
members.doc:
The digest push's ``tag``: ``digest:2026-W42``, so a late copy of the same period
replaces the earlier notification on the device, and the next period's doesn't.

members.name: in_quiet_hours
members.signature: in_quiet_hours(start: str | None, end: str | None, zone: tzinfo, now: datetime) -> bool
members.doc:
Whether ``now`` falls inside the window ``start``–``end`` in ``zone`` (§2.4).

``start`` is inside, ``end`` is not; a window with ``start`` after ``end`` crosses
midnight. **Fails open:** a half-set window, a bound that is no ``HH:MM`` or
``start == end`` answer ``False``. ``now`` is aware (a naive one is a ``ValueError``);
``zone`` is :func:`resolve_zone`'s answer. On a day the clocks change, the window is
read off the local wall clock: a window inside the skipped hour never happens that
night, and one inside the repeated hour holds both times round.

Only a ``quiet`` type's push is held, and a held push is dropped, not delayed: the
inbox row is written and e-mail goes as usual (:func:`~.delivery.plan_delivery`).

members.name: is_known_zone
members.doc:
Whether ``zoneinfo`` knows ``name`` — the update's check on ``timezone``.

``Europe/Zurich`` and ``UTC`` are; an empty name, a region alone (``Europe``), a path
(``../etc/passwd``) and ``None`` are not.

members.name: mail_due
members.signature: mail_due(event_day: date, today: date, *, sent: bool, late_days: int = MAIL_LATE_DAYS) -> bool
members.doc:
Whether a job's notification mail for an event is still owed to one recipient
(decision 5): not ``sent`` (no marker), and ``today`` is 0 to ``late_days`` days after
``event_day`` — the event's day and the 3 after it. A future ``event_day`` is not due.

Both are days in the job's own zone. A ``late_days`` below 0 is a :class:`ValueError`,
a ``datetime`` a :class:`TypeError`.

members.name: mail_event
members.doc:
An event key from the app's parts, joined with ``:``, a date as ISO (decision 6)::

    mail_event(company.id, day)  # kastlan: "42:2026-10-13"

The key names the event, never a person or what happened: ids and days, no name, no
title, no amount. A :class:`ValueError` for an empty part, or a key outside
:data:`MAIL_EVENT_PATTERN` (a space, an umlaut, over 64 characters, no part at all); a
:class:`TypeError` for a ``datetime``.

members.name: plan_delivery
members.signature: plan_delivery(notification_type: NotificationType, switches: TypeSwitches, *, active: bool, is_actor: bool, quiet_now: bool, email_verified: bool, keeps_inbox: bool, service: bool = False) -> Delivery
members.doc:
The :class:`Delivery` for one recipient (§3.3).

``switches`` is the recipient's, resolved (:func:`~.resource.resolve_switches`).
``active`` is false for a deactivated account and a demo; ``is_actor`` for the
event's own author. ``quiet_now`` is :func:`~.timing.in_quiet_hours` for the
recipient, and drops only the push, only of a ``quiet`` type. ``keeps_inbox``: the
app keeps an inbox (keksdose). ``service``: a service notice, on the app channel
whatever the switch says, never by mail.

members.name: push_outcome
members.doc:
The :class:`PushOutcome` of a push service's HTTP status; ``None`` — no answer, a
timeout, a connection error — is :attr:`PushOutcome.FAILED` (keksdose
``push_service.py:242-273``).

members.name: read_unsubscribe_token
members.signature: read_unsubscribe_token(secret: str | bytes, token: str) -> UnsubscribeClaim
members.doc:
The account and type a token names, after its MAC is checked in constant time.

Anything else is an :class:`~.errors.UnsubscribeTokenError` (400): another version, a
changed ``<data>`` or ``<mac>``, base64 padding, a token signed with another secret,
or a claim that is no ``<user id>:<type id>``.

members.name: resolve_switches
members.signature: resolve_switches(types: NotificationTypes, stored: Mapping[str, StoredSwitches]) -> dict[str, TypeSwitches]
members.doc:
The ``GET``'s ``types``: every type of ``types`` — the account's registry — in its
order, an unset switch as the type's default, ``None`` where the type doesn't offer
the channel. A stored row for a type ``types`` doesn't hold is left out.

members.name: resolve_zone
members.signature: resolve_zone(name: str | None, fallback: str = DEFAULT_ZONE) -> ZoneInfo
members.doc:
The zone quiet hours and the digest run in: ``name``, or ``fallback`` when it is
unset or no longer resolves (§3.4) — never UTC, never "no quiet hours".

``fallback`` is the app's zone and must resolve; a typo there is a
``ZoneInfoNotFoundError`` on the first call.

members.name: should_reap
members.signature: should_reap(failure_count: int, *, limit: int = PUSH_MAX_FAILURES) -> bool
members.doc:
Whether the daily job deletes a device: ``limit`` failures in a row,
:data:`PUSH_MAX_FAILURES` unless the app sets its own (keksdose's ``push_max_failures``
setting, ``reap_dead_subscriptions``). A ``limit`` below 1 is a :class:`ValueError`: it
would reap a device that never failed.

members.name: unsubscribe_key
members.doc:
The token's key: HMAC-SHA256 of ``eifi1-notifications-unsubscribe`` under the app's
signing secret (its JWT secret). 32 bytes.

members.name: unsubscribe_token
members.signature: unsubscribe_token(secret: str | bytes, user_id: int | str, type_id: str) -> str
members.doc:
The token for one account and one type: ``v1.<data>.<mac>``, URL-safe as it is.

A :class:`ValueError` for an empty or overlong user id, or a type id outside
:data:`~.registry.TYPE_ID_PATTERN`.

members.name: vapid_subject
members.doc:
The VAPID ``sub`` claim: ``mailto:`` the app's support address (§2.7), not
keksdose's ``admin@``. Pass the app's reply-to — server-kit
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.mail.support_address` by default. A new subject leaves existing
subscriptions working. A :class:`ValueError` for anything but a bare address.

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.feedback
modules.summary: The feedback contract as code (``docs/feedback-harmonization.md`` §3 in ``Eifi1/ui-kit``).
modules.doc:
The feedback contract as code (``docs/feedback-harmonization.md`` §3 in ``Eifi1/ui-kit``).

Schemas, enums, limits, the PATCH rules, rework bodies, crash filing, erasure and the
attachment URL check — every rule keksdose's backend enforces, as pure functions over
plain values, so kastlan and Kurvenschmiede import them instead of writing them a third
time. The database, the queries (RLS, ``company_id``), auth and the routes stay per app.

Layer 2 (0.9.0, ``docs/server-services-harmonization.md``): the flows written once against
ports each app implements — :class:`FeedbackService` over a :class:`FeedbackRepository`,
:func:`upload_attachment` and :func:`download_attachment` over an
:class:`AttachmentStorage`, :func:`throttle_upload` — re-exported here, without FastAPI.
The routes are ``eifi1_server_kit.feedback.router`` (the ``fastapi`` extra) and the fakes
and conformance checks ``eifi1_server_kit.feedback.testing``; neither is re-exported.

Public feedback (0.11, contract §9): the rules of :mod:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.public`
(the public body, who is told, the field lists), the reply, comment and vote shapes, the
four stores' ports and the service's public flows.

Rework as an entry (0.13, contract §10): ``FeedbackStatus.REWORK``, :data:`QUEUE_STATUSES`,
:class:`FeedbackEntryKind`, :func:`plan_rework`, :class:`FeedbackReworkCreate`,
:meth:`FeedbackService.rework`, and :func:`split_rework_blocks` for the migrations.

members.name: ACCEPTED_MEDIA_TYPES
members.doc:
Accepted media type → the extension a stored key carries (keksdose ``upload_guards.py:198``
``ATTACHMENT_EXT``). No SVG, no HTML: nothing that can carry script onto the app's origin.

members.name: ACCEPT_LIST
members.doc: The accepted types as an ``<input accept>`` / dialog list, in the contract's order.

members.name: ATTACHMENT_MARKER
members.doc:
The marker of one file line. It says ``[screenshot]`` for a PDF or a text log too: the
name is history, the format is contract (keksdose live #291).

members.name: AUTHOR_EDITABLE_FIELDS
members.doc:
The fields an author may edit while the row is in their lane (keksdose
``feedback_service.py:88``). Status, outcome and resolved_at record what the team decided.
``public`` joined in 0.11 (§9.3): the author may keep their own report private.

members.name: AUTHOR_EDITABLE_STATUSES
members.doc:
The author's lane: while a row is here its author may edit title / body / category
(keksdose ``feedback_service.py:89`` ``_AUTHOR_EDITABLE_STATUSES``). READY joins it
(contract §8.2): released for implementation is not yet answered, so there is nothing
the author's edit could contradict.

members.name: AWAITING_STATUSES
members.doc:
The statuses that wait on the person triaging (kit ``FEEDBACK_AWAITING_STATUSES``): OPEN,
since READY took over "released for implementation" (contract §8.2), and the two
answered statuses handed back for a verdict.

members.name: BLOCK_RULE_RE
members.doc: Any appended block's opening rule: a rework round or a folded kastlan comment.

members.name: COMMENTS_THROTTLED_DETAIL
members.signature: COMMENTS_THROTTLED_DETAIL = "Too many comments — please try again later."
members.doc: The comment and vote windows' sentences (§9.2 decision 19), on the same 429.

members.name: COMMENT_MAX
members.doc: A comment's body, after trimming: 1–4000 characters, plain text, no files (9.8).

members.name: CONTEXT_KEYS
members.doc: The ten keys the dialog writes (kit ``feedbackContext``; keksdose ``use-feedback-dialog.tsx:105``).

members.name: DECIDED_STATUSES
members.doc:
The decided statuses (contract §9.7, B2): a status-only move into one of them tells the
author nothing, so the admin's detail nudges toward a reply with that ``status_to``
(kit ``FEEDBACK_DECIDED_STATUSES``). A reply notifies; a status alone does not.

members.name: DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_POLICY
members.doc: The policy every schema uses until an app narrows it.

members.name: DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_PREFIX
members.doc:
Where every app serves attachments (contract §3.3), the ``/api/v1`` prefix included,
because the stored URL is what a client GETs back.

members.name: ERASED_MARK
members.doc:
What replaces the erased person's own identifiers where they were written INTO the text
(a crash body's ``User: <email> (#<id>)`` line, keksdose ``_ERASED_MARK``).

members.name: FEEDBACK_ANSWERED
members.doc:
The notification type a reply fires, to the author and the earlier commenters (9.11).
A reply only (``kind = 'reply'``): a rework entry sends nothing — no
``feedback_answered``, commenters not told, no admin mail (§10.2 decision 10); the REWORK
status, or the Rework chip on an OPEN row, is the inbox's signal. An admin's reply with
status REWORK is a reply and fires it.

members.name: FEEDBACK_COMMENT
members.doc: The notification type a visible comment fires, to the same people (9.11).

members.name: FEEDBACK_CONTEXT_KEEP
members.doc:
The context keys an anonymised row KEEPS — an allow-list, never a deny-list: a
deny-list keeps every key nobody thought about, and those are the ones that name people.
Everything here describes the SOFTWARE at the moment of the report.

``environment`` stays (Marcel, 2026-10-04): which copy of the software, or an erased dev
report reads as production. ``origin`` goes although it answers the same question: on a
developer's machine it is a LAN address or an ``sslip.io`` name with an IP in it.
``url`` goes (its query can carry what the person typed; ``route`` stays), ``ua`` goes
(a device fingerprint), as do ``fingerprint`` and every ``user_*`` key.

members.name: MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES
members.doc: Per-file ceiling (contract §3.5; keksdose ``upload_guards.py:197`` ``ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES``).

members.name: MAX_ATTACHMENT_URLS
members.doc:
How many files one report carries besides its one screenshot (keksdose
``schemas/feedback.py:14`` ``MAX_ATTACHMENT_URLS``; the kit's dialog stops at it).

members.name: MAX_BODY_LENGTH
members.doc:
A report's text and every rework appended to it: generous, because each rework adds to
it; bounded, because it is a column somebody else's request writes (Kurvenschmiede
``schemas/feedback.py:61`` ``MAX_BODY``).

members.name: MAX_CONTEXT_SIZE
members.doc:
The cap on a sent ``context``, measured as Kurvenschmiede measures it
(``schemas/feedback.py:69`` ``MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES``, ``:144``): the length of
``json.dumps(context, ensure_ascii=False)``. The ten keys fit in a fraction of it.

members.name: MAX_SCREENSHOT_URL_LENGTH
members.doc: keksdose's ``screenshot_url`` column is ``String(500)``.

members.name: MAX_TITLE_LENGTH
members.doc: ``feedback.title`` is ``String(255)`` in every app.

members.name: MIN_NEEDLE_LENGTH
members.doc:
Needles shorter than this are skipped: a 3-character display name ("Bob") appears inside
ordinary words, and the email is the identifier that matters.

members.name: NOT_NULLABLE_FIELDS
members.doc:
The columns a row cannot be without: an explicit ``null`` for one is refused rather
than written (keksdose ``schemas/feedback.py:80`` ``_NOT_NULLABLE``). ``public`` joined
in 0.11 (§9.3: NOT NULL). ``outcome`` is not here: since 0.11 it is refused whole.

members.name: OPAQUE_KEY_PATTERN
members.doc: Any opaque key: word characters, dots and dashes, not starting with a dot.

members.name: OUTCOME_READ_ONLY
members.signature: OUTCOME_READ_ONLY = "outcome is read-only; post a reply"
members.doc: Why a PATCH naming ``outcome`` is refused (§9.7): the answer is a list of replies now.

members.name: PICKABLE_CATEGORIES
members.signature:
PICKABLE_CATEGORIES: tuple[FeedbackCategory, ...] = (
    FeedbackCategory.BUG,
    FeedbackCategory.IDEA,
    FeedbackCategory.QUESTION,
    FeedbackCategory.OTHER,
)
members.doc: What the category picker offers: everything but CRASH (kit ``FEEDBACK_PICKABLE_CATEGORIES``).

members.name: PUBLIC_COMMENT_FIELDS
members.doc:
What a comment says to anyone (9.10); ``body`` is null when hidden, but for its writer
and an admin.

members.name: PUBLIC_PAGE_SIZE
members.doc: The public list's page (9.9): 50 rows unless asked, at most 100.

members.name: PUBLIC_REPLY_FIELDS
members.doc:
What a reply or rework entry says in the public detail (9.10, §10.3): ``kind`` carried,
never ``status_from``, never ``attachment_url``.

members.name: PUBLIC_REPORT_FIELDS
members.doc:
What a report says to anyone but its author and an admin (9.10): the list item's
fields, and the detail's ``body`` (the public body) and ``replies``.

members.name: QUEUE_STATUSES
members.doc:
The loops' queue (§10.2 decision 4): released for work — READY, REWORK — and the one
being worked on. Kurvenschmiede's loop adds OPEN (decision 9), a documented difference.

members.name: REFERENCE_LENGTH
members.doc: How many characters of the fingerprint the client is shown to quote.

members.name: REMOVED_URL
members.doc: What a removed attachment URL leaves behind (9.4).

members.name: REPLY_MAX
members.doc: A reply's body, after trimming: 1–8000 characters (9.7).

members.name: REWORKABLE_STATUSES
members.doc:
Everything the team has answered — a report can be sent back for rework from these
(contract §3.4, §10.3; kit ``FEEDBACK_REWORKABLE_STATUSES``): the five answered
statuses, and REWORK itself (a second rework adds another entry, §10.2 decision 4).
READY is not among them (§8.2).

members.name: REWORK_AUTHOR_ONLY
members.signature: REWORK_AUTHOR_ONLY = "Only the author sends a report back; an admin replies"
members.doc:
Why anyone but the report's author is refused a rework entry (§10.3): an admin answers
with a reply, which offers REWORK as a status.

members.name: REWORK_BLOCK_RE
members.doc:
One block that :func:`split_rework_blocks` turns into an entry: exactly
:func:`append_rework`'s rule, matched against a whole TRIMMED line; the group is the stamp.
A line :data:`REWORK_RULE_RE` matches that this does not (``--- REWORK ANSWERED
2026-09-16 ---``, ``--- REWORK 2026-09-04 ---``, ``--- REWORK (2) ---``) is no block.

members.name: REWORK_RULE_RE
members.doc:
The rule a rework round opens with, matched against a whole TRIMMED line (kit
``REWORK_RULE``). Anchored so "I did a REWORK --- honestly" is a sentence, not a round,
and so kastlan's folded ``--- COMMENT <stamp> · <name> ---`` blocks (§7.7) never count.

members.name: REWORK_STAMP_FORMAT
members.doc:
``YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM``, UTC — ``new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 16).replace("T", " ")``
(keksdose ``feedback-page.tsx:351``).

members.name: SHA12_KEY_PATTERN
members.doc: keksdose's (and, without ``jpeg``, Kurvenschmiede's) content-addressed key.

members.name: TERMINAL_STATUSES
members.doc:
The two settled states: ``resolved_at`` is stamped on entering them, cleared on leaving,
and a crash matching a row in one of them files a NEW row (keksdose
``feedback_service.py:90`` ``_TERMINAL_STATUSES``).

members.name: THROTTLED_DETAIL
members.signature: THROTTLED_DETAIL = "Too many attachments uploaded — please try again later."
members.doc:
The upload throttle's sentence, keksdose's (``upload_guards.py:97``); its support door
raises it too, through :func:`eifi1_server_kit.feedback.throttle_upload`.

members.name: UUID32_SHA12_KEY_PATTERN
members.doc: kastlan's ``FileStoragePort`` key: ``<uuid4 hex>_<sha256[:12]>.<ext>``.

members.name: VOTES_THROTTLED_DETAIL
members.signature: VOTES_THROTTLED_DETAIL = "Too many votes — please try again later."

members.name: AnonymisedFeedback
members.doc: The columns to assign (``changes``) and the attachment URLs the row named (``urls``).

members.name: AttachmentDownload
members.doc: One file, ready to answer (§2.12): the bytes, the type they give and the headers.

fields.name: headers
fields.doc: ``Content-Disposition`` and ``X-Content-Type-Options``.

members.name: AttachmentNotFoundError
members.doc:
A key outside the app's pattern, a file the store does not have, or one this
viewer may not read (→ 404, "Attachment not found").

members.name: AttachmentStorage
members.doc:
The app's attachment store (§2.5). It mints the key, so each app keeps its own
(keksdose ``content_addressed_key``, kastlan ``<uuid32>_<sha12>``, Kurvenschmiede its
HMAC with its dedupe and its sweep). There is no purge: the kit deletes no file.

methods.name: save
methods.signature: async save(data: bytes, upload: CheckedUpload, *, uploader: FeedbackActor, filename: str | None) -> str
methods.doc: Store a checked file and answer its key, one the app's AttachmentUrlPolicy accepts.

methods.name: read
methods.signature: async read(key: str, *, viewer: FeedbackActor) -> StoredAttachment | None
methods.doc:
The file, or None: missing, or not this viewer's to read (KS).

**The files predicate** (feedback §9.10, decision 12) is not the report's: a file
is read by its uploader, the author of a report naming it, or an admin — never
"anyone who can see the report". Public feedback shows other people a report,
never its files: no key reaches them (``public_body``), and a store that serves
any signed-in user (keksdose, kastlan) stays safe only because of that.

members.name: AttachmentUrlPolicy
members.doc:
An app's attachment URL shape: ``prefix`` + a key matching ``key_pattern``.

``key_re`` is what the download route checks a key against (it is the only thing
between a caller and the store path, keksdose ``feedback_router.py:90``), ``url_re``
what a report's URLs are checked against — built from the SAME pattern, so a stored
URL can never name a key the route would refuse (the pin keksdose's
``test_feedback_service.py:368`` keeps between its two hand-kept regexes).
Matching is ASCII-only: ``\w`` never admits a non-ASCII letter.

methods.name: is_key
methods.doc: Is ``key`` one this app minted — the download route's 404 guard.

methods.name: is_own_url
methods.doc: Is ``url`` one of this app's own attachment URLs (relative, this prefix, a valid key)?

methods.name: key_of
methods.doc: The key ``url`` names, or ``None`` when it is not one of this app's URLs.

methods.name: url_for
methods.doc: The URL a stored key is served at; refuses a key outside the pattern.

methods.name: validate_url
methods.doc: ``url`` unchanged, or :class:`UnknownAttachmentUrlError` (→ 422).

methods.name: validate_urls
methods.doc:
Each URL checked, then de-duplicated in the order given.

Keys are content-addressed in two apps, so the same picture pasted twice is the
same URL twice — one chip, not two, is what the reporter meant (keksdose
``schemas/feedback.py:42-58`` ``_attachment_urls_are_ours``).

members.name: Clock
members.doc:
A service's clock: an aware UTC ``datetime`` (feedback's ``resolved_at`` and a crash's
``seen_at``, a verdict's ``reviewed_at``). Not :data:`eifi1_server_kit.limiter.Clock`,
which is a monotonic float.

members.name: CrashCategoryNotAssignableError
members.doc: CRASH was set by hand on a create or an update (keksdose ``feedback_service.py:19``).

members.name: CrashDecision
members.doc: What to do with a crash whose fingerprint the app has looked up.

members.name: CrashReportCreate
members.doc:
``POST /feedback/crash`` — a crash the client's error boundary files (keksdose
``schemas/feedback.py:152``, feedback #160), with the contract's ``origin`` (≤ 200) and
``environment`` (≤ 20), §3.6.

Every string is capped, and anything over its cap is TRUNCATED, never refused: the
sender is a page that has just crashed, and a 422 would be a crash nobody ever sees.
Unknown fields are ignored for the same reason.

fields.name: boundary
fields.doc: "app": the whole shell went down; "page": one route's subtree did.

fields.name: origin
fields.doc: WHICH copy of the app crashed — without them a dev crash reads as production.

members.name: CrashReportResponse
members.doc:
Always a 202 (keksdose ``schemas/feedback.py:223``): stored, folded or suppressed is
a flag, never an error status — the caller is a crashed page.

fields.name: reference
fields.doc: The fingerprint's first 8 characters, quotable from the fallback UI.

members.name: ErasedFeedback
members.doc: What :meth:`FeedbackService.erase_author` did (§2.15).

fields.name: reports
fields.doc: Rows anonymised.

fields.name: keys
fields.doc: Bare policy keys no other row names, sorted; the app deletes them at its commit.

fields.name: comments
fields.doc: Comments scrubbed and un-named (§9.12), hidden ones included.

fields.name: votes
fields.doc: Votes deleted.

fields.name: replies
fields.doc:
Entries un-named and scrubbed, kept: an erased admin's replies and an erased
author's rework entries (whose files join ``keys``).

members.name: FeedbackActor
members.doc:
