Who is asking (§2.2): the ``viewer`` of a read, the ``uploader`` of a file, the
``actor`` of a write.

One app dependency builds it from the app's own ``get_current_user``. ``is_admin``
says exactly what the app's ``admin_guard`` lets through. A caller without a session
(Kurvenschmiede's feedback loop) builds one for the account it files under.

fields.name: display_name
fields.doc: The context stamp's and a crash body's name.

fields.name: is_admin
fields.doc: keksdose role ADMIN; kastlan ADMIN in the acting company; Kurvenschmiede role ADMIN.

fields.name: role
fields.doc:
The app's role name, for its ``public_viewer`` predicate (§9.2 decision 7):
Kurvenschmiede lets ADMIN, MEMBER and REVIEWER in, never CUSTOMER.

members.name: FeedbackAttachmentResponse
members.doc: ``POST /feedback/attachments`` → ``{"url": "/api/v1/feedback/attachments/<key>"}``.

members.name: FeedbackCategory
members.doc:
What a report is about.

CRASH is listed first on purpose (keksdose ``models/feedback.py:13-18``): it is the
one category nobody types — the client's error boundary files it — so the admin's
category sort puts it on top, and keksdose's Postgres label sits ``BEFORE 'BUG'``
(its migration 0050) so the database orders it the same way. Never client-settable:
see :func:`eifi1_server_kit.feedback.reject_manual_crash`.

members.name: FeedbackCommentCreate
members.doc:
``POST /feedback/{id}/comments`` (§9.8): plain text, 1–:data:`COMMENT_MAX`
characters after trimming, no files.

members.name: FeedbackCommentHide
members.doc: ``PATCH /feedback/{id}/comments/{comment_id}`` (§9.8), admin only.

members.name: FeedbackCommentResponse
members.doc: One comment (§9.8, §9.10): the same shape for every viewer.

fields.name: author_name
fields.doc:
Others: the first name; the writer and an admin: the full name; ``None``: "A user"
(an erased writer, an incomplete name, or a hidden comment for others).

fields.name: staff
fields.doc: keksdose's migrated comments whose writer is an admin.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: ``None`` when hidden, but for its writer and an admin.

members.name: FeedbackCommentRow
members.doc:
One comment (§9.8): ``feedback_comments``, read-only. ``user_id`` is ``None`` once
its writer is erased; ``hidden_at`` is set while an admin hides it.

members.name: FeedbackCommentStore
members.doc: The comments (§9.8). Async; every write flushes and none commits.

methods.name: for_report
methods.doc: The report's comments, hidden ones included, oldest first (``created_at``, then id).

methods.name: counts
methods.signature: async counts(ids: Collection[int], *, include_hidden: bool) -> Mapping[int, int]
methods.doc: Each report's comment count, in SQL; a report with none may be missing.

methods.name: commenters
methods.doc:
The writers of the report's comments, each once, in the order of their first
comment; erased writers left out (for ``feedback_recipients``).

methods.name: add
methods.signature: async add(new: NewFeedbackComment, *, actor: FeedbackActor) -> CommentRowT
methods.doc: Insert and flush. Fires ``feedback_comment``, sent after the commit.

methods.name: get
methods.signature: async get(feedback_id: int, comment_id: int) -> CommentRowT | None
methods.doc: The comment, when it belongs to that report; else None.

methods.name: apply
methods.signature: async apply(comment: CommentRowT, changes: Mapping[str, Any], *, actor: FeedbackActor | None) -> CommentRowT
methods.doc:
Assign and flush: ``hidden_at`` / ``hidden_by`` (a hide), or the erasure's
``body`` / ``user_id`` (``actor=None``).

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Delete it (its writer's own) and flush.

methods.name: by_author
methods.doc: The erasure's comments: those ``user_id`` wrote, hidden ones included.

methods.name: clear_hidden_by
methods.doc: Set ``hidden_by`` NULL where it is ``user_id`` (the erasure); how many rows.

members.name: FeedbackConflictError
members.doc:
The request contradicts the report's state (→ 409): the author taking back the vote
their report is (§9.6, "Your report counts as your vote").

members.name: FeedbackCreate
members.doc:
``POST /feedback`` (keksdose ``schemas/feedback.py:25``).

The client uploads every file first, so a row never names a file that did not arrive;
both URL fields must be this app's own (:attr:`attachment_url_policy`). CRASH is
refused by :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.reject_manual_crash` in the service, not
here, so the 422 carries a sentence rather than a validation list (as keksdose does).

fields.name: body
fields.doc:
Optional (Marcel, 2026-09-27): a title alone is a complete report. Stored as "",
never NULL; whitespace-only counts as none.

fields.name: screenshot_url
fields.doc: The ONE captured screenshot (keksdose dev #578), or none.

fields.name: attachment_urls
fields.doc: Every other file, in the order added; de-duplicated, order kept.

fields.name: attachment_url_policy
fields.doc: Which URLs may be named. Narrow it in the app's subclass.

fields.name: max_context_size
fields.doc: The cap on ``context`` (``None`` = uncapped).

members.name: FeedbackEntryKind
members.doc:
What one row of ``feedback_replies`` is (§10.2 decision 7): an admin's or a loop's
``reply``, or the author's ``rework`` — "this is not done yet", its own dated entry in
the report's timeline since round 0.40, where it used to be a block appended to the
body. Stored as the lower-case value (``VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'reply'``), so a
loop's INSERT without the column writes a reply and can never write a rework.

members.name: FeedbackError
members.doc: Base class for every refusal in :mod:`eifi1_server_kit.feedback`.

members.name: FeedbackForbiddenError
members.doc:
The actor may not make this change (→ 403; keksdose ``FeedbackUpdateForbiddenError``).

Raised for: not the author and not an admin; an author changing a field outside
title / body / category; an author editing a row outside OPEN / READY / IN_PROGRESS
without it being a rework append.

members.name: FeedbackNotFoundError
members.doc:
No such report, or one this actor may not see (→ 404, "Feedback not found").

Also what a foreign row answers where the app chose ``foreign_row="not_found"``
(Kurvenschmiede): indistinguishable from a missing one (server-services §2.10).

members.name: FeedbackPublicListItem
members.doc:
One row of the public list (§9.3, §9.9): titles only, no body — a SEPARATE model,
so nothing added to :class:`FeedbackResponse` reaches the public by default.

fields.name: author_name
fields.doc: The first name, or ``None`` ("A user").

fields.name: comment_count
fields.doc: Visible comments only.

members.name: FeedbackPublicReplyResponse
members.doc:
One reply or rework entry as the public detail shows it (§9.10, §10.3): never
``status_from``, never ``attachment_url``.

fields.name: author_name
fields.doc:
Others: the first name; an admin: the full name; ``None``: the app's word for its
admin ("Admin") — a loop's reply, a migrated outcome, an erased admin — or, on a
``rework`` entry, "A user" (an erased author), never the admin word.

fields.name: status_to
fields.doc:
The status the entry moved the report to; ``None``: no status change (a migrated
rework entry too).

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: ``reply`` (an admin's or a loop's answer) or ``rework`` (the author's, §10.3).

members.name: FeedbackPublicResponse
members.doc:
The public detail (§9.3, §9.9): the public body and the replies; the comments are
fetched beside it (``GET /feedback/{id}/comments``).

fields.name: author_name
fields.doc: The first name, or ``None`` ("A user").

fields.name: comment_count
fields.doc: Visible comments only.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.public_body`: no file lines, no attachment URL.

members.name: FeedbackReplyCreate
members.doc:
``POST /feedback/{id}/replies`` (§9.7), admin only: the answer, 1–:data:`REPLY_MAX`
characters after trimming, and the status it moves the report to, if any.

members.name: FeedbackReplyResponse
members.doc: One reply or rework entry on the admin's and the author's report (§9.7, §10.3).

fields.name: author_name
fields.doc:
Others: the first name; an admin: the full name; ``None``: the app's word for its
admin ("Admin") — a loop's reply, a migrated outcome, an erased admin — or, on a
``rework`` entry, "A user" (an erased author), never the admin word.

fields.name: status_to
fields.doc:
The status the entry moved the report to; ``None``: no status change (a migrated
rework entry too).

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: ``reply`` (an admin's or a loop's answer) or ``rework`` (the author's, §10.3).

fields.name: status_from
fields.doc: The status before the move: the admin view only (``None`` elsewhere).

fields.name: attachment_url
fields.doc:
A rework entry's one file (§10.3); ``None`` for a reply. The admin's and the
author's views only — never the public detail.

members.name: FeedbackReplyRow
members.doc:
One entry of ``feedback_replies``, read-only: an answer (§9.7) or, since 0.13, the
author's rework (§10.3), told apart by ``kind``. ``author_id`` is ``None`` for a loop's
reply, a migrated outcome, an erased admin — or an erased author's rework.

members.name: FeedbackReplyStore
members.doc:
The replies and rework entries (§9.7, §10.3), one table. Async; every write flushes
and none commits.

methods.name: for_reports
methods.doc:
Each report's entries, both kinds, oldest first (``created_at``, then id); a
report with none may be missing from the answer. One query for a page.

methods.name: add
methods.signature: async add(new: NewFeedbackReply, *, actor: FeedbackActor | None) -> ReplyRowT
methods.doc:
Insert and flush, ``kind`` and ``attachment_url`` included, and ``created_at``
when given. For ``kind = 'reply'`` only, fires ``feedback_answered`` (to
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.feedback_recipients`), sent after the commit; a
``rework`` entry fires nothing (§10.2 decision 10).

methods.name: by_author
methods.doc: The erasure's entries: those ``user_id`` wrote, both kinds.

methods.name: apply
methods.signature: async apply(reply: ReplyRowT, changes: Mapping[str, Any]) -> ReplyRowT
methods.doc: Assign and flush (the erasure's ``author_id``, ``body`` and ``attachment_url``).

members.name: FeedbackRepository
members.doc:
The app's feedback rows, on the request's session (§2.4). Async; every write
flushes and never commits. Ties in a list go to the higher id.

methods.name: get
methods.signature: async get(feedback_id: int, *, viewer: FeedbackActor) -> RowT | None
methods.doc: The row, or None: missing, or hidden from this viewer (ka's RLS, KS's visible_to).

methods.name: list_mine
methods.doc: The author's rows, newest first, the higher id first on a tie.

methods.name: inbox
methods.signature: async inbox(status: FeedbackStatus | None) -> Sequence[tuple[RowT, str | None]]
methods.doc:
Every row the request may see, in list_mine's order, each with its author's
current address: an outer join, None once the author is erased.

methods.name: open_crash
methods.doc:
The newest row with this fingerprint whose status is not in TERMINAL_STATUSES,
the higher id first on a tie.

methods.name: add
methods.doc:
Insert and flush, so the id is set. The app adds its own columns (ka's company)
and checks what is its own (KS claims the named uploads as new.user_id's).

methods.name: apply
methods.signature: async apply(row: RowT, changes: Mapping[str, Any], *, actor: FeedbackActor | None) -> RowT
methods.doc:
Assign and flush. The keys are §3.1's columns; the values the kit's (enums
included: a string column stores .value). `actor` makes the change: the request's
for an update and a crash's fold, None for the erasure (2.15).

methods.name: by_author
methods.doc: The erasure's rows (2.15).

methods.name: urls_named_except
methods.doc:
Every attachment URL the rows outside row_ids name, in a column or the body
(feedback_attachment_urls), and the ``attachment_url`` of their rework entries
(0.13): the erasure's shared-key check.

members.name: FeedbackResponse
members.doc:
One report on the wire (contract §3.1; keksdose ``schemas/feedback.py:117``).

Extra response fields are allowed and ignored by the kit — subclass to add them.

fields.name: user_id
fields.doc: NULL = the author's account was erased; the client renders ``<deleted user>``.

fields.name: user_email
fields.doc: Joined for the admin list only; ``None`` on ``/my``, create and update.

fields.name: body
fields.doc:
``""`` when none. Before round 0.40 rework rounds were appended here; an unmigrated
row may still carry them.

fields.name: attachment_urls
fields.doc: ``None`` = nothing attached (and what an older server answers by omission).

fields.name: outcome
fields.doc: The team's answer; ``None`` = none written.

fields.name: resolved_at
fields.doc: Set on ENTERING DONE / WONT_DO, cleared on leaving them.

fields.name: author_name
fields.doc: The admin: the full name; the author: their own full name. ``None``: no name.

fields.name: mine
fields.doc: The viewer wrote it.

fields.name: public
fields.doc: "Visible to others"; a CRASH is never public, whatever this says.

fields.name: filed_private
fields.doc: Made public by the round-0.38 migration: its author may switch it off at any status.

fields.name: votes
fields.doc: The people who want it (the author's own vote included) and whether the viewer is one.

fields.name: comment_count
fields.doc: The comments: an admin counts the hidden ones too.

fields.name: replies
fields.doc:
The answers and rework entries (``kind``), oldest first; ``status_from`` for an
admin only.

members.name: FeedbackReworkCreate
members.doc:
``POST /feedback/{id}/rework`` (§10.3), the report's author: what is still wanted,
1–:data:`REPLY_MAX` characters after trimming, and at most one file — one of this
app's attachment URLs (:attr:`attachment_url_policy`, else 422).

fields.name: attachment_url_policy
fields.doc:
Which URL may be named. Narrow it in the app's subclass; the service checks its own
policy too.

members.name: FeedbackRow
members.doc:
A report as the kit reads it (§2.3): read-only members, so an app's mapped row
satisfies it as it is. The kit never assigns to it — every write goes through
:meth:`FeedbackRepository.apply`. ``created_at`` is read only for the order.

members.name: FeedbackService
members.doc:
The contract's flows over the app's repository (§2.4, §2.10, §2.15).

``policy`` is the app's attachment URL shape; ``foreign_row`` what a non-admin gets on
another person's row — ``"forbidden"`` lets :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.plan_update`'s
403 speak (keksdose, kastlan), ``"not_found"`` answers 404 before it (Kurvenschmiede);
``now`` stamps ``resolved_at`` and a crash's ``seen_at``.

The demo refusal and the inbox's admin check are here too, for a caller without the
router (§2.8); over HTTP the app's own guards answer first.

Public feedback (0.11, §9.14), every part optional: ``replies``, ``comments``,
``votes`` and ``people`` are the app's stores on the request's session;
``public_viewer`` is the app's predicate on the viewer (``None``: no public parts —
kastlan); ``public_search`` whether ``q`` may search the title (False where it is
sealed — Kurvenschmiede). With ``public_viewer`` set, ``comments``, ``votes`` and
``people`` are required and the repository must implement
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.PublicFeedbackRepository` (:class:`ValueError`).

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(repository: FeedbackRepository[RowT], *, policy: AttachmentUrlPolicy, foreign_row: Literal['forbidden', 'not_found'] = 'forbidden', now: Clock = utc_now, replies: FeedbackReplyStore[Any] | None = None, comments: FeedbackCommentStore[Any] | None = None, votes: FeedbackVoteStore | None = None, people: PeopleLookup | None = None, public_viewer: Callable[[FeedbackActor], bool] | None = None, public_search: bool = True) -> None

methods.name: create
methods.signature: async create(actor: FeedbackActor, payload: FeedbackCreate) -> RowT
methods.doc:
File a report (§3.3): refused for a demo, CRASH refused (422), the first status
the server's (:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.initial_status`), the identity in
``context`` the session's (:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.stamp_identity`, §2.13),
``attachment_urls`` ``None`` for none. With a vote store, the author's vote is
cast after the report (§9.6).

methods.name: report_crash
methods.signature: async report_crash(actor: FeedbackActor, payload: CrashReportCreate, *, limiter: SlidingWindowRateLimiter | None = None) -> CrashReportResponse
methods.doc:
File a crash, or fold it into the open row with its fingerprint (§3.6).

``stored: false`` for a demo, then for a spent window — charged before the lookup,
so repeats count (§2.11) — and never an error status: the caller is a page that
has just crashed.

methods.name: list_mine
methods.doc: The actor's own reports, newest first — an admin's too.

methods.name: inbox
methods.signature: async inbox(actor: FeedbackActor, status: FeedbackStatus | None = None) -> Sequence[tuple[RowT, str | None]]
methods.doc:
Every report with its author's address, for an admin and nobody else
(:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.FeedbackForbiddenError` "Insufficient role").

methods.name: update
methods.signature: async update(actor: FeedbackActor, feedback_id: int, payload: FeedbackUpdate) -> RowT
methods.doc:
A PATCH, in keksdose's order (§2.10): refused for a demo; CRASH refused before
the lookup (422); the row this actor may see, or 404; a foreign row's 404 where
the app chose it; :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.plan_update` (403 or 422), with
the row's ``filed_private``; then the one write. ``public`` is a 422 where the app
has no public parts (no ``public_viewer``).

**The legacy append** (0.13 only, §10.3): an old client's rework append is written
as an entry (one write per store, the report last; ``body`` untouched) — the
actor's ``rework`` entry when the actor is the author, else (an admin on another's
report) a reply with status REWORK — and logged ``feedback.legacy_rework_append``.
Without a reply store the body is appended as before 0.13.

methods.name: erase_author
methods.signature: async erase_author(user_id: int, identifiers: Iterable[str | None]) -> ErasedFeedback
methods.doc:
Take an erased account out of its reports, and answer the files to delete (§2.15).

Each of the author's rows is anonymised
(:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.anonymise_feedback`) and written with
``actor=None``: an erasure claims nothing and answers nobody. ``keys`` are the bare
keys of the URLs those rows named — columns and the body's rework lines — that no
other row still names, sorted. Call it inside the app's own erasure transaction,
with a repository that does not commit; the app deletes the keys at its commit
(keksdose prefixes ``feedback/`` and arms its after-commit purge, kastlan deletes
after its one commit, Kurvenschmiede ignores them).

With the public-feedback stores (§9.12): the person's **comments** are scrubbed and
un-named (kept, shown as "A user"), their **votes** deleted, their **replies** (an
admin's) and **rework entries** (an author's, §10.3) un-named and scrubbed (kept),
each rework file taken off its entry and joining ``keys``
(:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.anonymise_reply`), and ``hidden_by`` cleared
where it was them.

methods.name: sees_public
methods.doc:
Does ``actor`` see the public parts? Never a demo (decision 8) and nobody when
the app has none (no ``public_viewer``); always an admin; else the app's predicate.

methods.name: admin_view
methods.signature: async admin_view(actor: FeedbackActor, pairs: Sequence[tuple[RowT, str | None]], *, to_response: ToResponse | None = None, reply_model: type[FeedbackReplyResponse] = FeedbackReplyResponse) -> list[FeedbackResponse]
methods.doc:
A page of reports as the admin sees them (§9.3): each ``(row, address)`` through
``to_response`` (default: :class:`FeedbackResponse` with ``user_email`` the
address), then what the stores given fill — ``author_name`` (the full name),
``mine`` (with public parts), ``votes`` / ``voted``, ``comment_count`` (hidden
ones included) and ``replies`` (oldest first, with ``status_from``, as written) —
with one call per store for the page.

methods.name: author_view
methods.signature: async author_view(actor: FeedbackActor, rows: Sequence[RowT], *, to_response: ToResponse | None = None, reply_model: type[FeedbackReplyResponse] = FeedbackReplyResponse) -> list[FeedbackResponse]
methods.doc:
A page of the actor's own reports (§9.3), as :meth:`admin_view` but: no address,
visible comments only, and the replies as others see them — first names, no
``status_from``, every attachment URL removed (:func:`public_text`).

methods.name: public_item
methods.signature: async public_item[ItemT: FeedbackPublicListItem = FeedbackPublicListItem](actor: FeedbackActor, entries: Sequence[PublicListEntry[Any]], *, model: type[ItemT] = FeedbackPublicListItem) -> list[ItemT]
methods.doc:
A page of the public list (§9.3, §9.10): titles only, the author's first name,
the counts the repository's SQL gave; one call to ``people`` for the page.

methods.name: public_view
methods.signature: async public_view[DetailT: FeedbackPublicResponse = FeedbackPublicResponse](actor: FeedbackActor, row: PublicFeedbackRow, *, model: type[DetailT] = FeedbackPublicResponse) -> DetailT
methods.doc:
The public detail (§9.3, §9.10): the public body (:func:`public_body`), the
replies as others see them, the counts — visible comments only — and the first
name; one call per store.

methods.name: reply
methods.signature: async reply(actor: FeedbackActor, feedback_id: int, payload: FeedbackReplyCreate) -> RowT
methods.doc:
An admin's answer (§9.7): refused for a demo, 403 "Insufficient role" for anyone
else, 404 for a report the admin cannot see. The reply is added (the store fires
``feedback_answered``); with a ``status`` the report moves by
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.plan_reply` — the reply first, the report last.
With ``status`` REWORK it is how an admin sends any report back (§10.3): still a
reply, and it notifies. Answers the report; :meth:`admin_view` makes it the answer
with its replies.

methods.name: rework
methods.signature: async rework(actor: FeedbackActor, feedback_id: int, payload: FeedbackReworkCreate) -> RowT
methods.doc:
The author sends a report back (§10.3): refused for a demo; the file one of this
app's URLs (422); the report this actor may see, or 404 — a foreign row 404 where
the app chose it; then :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.plan_rework` (403 for
anyone but the author, an admin included, and outside the reworkable statuses).
The ``rework`` entry is added — the store fires nothing for it — then the report
moves (REWORK for an admin author, OPEN otherwise): one write per store, the
report last. Answers the report; the router answers it with its replies.

methods.name: list_public
methods.signature: async list_public(actor: FeedbackActor, *, sort: PublicSort = 'newest', status: FeedbackStatus | None = None, category: FeedbackCategory | None = None, q: str | None = None, limit: int = PUBLIC_PAGE_SIZE, offset: int = 0) -> Sequence[PublicListEntry[Any]]
methods.doc:
The public list's page (§9.9): 404 for anyone outside the predicate (a demo
included); ``q`` trimmed, a 422 where titles are not searchable
(``public_search=False``); ``limit`` 1–100, ``offset`` 0 or more (422); a CRASH
filter finds nothing. :meth:`public_item` makes the answer.

methods.name: get_public
methods.signature: async get_public(actor: FeedbackActor, feedback_id: int) -> PublicFeedbackRow
methods.doc:
The report for the public detail (§9.9), or 404: the actor outside the
predicate, a missing report, a CRASH, or one that is not public — unless the actor
is its author or an admin. :meth:`public_view` makes the answer.

methods.name: comments
methods.signature: async comments[CommentT: FeedbackCommentResponse = FeedbackCommentResponse](actor: FeedbackActor, feedback_id: int, *, model: type[CommentT] = FeedbackCommentResponse) -> list[CommentT]
methods.doc:
A report's comments, oldest first, for whoever sees it (§9.8, §9.9; else 404).
A hidden one: its writer and an admin read it (``hidden`` true); anyone else gets
no body and no name. Others' bodies pass :func:`public_text`; an admin and the
writer see the full name, others the first.

methods.name: comment
methods.signature: async comment[CommentT: FeedbackCommentResponse = FeedbackCommentResponse](actor: FeedbackActor, feedback_id: int, payload: FeedbackCommentCreate, *, limiter: SlidingWindowRateLimiter | None = None, model: type[CommentT] = FeedbackCommentResponse) -> CommentT
methods.doc:
A comment (§9.8): refused for a demo; the window charged before the work
(429); 404 unless the actor sees the report for its comments; on any status, never
on a CRASH. The store's ``add`` fires ``feedback_comment``.

methods.name: hide_comment
methods.signature: async hide_comment[CommentT: FeedbackCommentResponse = FeedbackCommentResponse](actor: FeedbackActor, feedback_id: int, comment_id: int, payload: FeedbackCommentHide, *, model: type[CommentT] = FeedbackCommentResponse) -> CommentT
methods.doc:
Hide or unhide a comment (§9.8), an admin only (403 "Insufficient role"; a demo
refused first); 404 "Comment not found". Sets or clears ``hidden_at`` /
``hidden_by``; asking for the state it is in writes nothing.

methods.name: delete_comment
methods.signature: async delete_comment(actor: FeedbackActor, feedback_id: int, comment_id: int) -> None
methods.doc:
Its writer deletes their own comment (§9.8), a hard delete; anyone else — an
admin too, who hides instead — gets 404 "Comment not found". Refused for a demo.

methods.name: vote
methods.signature: async vote(actor: FeedbackActor, feedback_id: int, *, limiter: SlidingWindowRateLimiter | None = None) -> FeedbackVoteResponse
methods.doc:
"I want this too" (§9.6): refused for a demo; the window charged first (429);
404 unless the actor sees the report; idempotent; any status; never a CRASH.

methods.name: unvote
methods.signature: async unvote(actor: FeedbackActor, feedback_id: int, *, limiter: SlidingWindowRateLimiter | None = None) -> FeedbackVoteResponse
methods.doc:
Take a vote back (§9.6), as :meth:`vote`; the author cannot — 409 "Your report
counts as your vote". None to take back is the same answer.

members.name: FeedbackStatus
members.doc:
The nine statuses every app speaks (contract §2.1, §8.2, §10.2), in the chain's order.

``OPEN`` — filed, not yet triaged: nobody works on it, agents included; ``READY`` —
released for implementation by an admin, the triage step between OPEN and IN_PROGRESS
(keksdose live #396, contract §8.2: an admin sets OPEN → READY, and an admin's own
report starts there, :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.initial_status`);
``NEEDS_LIVE_TEST`` — resolved, but only checkable on a deployed build (keksdose
feedback #196); ``POSTPONED`` — deliberately not now, neither a refusal nor a queue
(keksdose feedback #195); ``REWORK`` — "Rework requested" (round 0.40, §10.2 decision
4): sent back by its author or an admin, released for work again, so in the loops'
queue with READY and IN_PROGRESS (:data:`QUEUE_STATUSES`); its next step is
IN_PROGRESS.

An app whose status column is a database enum adds the label before it can store
READY (Postgres: ``ALTER TYPE feedbackstatus ADD VALUE 'READY' AFTER 'OPEN'``);
existing OPEN rows stay OPEN — there is no back-fill. REWORK the same way (§10.4:
``ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'REWORK' AFTER 'READY'``, committed before any write of it).

members.name: FeedbackThrottledError
members.doc:
The upload window is spent (→ 429, contract §3.5): :data:`THROTTLED_DETAIL` with a
``Retry-After`` in whole seconds, rounded up, as :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.demo.DemoError`
carries one.

methods.name: headers
methods.doc: ``{"Retry-After": …}`` — the header the answer carries.

members.name: FeedbackUpdate
members.doc:
``PATCH /feedback/{id}`` (keksdose ``schemas/feedback.py:83``).

Every field is optional because this is a PATCH: ``None`` means "not sent", never "set
it to null". Apply ``model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`` through
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.plan_update`.

fields.name: outcome
fields.doc:
Frozen since 0.11 (§9.7): kept so an app's subclass still names it, but any PATCH
that names it, ``null`` included, is a 422 :data:`OUTCOME_READ_ONLY`.

fields.name: public
fields.doc:
"Visible to others" (§9.3): an admin any time; the author while the report is open,
or at any status on a ``filed_private`` report.

members.name: FeedbackValidationError
members.doc: A value the payload may not carry, whoever sends it (→ 422).

members.name: FeedbackVoteResponse
members.doc: ``PUT`` / ``DELETE /feedback/{id}/vote`` (§9.6): the count after, and the viewer's.

members.name: FeedbackVoteStore
members.doc: The votes (§9.6): one row per person per report. Async; every write flushes.

methods.name: counts
methods.signature: async counts(ids: Collection[int], *, viewer_id: int) -> Mapping[int, tuple[int, bool]]
methods.doc: Each report's ``(votes, the viewer voted)``, in SQL; a report with none may be missing.

methods.name: put
methods.signature: async put(feedback_id: int, user_id: int) -> None
methods.doc: Add the vote; a second ``put`` is the same one row (idempotent).

methods.name: delete
methods.signature: async delete(feedback_id: int, user_id: int) -> None
methods.doc: Remove the vote; none to remove is no error.

methods.name: delete_by_author
methods.doc: The erasure: delete every vote ``user_id`` cast; how many.

members.name: NewFeedback
members.doc: A row to insert (§2.3): the kit's columns; the app adds its own (kastlan's company).

fields.name: attachment_urls
fields.doc: ``None`` for none, never ``[]``.

fields.name: public
fields.doc: "Visible to others" (§9.3): a new report is public; the service passes False for a CRASH.

members.name: NewFeedbackComment
members.doc: A comment to insert (§9.8): never ``staff``, never hidden.

members.name: NewFeedbackReply
members.doc:
An entry to insert (§9.7, §10.3): a reply, or a ``rework`` with its one file. The
store adds ``created_at`` (``server_default now()``) unless one is given — the
migration's explicit stamp — and the app its own columns (kastlan's ``company_id``,
keksdose's ``notified_at``).

members.name: PeopleLookup
members.doc: The one read of ``users`` (§9.5): the names the views show.

methods.name: names
methods.signature: async names(user_ids: Collection[int]) -> Mapping[int, tuple[str, str]]
methods.doc:
``(first_name, last_name)`` for each id found; never a demo or system account
(left out, so it is shown as "A user"). One query for a page.

members.name: PublicFeedbackRepository
members.doc: The public reads (§9.9), on the app's repository. Async; reads only.

methods.name: public_page
methods.signature: async public_page(*, viewer_id: int, sort: PublicSort, status: FeedbackStatus | None, category: FeedbackCategory | None, q: str | None, limit: int, offset: int) -> Sequence[PublicListEntry[RowT]]
methods.doc:
Public rows only (``public`` and not CRASH), filtered, sorted — ``newest``
(``created_at``, then id, descending), ``votes`` (most, then newest) or ``updated``
(``updated_at``, then id) — and paged, each with its counts in SQL (a ``GROUP BY``,
never per row). ``q`` searches ``title`` (case-insensitive) where it is a
plaintext column; the service never sends one where it is not.

methods.name: get_public
methods.doc:
The row by id, whatever its flag and whoever asks, or None when missing (kastlan:
within the company's RLS). The service decides who sees it.

members.name: PublicFeedbackRow
members.doc:
A report as the public parts read it (§9.3): :class:`FeedbackRow` and the columns
the public list and detail show.

members.name: PublicListEntry
members.doc:
One row of the public list with its counts, as the repository's SQL answers them
(§9.9, B4): ``votes`` and ``comment_count`` (visible comments) are counts, ``voted``
whether the viewer has a vote.

members.name: PublicSort
members.doc:
How the public list may be sorted (§9.6): ``newest`` (the default), ``votes`` (most,
then newest) or ``updated``.

members.name: ReplyPlan
members.doc:
What a reply does to its report (§9.7): ``changes`` to write onto the row (empty
when the reply moves no status), and the ``status_from`` / ``status_to`` the reply
row records (both ``None`` then).

members.name: ReworkBlock
members.doc:
One rework round of an old body (§10.4): when it was sent (UTC, to the minute), what
it says, and its one file — the block's first ``[screenshot]`` line — or ``None``.

members.name: StoredAttachment
members.doc: A stored file as :meth:`AttachmentStorage.read` answers it (§2.5).

fields.name: media_type
fields.doc: As stored, or from the key's extension (kk, ka); the kit re-reads the bytes (2.12).

fields.name: filename
fields.doc: ``None``: served as ``attachment.<ext>``.

members.name: UnknownAttachmentUrlError
members.doc: A ``screenshot_url`` / ``attachment_urls`` entry that is not this app's own attachment URL.

members.name: UpdatePlan
members.doc:
What to write onto the row: ``changes`` is the sent fields, plus the server's own
``status`` (a rework sent back to the queue — :func:`rework_status`; ``reopened``
says it happened) and ``resolved_at`` (a stamp or a clear) when they apply.

``rework`` (0.13 only, §10.3): set when ``reopened`` — the appended block, split, for
the service to write as an entry; ``body`` is then NOT in ``changes``.

members.name: anonymise_feedback
members.signature: anonymise_feedback(*, title: str | None, body: str | None, context: Mapping[str, Any] | None, screenshot_url: str | None, attachment_urls: Iterable[str] | None, identifiers: Iterable[str | None], policy: AttachmentUrlPolicy = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_POLICY) -> AnonymisedFeedback
members.doc:
One report with its author taken out (keksdose ``_anonymise_feedback`` row loop, ``:1201-1214``).

``identifiers`` are the person's own strings — build them with
:func:`eifi1_server_kit.auth.erasure_identifiers` (the email, the old display name, the
full name in every order, longest first; never a bare first or last name). The body's
``[screenshot] <url>`` lines are stripped (the fix this module documents) BEFORE the
scrub, and every URL the row named is returned in ``urls`` for
:func:`attachment_keys_to_purge`. ``changes`` sets ``user_id``, ``crash_fingerprint``,
``screenshot_url`` and ``attachment_urls`` to ``None``.

members.name: anonymise_reply
members.signature: anonymise_reply(*, body: str | None, attachment_url: str | None, identifiers: Iterable[str | None]) -> AnonymisedFeedback
members.doc:
One entry of ``feedback_replies`` with its writer taken out (§9.12, §10.3): kept,
``author_id`` ``None``, the body scrubbed (:func:`scrub_text`). A rework entry's file
goes as the report's do: ``attachment_url`` set to ``None`` and the URL answered in
``urls`` for :func:`attachment_keys_to_purge` (an entry without one is not written
there).

members.name: append_rework
members.signature: append_rework(body: str, note: str, url: str | None = None, *, now: datetime, prefix: str = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_PREFIX) -> str | None
members.doc:
``body`` with one rework round appended — the exact text the contract's PATCH carried.

Legacy (§10.3): a rework is an entry now; this is the shape a migration's downgrade
writes back and an old client still sends for one release.

Mirrors the kit's ``appendRework``: the note is required and trimmed (a file alone
cannot be sent — ``None`` for a blank note, as the kit returns ``null``); ONE file per
round, as one ``[screenshot] <url>`` line; ``\n\n`` is left out when the old body is
``""``. The old body is kept byte for byte, so the result strictly extends it — which
is what :func:`eifi1_server_kit.feedback.is_rework_append` recognises.

Raises :class:`ValueError` for a ``url`` outside ``prefix``: written anyway it would sit
in the body as prose no reader recognises as a file.

members.name: appended_text
members.signature: appended_text(old_body: str | None, new_body: str) -> str
members.doc: What a rework append added (``""`` when ``new_body`` does not extend ``old_body``).

members.name: attachment_keys_to_purge
members.signature: attachment_keys_to_purge(erased_urls: Iterable[str], other_urls: Iterable[str], *, policy: AttachmentUrlPolicy = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_POLICY) -> list[str]
members.doc:
The keys whose objects may be deleted, sorted (keksdose ``:1182-1222``).

Content-addressed keys carry no user, so two people who upload byte-identical files
share one object: a URL any OTHER report still names — in a column or in its body
(collect those with :func:`feedback_attachment_urls`) — is kept. URLs that are not this
app's own are never purge candidates. The purge itself is the app's (keksdose prefixes
``feedback/`` and hands the list to its object store after the commit).

members.name: attachment_line
members.doc: The body line for one uploaded file (kit ``feedbackAttachmentLine``).

members.name: body_attachment_urls
members.signature: body_attachment_urls(body: str | None, *, prefix: str = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_PREFIX) -> list[str]
members.doc: The URLs a body's ``[screenshot]`` lines name — a rework's files live there, not in the columns.

members.name: check_author_edit
members.signature: check_author_edit(status: FeedbackStatus | str, changes: Mapping[str, Any], *, is_author: bool, reworking: bool, filed_private: bool = False) -> None
members.doc:
The non-admin half of the lanes (keksdose ``feedback_service.py:152-161``), in its order.

Raises :class:`FeedbackForbiddenError` with keksdose's wording: ``Not the author``;
``Author cannot change: <fields>``; ``Entry is in <STATUS>; only OPEN / READY /
IN_PROGRESS entries can be edited by the author`` (unless ``reworking``, or a
``public``-only change on a ``filed_private`` report, §9.3).

members.name: context_size
members.doc: The size :data:`MAX_CONTEXT_SIZE` is compared with (``0`` for no context).

members.name: crash_body
members.signature: crash_body(payload: CrashReportCreate, *, user_id: int | str, user_email: str, fingerprint: str, seen_at: str | None = None) -> str
members.doc:
The diagnostics block, as plain greppable text (keksdose ``_crash_body``, ``:262``).

The ``User:`` line embeds the address — which is why erasure scrubs bodies too
(:func:`eifi1_server_kit.feedback.anonymise_feedback`).

members.name: crash_context
members.signature: crash_context(payload: CrashReportCreate, *, user_id: int | str, user_email: str | None, user_display_name: str | None, fingerprint: str, seen_at: str) -> dict[str, Any]
members.doc:
A new crash row's ``context`` (keksdose ``:346-366``; contract §3.2).

The dialog's key set — so the admin view renders a crash like a hand-filed report,
``origin`` and ``environment`` included (the env chip) — plus what only an automatic
report has: ``fingerprint``, ``boundary``, ``online``, ``occurrences``,
``first_seen_at``, ``last_seen_at`` and ``auto_reported: true``.

members.name: crash_fingerprint
members.signature: crash_fingerprint(payload: CrashReportCreate, user_id: int | str) -> str
members.doc:
Same user, build, route, error and top of stack → same key (keksdose ``_fingerprint``, ``:228``).

``sha256`` over ``\x1f``-joined ``str(user_id)``, version, route, name, the normalised
message and the first 3 normalised stack lines, cut to 32 hex characters. Per user by
design — two people on the same broken page are two reports. Only 3 frames, because
deeper ones drift with React's call path. ``origin`` / ``environment`` take no part.

members.name: crash_reference
members.doc: The first 8 fingerprint characters, or ``None`` (keksdose ``feedback_router.py:166``).

members.name: crash_seen_at
members.signature: crash_seen_at(payload: CrashReportCreate, now: datetime | None = None) -> str
members.doc: When it happened, ISO 8601: the client's ``occurred_at``, else ``now`` (UTC).

members.name: crash_title
members.doc:
``[crash] <name>: <message>``, at most 255 characters and never blank (keksdose ``:254``).

``feedback.title`` is ``String(255)`` while a message may be 2000 characters: an
untruncated title is a 500 on INSERT — the crash reporter crashing.

members.name: decide_crash
members.doc:
Fold into the open row, or file a new one.

``candidate_status`` is the status of the row the APP'S QUERY found: the newest row with
the same fingerprint whose status is NOT terminal — keksdose ``record_crash``
(``feedback_service.py:312-318``) filters ``status NOT IN TERMINAL_STATUSES`` in the
query itself, so an older re-opened row is counted even when a newer one with the same
fingerprint was settled. Passing the newest row of ANY status instead files a duplicate
in exactly that case (kastlan's finding). With keksdose's query the candidate always
folds; ``None`` (no open row) files a new one — a fixed crash coming back is news, and
hiding it inside a resolved entry is how a regression goes unnoticed. Any non-terminal
status folds, IN_EVALUATION included.

members.name: download_attachment
members.signature: async download_attachment(actor: FeedbackActor, key: str, *, storage: AttachmentStorage, policy: AttachmentUrlPolicy, require_utf8_text: bool = False) -> AttachmentDownload
members.doc:
One stored file, with Kurvenschmiede's download rules for all three (§2.12).

404 ("Attachment not found") for a key outside the policy's pattern — the only thing
between a caller and the store path — and for a file the store does not have or will
not show this viewer. The type is read off the BYTES, never the stored word: their
signature, else ``text/plain; charset=utf-8`` when stored as text and still text,
else ``application/octet-stream``. ``Content-Disposition`` always — ``inline`` for
the four pictures only — with the stored name or ``attachment.<ext>``, and
``X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`` always.

members.name: feedback_attachment_urls
members.signature: feedback_attachment_urls(*, screenshot_url: str | None, attachment_urls: Iterable[str] | None, body: str | None, policy: AttachmentUrlPolicy = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_POLICY) -> set[str]
members.doc: Every attachment URL one report names — both columns AND the body's rework lines.

members.name: feedback_recipients
members.signature: feedback_recipients(*, author_id: int | None, commenter_ids: Iterable[int | None], writer_id: int | None) -> list[int]
members.doc:
Who hears of a new reply or comment (9.11): the report's author first, then each
earlier commenter in the order of their first comment; never the writer, nobody twice,
no ``None`` (an erased account). Never asked for a rework entry, which tells nobody
(§10.2 decision 10).

The app still drops anyone who may no longer see the report (a commenter outside
``public_viewer``, a report switched off) and any deactivated, erased or demo account.

members.name: fold_crash_context
members.signature: fold_crash_context(context: Mapping[str, Any] | None, seen_at: str) -> dict[str, Any]
members.doc:
The existing row's context with one more occurrence (keksdose ``:322-331``).

A NEW dict, never a mutation: a plain JSON column has no mutation tracking, so an
in-place edit is never written and the counter would sit at 1 forever.

members.name: initial_status
members.signature: initial_status(*, author_is_admin: bool, crash: bool = False) -> FeedbackStatus
members.doc:
The status a new row is filed in, decided by the server at submit (contract §8.2).

READY for an admin's own report: an admin filing it has triaged it by writing it, so it
is released for implementation at once (keksdose live #396, Marcel: "my (or admin
feedback) will be right away persisted with ready to implement"). OPEN for everyone
else's — filed, not yet triaged. A crash report is OPEN whoever's session it came
from: nobody has looked at it yet.

members.name: is_public
members.signature: is_public(category: FeedbackCategory | str, public: bool | None) -> bool
members.doc:
Is a report in the public parts (9.3)? Its ``public`` flag is set and it is no
CRASH: a crash's body carries the reporter's address, whatever its flag (decision 9).

members.name: is_rework_append
members.signature: is_rework_append(old_body: str | None, changes: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool
members.doc:
Is this PATCH an APPEND to the body — the rework composer's shape?

Legacy (§10.3): server-kit 0.13 turns such a PATCH into a rework entry
(:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.plan_update`'s ``rework``); from 0.14 it is a 422.

keksdose ``feedback_service.py:93`` ``_is_rework_append``, as the contract states it
(§3.4): the changed fields are ``{"body"}`` and nothing else, and the new body strictly
extends the old one, so the original is still there verbatim and first. A rewrite, a
truncation, or a body change bundled with any other field (a status included) is not
one. Asked of every actor, admins included (keksdose live #331).

``changes`` is what the client actually sent — ``payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)``.

members.name: legacy_rework_block
members.signature: legacy_rework_block(old_body: str | None, new_body: str, *, now: datetime, prefix: str = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_PREFIX) -> ReworkBlock
members.doc:
The block an old client's append carries (§10.3): the appended text split by
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.split_rework_blocks` when it is exactly one
well-formed block; anything else appended is one round sent ``now``, its text the
note, no file.

members.name: normalise_crash_text
members.doc:
Fold what differs between two occurrences of the SAME defect (keksdose ``_normalise``, ``:212``).

Hex runs of 6+ (build hashes, chunk names, uuids) then digit runs (ids, offsets, line
numbers) become ``#``; whitespace folds to one space; the ends are stripped. Without it
"Loading chunk 1234 failed" and "Loading chunk 5678 failed" are two entries per visitor.

members.name: opens_with_rework_rule
members.signature: opens_with_rework_rule(old_body: str | None, new_body: str) -> bool
members.doc:
Does the appended part open with a ``--- REWORK … ---`` rule line?

A STRICTER test than the contract's append rule, for an app that wants to tell a
rework from any other append (the contract does not ask it to; keksdose never has).

members.name: plan_reply
members.signature: plan_reply(*, status: FeedbackStatus | str, new_status: FeedbackStatus | str | None, now: datetime | None = None) -> ReplyPlan
members.doc:
A reply's status move, as data (§9.7). ``status`` is the row's stored one,
``new_status`` what the reply chose; ``None`` changes nothing.

With a status, ``changes`` holds it and ``resolved_at`` by :func:`resolved_at_change`
(as :func:`plan_update`), and the reply records the move — also onto the status the
row already has, which is how a reply answers the nudge after a status-only move into
a decided status. CRASH is a category, not a status, so nothing is refused here.

members.name: plan_rework
members.signature: plan_rework(*, status: FeedbackStatus | str, is_author: bool, actor_is_admin: bool, now: datetime | None = None) -> ReplyPlan
members.doc:
A rework entry's move, as data (§10.3): the report's author only — anyone else,
an admin included, is a :class:`FeedbackForbiddenError` :data:`REWORK_AUTHOR_ONLY` —
on a row in :data:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.REWORKABLE_STATUSES` (else 403 "Entry is
in <STATUS>; …"). The row goes to :func:`rework_status` (REWORK for an admin author,
OPEN otherwise), ``resolved_at`` cleared on leaving DONE / WONT_DO, and the entry
records ``status_from`` / ``status_to``.

members.name: plan_update
members.signature: plan_update(*, status: FeedbackStatus | str, body: str | None, changes: Mapping[str, Any], is_admin: bool, is_author: bool, now: datetime | None = None, filed_private: bool = False, prefix: str = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_PREFIX) -> UpdatePlan
members.doc:
The whole PATCH rule for one row, as data (keksdose ``update_feedback``).

``status`` / ``body`` are the row's STORED values; ``changes`` is what the client sent
(``payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)``) and is not mutated. Raises
:class:`CrashCategoryNotAssignableError` (→ 422) or :class:`FeedbackForbiddenError`
(→ 403); otherwise every key of :attr:`UpdatePlan.changes` is a column to assign.
``now`` stamps ``resolved_at`` (default: the current UTC time). ``filed_private`` is
the row's flag (§9.3): its author may then switch ``public`` at any status.

**The legacy append** (0.13 only, §10.3): a rework append on a row outside the author's
lane sets :attr:`UpdatePlan.rework` (:func:`legacy_rework_block`, its file found under
``prefix``) and drops ``body`` from ``changes``; the status is :func:`rework_status`'s.

members.name: public_body
members.signature: public_body(body: str | None, *, policy: AttachmentUrlPolicy = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_POLICY) -> str
members.doc:
A report's body as the public detail shows it (9.4), applied by the server, never
the client.

Every ``[screenshot] <url>`` line is dropped (§3.4's pattern); every other attachment
URL is removed wherever it stands (:func:`public_text`); kastlan's folded headers
``--- COMMENT <stamp> · <name> ---`` become ``--- COMMENT <stamp> ---``. The
``--- REWORK <stamp> ---`` lines and the notes stay: the author's own words.

members.name: public_text
members.signature: public_text(text: str | None, *, policy: AttachmentUrlPolicy = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_POLICY) -> str
members.doc:
``text`` with every attachment URL of ``policy`` removed, wherever it stands (9.4):
each leaves ``[…]``. A path under another prefix is kept.

Applied to every comment and reply body that leaves for someone other than its writer
and an admin (P-e), and by :func:`public_body`.

members.name: reject_manual_crash
members.doc:
Refuse CRASH set by hand — on a create or an update, admins included.

keksdose ``feedback_service.py:23`` ``_reject_manual_crash``: a row wearing the badge
means the error boundary filed it, so it carries a fingerprint and an ``auto_reported``
context; the dedupe and the occurrence counter hang off those. Call it BEFORE loading
the row, so the payload is refused whether or not the row exists.

members.name: reopens
members.signature: reopens(status: FeedbackStatus | str, *, reworking: bool) -> bool
members.doc:
Does a rework append send this row back to the queue? Yes outside OPEN / READY /
IN_PROGRESS (keksdose ``:179``); :func:`rework_status` says to which status.

members.name: resolved_at_change
members.signature: resolved_at_change(old_status: FeedbackStatus | str, new_status: FeedbackStatus | str | None) -> Literal['stamp', 'clear'] | None
members.doc:
What a status write does to ``resolved_at`` (keksdose ``feedback_service.py:185-194``).

``"stamp"`` on a genuine transition INTO DONE / WONT_DO (DONE → DONE and DONE → WONT_DO
keep the original date), ``"clear"`` on leaving them (a rework back to OPEN, the
DONE → IN_EVALUATION back-step), ``None`` otherwise — including when no status was sent.

members.name: rework_count
members.doc:
How many times a report has been sent back: its ``--- REWORK … ---`` rule lines.

Legacy (§10.3): a report's reworks are its ``rework`` entries now; this counts an
unmigrated body (the client's fallback without ``replies``).

Derived, never stored (contract §3.1), so nothing can forget to set it. Folded kastlan
comments do not count (kit ``reworkCount``).

members.name: rework_stamp
members.doc: The stamp of a rework rule: ``now`` in UTC, to the minute. A naive ``now`` is read as UTC.

members.name: rework_status
members.doc:
Where a rework sends a row back to (§10.2 decision 5): REWORK when an admin sends
it — an admin's rework is already triaged, released for work again — and OPEN
otherwise, because a user's rework is new input for the triager, who releases it to
REWORK. (Before 0.13 an admin's went to READY.)

members.name: scrub_context
members.signature: scrub_context(context: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None
members.doc:
Keep the diagnostics, drop everything that names the reporter (keksdose ``_scrub_context``, ``:1156``).

A NEW dict (a JSON column has no mutation tracking); ``None`` when nothing is left.

members.name: scrub_text
members.signature: scrub_text(text: str | None, needles: Iterable[str | None]) -> str
members.doc:
Replace each needle wherever it appears, case-insensitively (keksdose ``_scrub_text``, ``:1135``).

Only exact, known strings are removed. Free prose is left alone deliberately: a rule
broad enough to catch a name somebody typed about themselves is broad enough to mangle
the report, and an operator can still edit a self-identification out by hand.

members.name: split_body_attachments
members.signature: split_body_attachments(body: str | None, *, prefix: str = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_PREFIX) -> tuple[str, list[str]]
members.doc:
``(text, urls)``: the body without its file lines (trailing blank lines dropped), and
the URLs those lines named, in body order (kit ``splitBodyAttachments``).

members.name: split_rework_blocks
members.signature: split_rework_blocks(body: str | None, *, prefix: str = DEFAULT_ATTACHMENT_URL_PREFIX) -> tuple[str, list[ReworkBlock]]
members.doc:
``(description, blocks)``: a body without its rework rounds, and the rounds, in body
order (§10.4) — what each app's migration writes as ``rework`` entries.

A block opens on a line :data:`REWORK_BLOCK_RE` matches (after trimming) and runs to
the next :data:`BLOCK_RULE_RE` line or the end; its first ``[screenshot]`` line under
``prefix`` is ``url``, the rest, trimmed, is ``note``. kastlan's folded ``--- COMMENT
… ---`` blocks stay in the description as they are. The description loses its trailing
whitespace; a body without a block comes back unchanged (``""`` for ``None``).

Raises :class:`ValueError` on a line :data:`REWORK_RULE_RE` matches that is no block
(``--- REWORK ANSWERED 2026-09-16 ---``, a date-only rule) or a stamp that is no date,
so a migration stops rather than guess. Split ``body`` only, never ``outcome``:
keksdose's ``outcome`` holds such lines from old loop answers.

members.name: stamp_identity
members.signature: stamp_identity(context: Mapping[str, Any] | None, *, user_id: int | str | None, user_email: str | None, user_display_name: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]
members.doc:
The sent context with ``user_id`` / ``user_email`` / ``user_display_name`` written by
the server from the session (Kurvenschmiede ``feedback_service.py:165`` ``stamped_context``).

Everything else — the page, the browser, the build — is the client's to know. Returns a
NEW dict: a plain JSON column has no mutation tracking (keksdose
``feedback_service.py:323-327``).

members.name: throttle_upload
members.doc:
Charge one upload to ``user_id``'s window, or refuse with
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.FeedbackThrottledError` (429, ``Retry-After``).

keksdose's support door calls it too, on the same ``.upload`` window, so the 429's
sentence is written once.

members.name: truncate
members.doc: ``text`` cut to ``limit`` characters, the last one an ellipsis when it was cut.

members.name: upload_attachment
members.signature: async upload_attachment(actor: FeedbackActor, file: UploadSource, *, declared_type: str | None, filename: str | None, storage: AttachmentStorage, policy: AttachmentUrlPolicy, limiter: SlidingWindowRateLimiter | None, decode_images: bool = False, require_utf8_text: bool = False) -> str

members.name: utc_now
members.doc: The current time, aware, in UTC — the default :data:`Clock`.

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.feedback.router
modules.summary: The feedback routes as one router factory: ``feedback_router(FeedbackDeps(...))``.
modules.doc:
The feedback routes as one router factory: ``feedback_router(FeedbackDeps(...))``.

Layer 2 (``docs/server-services-harmonization.md`` §2.8–§2.10, §4.1 in ``Eifi1/ui-kit``),
behind the ``fastapi`` extra (``eifi1-server-kit[fastapi]``). The app passes its own
dependencies and shapes — the actor, the repository on the request's session, the
storage, its demo guard factory and its admin guard, its attachment URL policy and its
schema subclasses — and includes the router as it includes its own::

    router = feedback_router(FeedbackDeps(
        actor=feedback_actor, repository=feedback_repository, storage=feedback_storage,
        demo_guard=not_in_the_demo, admin_guard=require_role(UserRole.ADMIN),
        policy=FEEDBACK_ATTACHMENTS, create_model=FeedbackCreate, decode_images=True,
    ))
    app.include_router(router, prefix="/api/v1")
    app.state.feedback_limiters = FeedbackLimiters()
    install_contract_error_handlers(app)

**The guards are the app's** (§2.8), first in each route's ``dependencies=[…]``, so
FastAPI runs them before the endpoint's parameters and before the body is validated (a
demo's ``json={}`` is a 403 ``demo_refused``, not a 422), and the apps' route walks find
them by their own names. ``demo_guard("uploads")`` guards the upload,
``demo_guard("feedback")`` the create and the PATCH, ``admin_guard`` the inbox; the crash
route takes none (its service answers a demo ``stored: false``).

**The endpoints carry keksdose's names** (``upload_attachment``, ``download_attachment``,
``create``, ``report_crash``, ``list_my``, ``list_all``, ``update``), the upload's field is
``file``, the inbox's query ``status_filter`` and the path parameter ``{feedback_id}``, so
keksdose's operation ids and its ``Body_upload_attachment_api_v1_feedback_attachments_post``
component stay as they are. An app's own extra routes go AFTER this router: a
``GET /feedback/{feedback_id}`` included first would take ``GET /feedback/my``.

**The router raises no** ``HTTPException``: past the app's guards every refusal is a kit
refusal, answered by :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.errors.install_contract_error_handlers`.
Each request builds a :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.FeedbackService` on the
request's repository; each flow makes at most one repository write, as its last step, and
the kit never commits (§2.7).

**Public feedback** (0.11, ``docs/feedback-harmonization.md`` §9.9): with ``deps.replies``
the router adds ``POST /{feedback_id}/replies`` (``create_reply``) and, since 0.13 (§10.3),
``POST /{feedback_id}/rework`` (``create_rework``, the author's, behind the demo guard
only); with
``deps.public_viewer`` (which needs ``comments``, ``votes`` and ``people``) eight more —
``list_public``, ``get_public``, ``list_comments``, ``create_comment``, ``hide_comment``,
``delete_comment``, ``vote``, ``unvote``. They go after the inbox and before the PATCH, so
``/public`` comes before any ``/{feedback_id}`` GET the app adds after this router. The
existing answers fill the new fields from the stores given (one call per store a page).

No ``from __future__ import annotations`` here, on purpose: the endpoints' parameter
types are the app's models, closed over in the factory, and FastAPI cannot resolve a
string annotation that names a local.

members.name: FeedbackDeps
members.doc: What an app hands :func:`feedback_router` (§2.9): its dependencies, shapes and choices.

fields.doc: The app's dependency answering a :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.FeedbackActor`.

fields.name: repository
fields.doc: The app's dependency answering a ``FeedbackRepository[RowT]`` on the request's session.

fields.name: storage
fields.doc: The app's dependency answering an :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.AttachmentStorage`.

fields.name: demo_guard
fields.doc: The app's factory: ``demo_guard("uploads")``, ``demo_guard("feedback")``.

fields.name: admin_guard
fields.doc: The app's dependency on ``GET /feedback``.

fields.name: policy
fields.doc: The app's keys and URLs; ``policy.prefix`` must be the mounted path.

fields.name: create_model
fields.doc: The app's subclass: its names and fields. Its ``attachment_url_policy`` must be ``policy``.

fields.name: to_response
fields.doc:
``(row, address)`` → the answer; ``None``: ``response_model.model_validate(row)``
with ``user_email`` the address (the inbox's; ``None`` everywhere else).

fields.name: foreign_row
fields.doc: A non-admin's PATCH on another person's row: 403 (keksdose, kastlan) or 404 (Kurvenschmiede).

fields.name: decode_images
fields.doc: :func:`~eifi1_server_kit.uploads.ensure_decodable_image` on every upload (the ``images`` extra; kk, ka).

fields.name: require_utf8_text
fields.doc: Text is text only when UTF-8 (Kurvenschmiede).

fields.name: replies
fields.doc: The app's dependency answering a ``FeedbackReplyStore``: mounts ``create_reply``.

fields.name: comments
fields.doc:
The app's dependencies answering a ``FeedbackCommentStore``, a ``FeedbackVoteStore``
and a ``PeopleLookup``: each required with ``public_viewer``.

fields.name: public_viewer
fields.doc:
Who sees the public parts, on the viewer (an admin always does, a demo never):
keksdose every signed-in user, Kurvenschmiede ADMIN / MEMBER / REVIEWER. ``None``
mounts no public route (kastlan).

fields.name: public_search
fields.doc: ``q`` searches the title; False where titles are sealed (Kurvenschmiede): a 422.

fields.name: rework_model
fields.doc:
``POST /{feedback_id}/rework``'s body (§10.3): subclass it to narrow its
``attachment_url_policy``; the service checks ``policy`` either way.

members.name: app_state_limiters
members.doc:
The app's :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.limiter.FeedbackLimiters`, read per request from
``app.state.feedback_limiters`` — built once in ``create_app``, so a test that builds an
app per test starts with empty windows.

members.name: feedback_router
members.signature: feedback_router[RowT: FeedbackRow](deps: FeedbackDeps[RowT], *, prefix: str = '/feedback', tags: Sequence[str] = ('feedback',)) -> APIRouter
members.doc:
The contract's seven routes (§3.3), on ``APIRouter(prefix=prefix, tags=tags)``, in
this order: ``POST /attachments``, ``GET /attachments/{key}``, ``POST ""``,
``POST /crash``, ``GET /my``, ``GET ""``, then public feedback's routes (§9.9: the
eight with ``public_viewer``, ``POST /{feedback_id}/replies`` and
``POST /{feedback_id}/rework`` with ``replies``), and ``PATCH /{feedback_id}`` last.

Raises :class:`ValueError` when ``deps.create_model.attachment_url_policy`` is not
``deps.policy``: two policies would let a report name a key the download refuses; and
when ``deps.public_viewer`` is set without ``comments``, ``votes`` or ``people``.

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.uploads
modules.summary: What an uploaded attachment IS, decided by its bytes — and how it may be served back.
modules.doc:
What an uploaded attachment IS, decided by its bytes — and how it may be served back.

The contract's attachment policy (§3.5): ``image/png``, ``image/jpeg``, ``image/webp``,
``image/gif``, ``application/pdf``, ``text/plain``; 10 MB per file; an empty file is a
400, an oversized one a 413, a file claiming to be a picture that is not one a 400,
anything else a 415. Images are served ``inline``, everything else as ``attachment``.

**The bytes decide, not the header** — Kurvenschmiede's approach, lifted from
``kurvenschmiede/adapters/api/feedback_router.py:54-116``: the declared type is the
client's word for it, and a file labelled ``image/png`` containing a script would be a
stored cross-site script against the admin who opens it. A picture or a PDF is named by
its signature; plain text has none, so it needs the declaration and no NUL byte —
keksdose's policy, and the default (``require_utf8_text=True`` adds Kurvenschmiede's
UTF-8 rule). No Pillow: a magic-number table is smaller than the dependency. What that gives up — a
truncated PNG passes, because only the head is read — is the trade Kurvenschmiede made
knowingly; keksdose's Pillow ``verify()`` (dev#510) is :func:`ensure_decodable_image`,
behind the optional ``images`` extra, for an app that wants it after the check.

Nothing here stores anything. :func:`check_upload` answers what the file is;
:func:`store_attachment` runs the check, mints keksdose's content-addressed key and hands
the bytes to the app's own ``save`` — the object store, the disk or a table stays the app's.

members.name: ACCEPTED_MEDIA_TYPES
members.doc:
Accepted media type → the extension a stored key carries (keksdose ``upload_guards.py:198``
``ATTACHMENT_EXT``). No SVG, no HTML: nothing that can carry script onto the app's origin.

members.name: ACCEPT_LIST
members.doc: The accepted types as an ``<input accept>`` / dialog list, in the contract's order.

members.name: EXTENSION_MEDIA_TYPES
members.doc:
Extension → the ``Content-Type`` to serve it with (keksdose ``upload_guards.py:206``
``EXT_MEDIA_TYPE``). ``jpeg`` is read as well as written ``jpg`` for keys minted elsewhere.

members.name: IMAGE_MEDIA_TYPES
members.doc: The ONLY media types any download may serve ``inline`` (keksdose ``upload_guards.py:227``).

members.name: MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES
members.doc: Per-file ceiling (contract §3.5; keksdose ``upload_guards.py:197`` ``ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES``).

members.name: UNDECODABLE_IMAGE_TYPES
members.doc:
Picture types Pillow has no decoder for, which :func:`ensure_decodable_image` lets
through unparsed (keksdose ``upload_guards.py:46`` ``UNDECODABLE_IMAGE_TYPES``): the
guard exists to catch a RENAMED file and would refuse every real HEIC from a phone with
the fakes. Not in :data:`ACCEPTED_MEDIA_TYPES`; it matters to an app's own wider policy
(keksdose's receipt scans).

members.name: CheckedUpload
members.doc: An accepted file: what it is, the extension its key carries, how it is served.

members.name: EmptyUploadError
members.doc: The file has no bytes (→ 400).

members.name: NotAnImageError
members.doc: Declared as one of the accepted pictures, and the bytes are not one (→ 400).

members.name: StoredUpload
members.doc: What :func:`store_attachment` stored: the key, and the checked file it was minted for.

members.name: UnsupportedUploadTypeError
members.doc: Not one of the accepted types, whatever it is called (→ 415).

members.name: UploadRejectedError
members.doc: Base class of every upload refusal; ``status_code`` is the contract's answer (§3.7).

members.name: UploadSource
members.doc:
What :func:`read_capped_upload` reads: Starlette's ``UploadFile`` (FastAPI's is the
same class), or anything with its ``read``.

members.name: UploadTooLargeError
members.doc: The file is over the per-file ceiling (→ 413).

members.name: bare_media_type
members.doc:
The declared type without parameters, lower-cased (``text/plain; charset=…`` → ``text/plain``).

keksdose ``upload_guards.py:86`` ``bare_media_type``.

members.name: check_upload
members.signature: check_upload(data: bytes, declared_type: str | None, *, max_bytes: int = MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES, require_utf8_text: bool = False) -> CheckedUpload
members.doc:
Accept or refuse one uploaded file, by its bytes.

In order — the contract's statuses (§3.5, §3.7) on Kurvenschmiede's detection
(``feedback_router.py:123`` ``_read_upload``):

1. no bytes → :class:`EmptyUploadError` (400);
2. over ``max_bytes`` → :class:`UploadTooLargeError` (413) — read the upload with
   :func:`read_capped_upload`, which reads one byte past the cap and no more, and
   refuses these two before the whole of a huge upload is ever in memory;
3. :func:`sniffed_type` names it → accepted, as the DETECTED type (a PNG declared
   ``image/jpeg`` is stored and served as a PNG); declared ``text/plain`` without a NUL
   byte is text in any encoding, unless ``require_utf8_text=True`` (Kurvenschmiede)
   asks for UTF-8 as well;
4. otherwise, declared as one of the accepted pictures → :class:`NotAnImageError`
   (400: "renamed to .png"); anything else → :class:`UnsupportedUploadTypeError` (415).

One deliberate difference from Kurvenschmiede: there a declared ``image/*`` OUTSIDE the
list (``image/svg+xml``, ``image/heic``) was a 400; the contract (§3.7) and keksdose's
test (``test_feedback_attachments.py:125``) call a type outside the list a 415.

members.name: content_addressed_key
members.doc:
keksdose's key: ``sha256(bytes)[:12].<ext>`` (``upload_guards.py:272``).

The same paste twice is one URL — and, for erasure, one object two reports may share
(see :func:`eifi1_server_kit.feedback.attachment_keys_to_purge`). kastlan mints
``<uuid32>_<sha12>.<ext>`` and Kurvenschmiede an HMAC of the same shape; they pass
their own ``mint_key`` to :func:`store_attachment`, or call :func:`check_upload` alone.

members.name: content_disposition
members.signature: content_disposition(filename: str, disposition: Disposition = 'attachment', *, fallback: str | None = None) -> str
members.doc:
A ``Content-Disposition`` value whose filename cannot break the header, and whose
plain name is a file name every system will write.

The name is whatever the client called the file. The ORIGINAL goes into the RFC 5987
``filename*``, percent-encoded, so nothing is lost; every browser prefers that one, and
so does ui-kit's ``filenameFromDisposition`` (0.34). The plain ``filename=`` is for a
reader that takes nothing else — ``curl -J`` among them — and is narrowed to ASCII:
Starlette encodes header values as latin-1, so an en dash or a CJK character there was
a 500 out of a plain GET (keksdose ``upload_guards.py:277``, on its object-store branch
only). Quotes, backslashes and anything not printable are dropped; accents are folded
(``Débattement-à-gauche.csv`` → ``Debattement-a-gauche.csv``), and what still isn't
safe ASCII becomes ``_`` (``停车扫描-1.csv`` → ``____-1.csv``) — never ``?``, which
Windows refuses in a file name (KS S2; 0.7 wrote ``D?battement-?-gauche.csv``). Cut to
100 characters; nothing left is ``attachment``.

``fallback`` is the plain name an app would rather offer — ``curve-12.csv``, a record's
id — narrowed the same way; ``filename*`` keeps the original either way. keksdose's
``content_disposition`` and Kurvenschmiede's ``_disposition``
(``feedback_router.py:156``), merged.

members.name: ensure_decodable_image
members.signature: ensure_decodable_image(data: bytes, media_type: str | None) -> None
members.doc:
Refuse a picture whose bytes Pillow cannot parse (→ :class:`NotAnImageError`, 400).

keksdose's dev#510 guard (``upload_guards.py:147`` ``ensure_decodable_image``), lifted
as it is: :func:`check_upload` reads only the signature, so a PNG cut off after its
first bytes passes there — and is stored, attached, and shown to the person on the
other end as the browser's broken-image icon, which tells them nothing. Call it AFTER
:func:`check_upload`, with the DETECTED type (``checked.media_type``), as keksdose's
``store_attachment_bytes`` does. The status is the contract's for "declared a picture,
and it is not one" — 400, the same class and sentence as :func:`check_upload`'s.

What it does, exactly keksdose's:

* any ``image/*`` type is opened with ``PIL.Image.open`` and ``verify()``-ed — no
  ``load()``. ``verify()`` parses the container without decoding the raster, so it
  costs almost nothing on a real screenshot. It catches anything Pillow cannot
  identify, a truncated or corrupt PNG (chunk CRCs) and a truncated WebP; a JPEG or GIF
  cut off mid-raster still passes, since only decoding would see that;
* every failure is the same answer (``except Exception``), a decompression bomb
  included: the limit is Pillow's own, ``PIL.Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`` (≈ 89.5 M
  pixels) — ``open`` RAISES over twice that, and only WARNS
  (``DecompressionBombWarning``) between one and two times it, which passes unless the
  app turns that warning into an error. The kit sets no limit of its own; an app may
  lower Pillow's global;
* any other type returns at once — a PDF or a text file is served as a download and
  never drawn — and so do :data:`UNDECODABLE_IMAGE_TYPES`, which Pillow cannot open.

Pillow is imported lazily, and without the ``images`` extra
(``eifi1-server-kit[images]``) EVERY call raises :class:`ImportError` saying so — a
text file included — so a missing extra shows on the first upload rather than the
first picture. (keksdose imported it inside the ``try``, where a missing Pillow would
have refused every picture as "not an image".)

members.name: inline_or_attachment
members.doc:
The ``Content-Disposition`` a stored file may be served with: ``inline`` for the four
picture types, ``attachment`` for everything else — PDFs and text included, so neither is
ever interpreted in the app's origin (keksdose ``upload_guards.py:230``, feedback #87).
Unknown or absent is the safe answer, not the convenient one.

members.name: is_plain_text
members.signature: is_plain_text(data: bytes, *, require_utf8_text: bool = False) -> bool
members.doc:
No NUL byte in it — and, with ``require_utf8_text``, valid UTF-8 as well.

The default is keksdose's policy, the canon: it accepted any file declared
``text/plain`` (``upload_guards.py`` before 0.1.0), and its support chat shares that
policy, so a Windows-1252 bank export or a Latin-1 log is a text file like any other.
The encoding is not a security property here — text is only ever served as an
``attachment`` (:func:`inline_or_attachment`), never rendered in the app's origin, so
a browser saves the bytes as they are whatever ``charset`` the response names. The
NUL check stays: a text file has none, a binary renamed ``.txt`` almost always does.
(So does UTF-16, beside every ASCII character — such an export is refused too.)

``require_utf8_text=True`` is Kurvenschmiede's stricter rule
(``feedback_router.py:81`` ``_is_text``), kept for the app that wants it.

members.name: media_type_for_extension
members.doc: The ``Content-Type`` to serve a key's extension with, or ``None`` for an unknown one.

members.name: read_capped_upload
members.signature: async read_capped_upload(file: UploadSource, max_bytes: int = MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES) -> bytes
members.doc:
The bytes of an upload, read no further than one byte past ``max_bytes``.

``await file.read(max_bytes + 1)``: one byte past the cap is enough to know the file is
over it, so a 2 GB upload is never read whole to be refused (keksdose
``upload_guards.py:254``, Kurvenschmiede ``feedback_router.py:73``, kastlan
``feedback_router.py:111`` — the same line in each). Over the cap →
:class:`UploadTooLargeError` (413), no bytes → :class:`EmptyUploadError` (400), with
:func:`check_upload`'s wording. Then hand the bytes to :func:`check_upload` or
:func:`store_attachment` with the same ``max_bytes``.

members.name: signature_type
members.doc:
What these bytes say they are by their first few, or ``None``.

Kurvenschmiede ``feedback_router.py:69`` ``signature_type``.

members.name: sniffed_type
members.signature: sniffed_type(data: bytes, declared: str = '', *, require_utf8_text: bool = False) -> str | None
members.doc:
What a file IS, or ``None`` for anything this feature is not for.

Kurvenschmiede ``feedback_router.py:91`` ``sniffed_type``: the signature first, and
only when there is none, ``text/plain`` — if it was declared so and
:func:`is_plain_text` holds (no NUL; UTF-8 too with ``require_utf8_text``).
``declared`` may carry parameters; they are dropped.

members.name: store_attachment
members.signature: async store_attachment(data: bytes, declared_type: str | None, *, save: SaveFn, mint_key: MintKeyFn = content_addressed_key, max_bytes: int = MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES, require_utf8_text: bool = False) -> StoredUpload
members.doc:
The whole upload policy for one attachment, with the storing left to the app.

keksdose ``upload_guards.py:250`` ``store_attachment_bytes`` without its object store:
:func:`check_upload`, then ``mint_key(data, extension)``, then
``await save(key, data, media_type)`` — ``save`` adds whatever prefix or folder the app
keeps its attachments under. The caller keeps what is genuinely its own: the throttle
(charge it before or after this, see :mod:`eifi1_server_kit.limiter`), any per-user
refusal (keksdose's demo account), and the URL it answers with.

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.limiter
modules.summary: An in-process sliding-window rate limiter: at most N hits per key per window.
modules.doc:
An in-process sliding-window rate limiter: at most N hits per key per window.

keksdose ``backend/keksdose/infrastructure/rate_limit.py:45-124``
``SlidingWindowRateLimiter``, unchanged in behaviour — the lock, the blocked-hit rule and
the once-per-window sweep included. kastlan's copy (``infrastructure/rate_limit.py``) has
the same constructor and ``hit``/``reset``, so it swaps in as is.

**Process-local.** The window lives in this process's memory: each Cloud Run instance and
each uvicorn worker keeps its own counters (Kurvenschmiede's 2 workers make "20 an hour"
an effective 40). It bounds one client hammering one process — a browser stuck in a render
loop — not a cross-instance total. ``hit()`` is the whole contract, so a shared store
(Redis, a table) could replace the deques without touching a caller.

**No module globals here.** Build limiters per app — in ``create_app``, on
``app.state`` — so a test that builds an app per test starts with empty windows
(Kurvenschmiede ``infrastructure/security.py:288`` ``AuthLimiters`` / ``FeedbackLimiters``).
:class:`FeedbackLimiters` is that pair for the feedback routes.

**Whose address a window counts** is :func:`client_ip`'s answer: counted from the RIGHT of
``X-Forwarded-For``, as many hops as the app has proxies — never the left-most entry,
which the client writes itself.

**When to charge: before the work.** Call ``hit()`` where a request starts costing the
server something — the feedback contract's rule since round 0.36 (§3.5, §3.6, as all
three apps did; ``docs/server-services-harmonization.md`` §2.11), and what
:mod:`eifi1_server_kit.feedback.service` does:

* uploads — BEFORE the file is read and checked (keksdose
  ``upload_guards.throttle_attachment``), so a refused file uses a slot;
* crashes — BEFORE the dedupe (keksdose ``feedback_router.py:155``), so repeats count and
  ``occurrences`` stops rising after 20 an hour.

members.name: FeedbackLimiters
members.doc:
The feedback routes' budgets, keyed by user — one instance per app.

``upload``, ``comment`` and ``vote`` answer a refusal with 429 + ``Retry-After``;
``crash`` answers with a 202 ``stored: false``, never an error status (a crashed page
must not collect failures). Each is charged before the work (§3.5).
