methods.name: hit
methods.doc:
Register an attempt for ``key``.

``None`` when it is permitted; otherwise the seconds until the oldest hit ages out
(a ``Retry-After`` hint — see :func:`retry_after_header`). A blocked attempt is NOT
recorded, so a client that keeps hammering does not push its own unblock time out.

methods.name: count
methods.doc:
How many hits ``key`` has inside the window now, without recording one.

Never more than ``max_hits``, since a blocked hit is not recorded. A key never
hit answers ``0`` and is not added to the map.

methods.name: forget
methods.doc:
Drop ``key``'s window, as if it had never been hit. A sign-in that succeeds
clears its address's failures this way (:class:`eifi1_server_kit.auth.LoginFailureThrottle`).

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Drop all windows — the test seam.

members.name: client_ip
members.signature: client_ip(headers: Mapping[str, str], peer: str | None, *, trusted_hops: int) -> str
members.doc:
The caller's address for a per-IP window, counted from the RIGHT of
``X-Forwarded-For`` (``docs/landing-demo-harmonization.md`` §5.1)::

    ip = client_ip(request.headers, request.client.host if request.client else None,
                   trusted_hops=settings.trusted_proxy_hops)

**Why from the right.** Every proxy APPENDS the address it was connected from, so the
right end of the header is written by the app's own proxies and the left end by the
client — who may send any ``X-Forwarded-For`` it likes. The left-most entry (what
keksdose's ``client_ip`` and Kurvenschmiede's ``caller_address`` read) is therefore the
client's own choice: a random header per request is a fresh window per request, so the
demo's five-an-hour per IP would not hold, and 500 scripted starts would fill the live
cap and close the demo for a day. Counted from the right, the answer is the address the
outermost trusted proxy saw, which the client cannot choose.

``trusted_hops`` is the number of proxies in front of the app that each append to the
header (Caddy, a Cloud Run front end); it is the app's setting, per environment.
**Measure it once**: send a request with ``X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7`` and log the
header that arrives — your own address sits ``trusted_hops`` entries from the right,
and the fake one left of it. Then:

* ``0`` — no proxy: the header is ignored and ``peer`` answers (local development, a
  directly exposed process);
* ``N`` — the ``N``-th entry from the right;
* a header with fewer than ``N`` entries did not pass every proxy counted, so nothing
  in it is vouched for, and ``peer`` answers — never the left-most entry. Every such
  request shares the peer's window, which is the safe error: it limits too much,
  never too little.

Repeated ``X-Forwarded-For`` lines count as one comma-joined list, in order, when
``headers`` is Starlette's :class:`~starlette.datastructures.Headers` (a plain mapping
holds one value per name, matched without regard to case). Empty entries are skipped.
``peer`` is the TCP peer (``request.client.host``); without one the answer is
:data:`UNKNOWN_CLIENT`. The entry is returned as written — a limiter key, not a parsed
address.

members.name: retry_after_header
members.doc:
The ``Retry-After`` value for a ``hit()`` answer: whole seconds, rounded up past it
(keksdose ``upload_guards.py:82``: ``str(int(retry_after) + 1)``).

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.errors
modules.summary: The kit's refusals as HTTP answers: one call, so no app maps them by hand — or forgets to.
modules.doc:
The kit's refusals as HTTP answers: one call, so no app maps them by hand — or forgets to.

Every refusal the kit raises is a plain exception carrying the contract's status as
``status_code`` (:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.feedback.FeedbackError` 422 / 403 / 404 / 429,
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.uploads.UploadRejectedError` 400 / 413 / 415, the translation
review's 422 / 403, :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.AuthError` 400 / 401 / 403 / 409,
user administration's :class:`~eifi1_server_kit.user_admin.AccountError` 409 and
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.user_admin.RosterQueryError` 422, the settings rule's
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.settings.PatchNullError` 422, the demo's
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.demo.DemoError` 403 / 404 / 429 / 503, and billing's
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.BillingError` 400 / 402 / 404 / 409 / 422 / 502 / 503 and
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.billing.PlanLimitError` 402, a token route's
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.jobs.JobsTokenError` 401, and the notifications'
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.notifications.NotificationError` 400 / 409 / 422).
Most of them are :class:`ValueError` subclasses — on purpose, so one
raised inside a Pydantic validator is still a 422 there — and that is the trap this module
closes: keksdose (``main.py:166``) and Kurvenschmiede (``main.py:193``) each answer every
uncaught ``ValueError`` with a 400, so a kit refusal that slipped past an endpoint's own
``except`` came out as 400 instead of 403, 415 or 422, silently.

:func:`install_contract_error_handlers` registers one handler for each kit base class.
Starlette picks the handler by walking the exception's MRO
(``starlette/_exception_handler.py`` ``_lookup_exception_handler``) and takes the first
class it has one for, so ``FeedbackForbiddenError`` reaches the ``FeedbackError`` handler
before ``ValueError``'s — whichever was registered first. An endpoint's own ``except``
still wins over both; this answers only what nobody caught. The body is FastAPI's own
``HTTPException`` shape, ``{"detail": str(exc)}``, so no client can tell the difference —
plus ``"code"`` for a refusal that carries one (:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.AuthError`:
``{"detail": "Invalid credentials", "code": "invalid_credentials"}``), which the kit's
pages switch on instead of the English detail — and the refusal's ``extra`` fields, for
one that names something (:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.user_admin.AccountError`: kastlan's
``{"detail": …, "code": "last_admin", "companies": [...]}``; a plan limit's ``dimension``,
``plan``, ``limit`` and ``used``) — and the refusal's
``headers``, for one that carries a ``Retry-After``
(:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.demo.DemoError`'s ``demo_rate_limited``).

kastlan routes its refusals through ``DomainError`` and may keep mapping kit errors
there; the installer is the same answer without the mapping.

``{"detail": str(exc)}`` at the refusal's own ``status_code`` — the handler

A refusal with a ``code`` (:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.auth.AuthError`,
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.user_admin.AccountError`,

would.

methods.name: scope
methods.doc:
What ``viewer`` may list: their grant; for a review token, the grant with its
areas ``("kit",)``.

:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.translation_review.TranslationAccessError` (403), in this
order: a grant without a locale (:data:`NO_REVIEW_ACCESS`); a review token on a grant
with an area limit (:data:`NO_KIT_REVIEW_ACCESS`, T2) — a token lists every ``kit.``
verdict, more than a legal-only grant may see. keksdose refuses such a token at mint
and on every sign-in (``translation_review_token_service.py:59-71``, ``:133``); the
kit refuses it for every app.

methods.name: list_reviews
methods.doc:
``GET /translations/reviews``: every verdict the viewer may see, by locale, then key.

The store filters by area; the answer is filtered again by locale and
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.translation_review.in_areas`, so a store that answers too
much never shows a key outside the grant.

methods.name: save
methods.signature: async save(viewer: TranslationReviewer, items: Sequence[TranslationReviewWrite]) -> list[TranslationReviewOut]
methods.doc:
``PUT /translations/reviews``: a verdict on each item, replacing what was said before.

All or nothing: every pair is checked before anything is written. The last item per
``(locale, key)`` wins, in first-seen order. A blank ``note`` or ``suggestion`` is
``None``, and ``suggestion`` is dropped unless the verdict is ``NEEDS_CHANGE``. The
rows come back with the viewer's own name.

methods.name: clear
methods.signature: async clear(viewer: TranslationReviewer, keys: Sequence[tuple[str, str]]) -> int
methods.doc:
``POST /translations/reviews/clear``: the pairs back to unreviewed, after the same
checks as a save. Answers how many verdicts existed.

methods.name: export
methods.doc:
The account export's rows for ``data[VERDICTS_EXPORT_KEY]`` (§6.2.10, T1): keksdose's
shape (``account_export_service.py:375-387``), oldest first — ``locale``, ``string``
(the key: a bare ``key`` reads as a secret to
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.user_admin.assert_no_secrets`), ``text``, ``verdict`` (its
value), ``suggestion``, ``note`` (in that order, ``:383-384``), ``reviewed_at``.

members.name: TranslationReviewStore
members.doc:
The app's verdict rows, on the request's session (§6.2.3). Async; ``put`` and
``clear`` flush and never commit.

methods.name: verdicts
methods.signature: async verdicts(locales: Sequence[str], areas: Sequence[str] | None) -> Sequence[tuple[RowT, ReviewerName | None]]
methods.doc:
Every verdict in locales, and inside areas when given (None: every area), by
locale, then key, each with its reviewer's current name: an outer join, None once
the account is gone. The area filter comes from area_like_patterns, never by hand.

The row of each (locale, key), found or added, takes every field. Flush; the
rows in the order given. The kit sends each pair once.

members.name: TranslationReviewer
members.doc:
Who is reviewing (§6.2.2): the viewer of a list, the reviewer of a save or a clear.

One app dependency builds it from the app's own ``get_current_user``. ``grant`` is the
app's ``review_grant(…)``. keksdose's review token is this same view with
``kit_only=True``: its list is the area ``kit``, a write naming any other key is
refused whole, and a token on a grant with an area limit is refused its list.

fields.doc: The ``reviewer_id`` of what they write.

fields.doc: The reader's language: the order of ``reviewer_name`` (§6.2.5).

fields.doc: Signed in with a review token (keksdose): the kit's keys only.

fields.doc: The locales the CALLER may review, in the UI's order. Every locale for an admin.

The areas the caller is limited to (``["legal"]``; ``["kit"]`` for a review token),
NULL for every area.

members.name: TranslationVerdict
members.doc:
What a reviewer said about one string in one locale (keksdose ``models/translation_review.py:13``).

Two values, not a scale; "not looked at yet" is the ABSENCE of a row, and "changed since
it was looked at" is derived by comparing ``text`` with the bundle.

members.name: area_like_patterns
members.doc:
:func:`in_areas` as SQL ``LIKE`` patterns, for a listing that filters in the query.

Per area, the four arms of :func:`in_areas`: the key itself, ``<area>.%``, ``<area>:%``
and the kit's wording for it, ``kit.<area>.%`` — ``["legal"]`` gives ``["legal",
"legal.%", "legal:%", "kit.legal.%"]``. ``None`` (every area) is ``None``: no filter at
all. An empty list gives an empty list, and an ``OR`` of nothing matches nothing, as
``in_areas`` does.

Kurvenschmiede's finding after 0.2.1: a listing that narrows by area in SQL
(``key LIKE 'legal.%'``) never went through ``in_areas``, so the ``kit.<area>.`` arm
reached the write check and not the list. Build the filter from this, never by
hand, and the two cannot drift. ``%`` and ``_`` in an area are escaped with
:data:`LIKE_ESCAPE`; name it in the query. ``LIKE`` is case-sensitive in PostgreSQL,
as ``in_areas`` is; in SQLite only with ``PRAGMA case_sensitive_like = ON``::

    patterns = area_like_patterns(grant.areas)
    if patterns is not None:
        query = query.where(or_(*(Row.key.like(p, escape=LIKE_ESCAPE) for p in patterns)))

members.name: assert_allowed
members.signature: assert_allowed(grant: ReviewGrant, pairs: Iterable[tuple[str, str]], locale_codes: Sequence[str]) -> None
members.doc:
Every ``(locale, key)`` inside the grant, or nothing is written (keksdose ``_assert_allowed``, ``:115``).

An unknown locale is a :class:`TranslationLocaleError` (422); a locale or key outside
the grant a :class:`TranslationAccessError` (403).

members.name: can_review_kit
members.doc:
May this grant mint or use a review token? Some locale, and no area limit at all
(keksdose ``translation_review_token_service.py:57``).

0.12 (server services §6, decision T2): the same rule as
:meth:`~eifi1_server_kit.translation_review.TranslationReviewService.scope`, which
refuses a kit-only viewer on an area-limited grant. Until 0.11 an area covering
``kit.`` was let through here and refused there; no app has such a grant.

members.name: hash_review_token
members.doc: The SHA-256 hex digest the table stores (64 characters; keksdose ``_hash``).

members.name: in_areas
members.signature: in_areas(key: str, areas: Sequence[str] | None) -> bool
members.doc:
Whether ``key`` lies in one of ``areas`` — the area itself, anything under ``<area>.``
or ``<area>:``, or the kit's wording for it under ``kit.<area>.`` (``None`` = every
area; keksdose ``translation_review_service.py:91``).

The ``kit.<area>.`` arm is ui-kit 0.28's: the legal pages' shared sections are the kit's
words, flattened under ``kit.`` like all of them, so a reviewer granted ``["legal"]``
must reach ``kit.legal.*`` too — read and write — or the lawyer never sees the text all
three apps share (docs/legal-harmonization.md §7.5 in ui-kit). The ``<area>:`` arm is
0.10's, for kastlan's ``ns:key`` (``legal:imprint.title``; i18n-harmonization H1,
server-services §6.2.4). The kit's ``keyInArea`` applies the same four arms on the page.

members.doc: Is ``key`` the kit's own wording (keksdose ``translation_review_token_service.py:49``)?

members.doc: ``prefix`` + exactly 43 URL-safe characters.

members.doc: Does the Bearer value carry the review-token prefix? (keksdose ``looks_like_review_token``).

members.name: new_review_token
members.doc: A fresh raw token: ``prefix`` + 43 URL-safe characters. Show it once; store its hash.

members.name: normalize_areas
members.signature: normalize_areas(raw: Iterable[str] | None, review_areas: Sequence[str]) -> list[str] | None
members.doc: ``raw`` as known areas in ``review_areas`` order; ``None`` or empty = every area (keksdose ``:78``).

members.name: normalize_locales
members.doc:
``raw`` as shipped codes, de-duplicated, in ``locale_codes`` order (keksdose ``:61``).

Case-insensitive (``"DE-ch"`` is ``"de-CH"``) because a grant is typed by a person, but
never fuzzy: ``"de"`` is not ``"de-CH"``. An unknown code is a :class:`TranslationLocaleError`.

members.name: require_kit_keys
members.doc:
A review token reaches the kit's keys and nothing else: one other key in a batch
refuses the whole batch (keksdose ``translations_router.py:65`` ``_kit_keys_only``).

members.name: review_grant
members.signature: review_grant(profile: ReviewerProfile, *, is_admin: bool, is_reviewer: bool, locale_codes: Sequence[str], is_demo: bool = False) -> ReviewGrant
members.doc:
The caller's grant (keksdose ``allowed_locales`` / ``allowed_areas``, ``:96-112``).

An admin: every locale, every area. A reviewer: exactly the granted locales (in UI
order, unknown ones ignored) and the granted areas. Anyone else: nothing — the role is
the permission and the locales are its scope, so a leftover list grants nothing. A
demo session: nothing, whatever role it wears (keksdose ``review_grant_of``, made the
kit's in 0.10; server-services §6.2.2).

members.signature: review_token_expiry(now: datetime, hours: int = DEFAULT_REVIEW_TOKEN_HOURS) -> datetime
members.doc: When a token minted at ``now`` stops working; ``hours`` within 1–72.

members.name: review_token_is_live
members.signature: review_token_is_live(*, now: datetime, expires_at: datetime, revoked_at: datetime | None, created_at: datetime, sessions_invalid_before: datetime | None) -> bool
members.doc:
The token row's own half of keksdose's ``authenticate`` (``:105-123``): not revoked,
not expired, and not minted before the account's sessions were last invalidated.

The account's half — it exists, it is active, its grant still covers the kit
(:func:`eifi1_server_kit.translation_review.can_review_kit`) — is the app's.

members.doc:
The live tokens to revoke before minting one more, so at most ``cap`` stay live
(keksdose ``mint``: ``live[: max(0, len(live) - MAX_LIVE_TOKENS + 1)]``).

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.translation_review.router
modules.summary: The translation review routes as one router factory: ``translation_review_router(TranslationReviewDeps(...))``.
modules.doc:
The translation review routes as one router factory: ``translation_review_router(TranslationReviewDeps(...))``.

Layer 2 (``docs/server-services-harmonization.md`` §6.2.6–§6.2.8 in ``Eifi1/ui-kit``),
behind the ``fastapi`` extra (``eifi1-server-kit[fastapi]``). The app passes its own
dependencies — the reviewer view on its ``get_current_user`` (keksdose's also reads a
review token), the store on the request's session — and its UI locales, and includes the
router as it includes its own::

    router = translation_review_router(TranslationReviewDeps(
        reviewer=translation_reviewer, store=translation_review_store,
        locale_codes=UI_LOCALE_CODES,
    ))
    app.include_router(router, prefix="/api/v1")
    install_contract_error_handlers(app)

Mounted at ``/api/v1``, the paths are :data:`~eifi1_server_kit.cors.TRANSLATION_REVIEW_ROUTES`'s.

**No route guard** (§6.2.6): the three routes are "any signed-in", and the viewer's grant
gates each — a ``GET`` with no locale is 403, a write outside the grant 403. A demo is
granted nothing. **The endpoints carry keksdose's names** (``list_translation_reviews``,
``save_translation_reviews``, ``clear_translation_reviews``), so its and kastlan's
operation ids stay. An app's own routes (keksdose's review tokens, kastlan's
``GET /translations/documents``) go AFTER this router, on a router of their own.

**The router raises no** ``HTTPException`` (§6.2.8): past the app's ``reviewer``
dependency every refusal is layer 1's, answered by
:func:`~eifi1_server_kit.errors.install_contract_error_handlers`. The bodies are the
kit's models, which refuse unknown fields (T5), so a misspelt field is a 422 for every
app. Each request builds a
:class:`~eifi1_server_kit.translation_review.TranslationReviewService` on the request's
store; each makes at most one store write, as its last step, and the kit never commits.

No ``from __future__ import annotations`` here, on purpose: the parameters'
``Depends(deps.reviewer)`` and ``Depends(deps.store)`` name the factory's locals, and
FastAPI cannot resolve a string annotation that names a local.

modules.name: eifi1_server_kit.cors
modules.summary: CORS for a few EXTRA origins — exact origins, a few paths, and never with credentials.
modules.doc:
CORS for a few EXTRA origins — exact origins, a few paths, and never with credentials.

keksdose ``backend/keksdose/infrastructure/extra_origin_cors.py`` (its showcase CORS,
Marcel 2026-10-03), with the paths and the per-path methods / headers as parameters.

An app's own origin is served by Starlette's ``CORSMiddleware`` with
``allow_credentials=True``. No app sends a cookie today (the refresh token travels in the
JSON body), but that middleware has ONE policy for every origin it allows, so adding
another origin there would hand that origin credentialed requests too (and
``https://eifi1.github.io`` is every GitHub Pages site of the account). So the extra
origins get their own, smaller answer:

* **no credentials** — never ``Access-Control-Allow-Credentials``: they authenticate with
  a Bearer token (keksdose's review token) and nothing else;
* **listed paths only** — :class:`ExtraOriginRoute` per path, each with its own methods
  and request headers. Everywhere else such an origin gets no CORS headers at all, so the
  browser refuses to hand the response over;
* **preflight answered here** — 204 for an allowed path and method, 403 otherwise.
  ``CORSMiddleware`` answers a preflight from an origin it does not know with 400, so this
  layer MUST sit OUTSIDE it: add it AFTER ``CORSMiddleware`` (Starlette's
  ``add_middleware`` wraps outward), then call :func:`assert_outside_cors_middleware`;
* **the credentials leak stripped** — ``CORSMiddleware`` adds its "simple" headers,
  ``Allow-Credentials: true`` among them, to EVERY response that carries an ``Origin``,
  allowed or not; it only withholds ``Allow-Origin``. Beside this layer's
  ``Allow-Origin`` that would let a page on the extra origin read a cookie-carrying
  response. Measured in the test that pins it; removed from every response to an extra
  origin.

The endpoints still authorise every call themselves; this only decides what a browser on
that origin may read.

members.name: DEFAULT_MAX_AGE
members.doc: Ten minutes (keksdose): a showcase calls the same few paths over and over.

members.name: TRANSLATION_REVIEW_ROUTES
members.doc:
The kit showcase's routes (keksdose ``EXTRA_ORIGIN_PATHS``, ``extra_origin_cors.py:29-37``):
the public health ping it wakes a scaled-to-zero backend with, and the translation
review list / write / clear. keksdose allowed GET, PUT and POST on all three; here each
path has the methods the showcase actually sends to it.

members.doc: Narrow, credential-free CORS for ``origins`` on ``routes`` (see the module docstring).

methods.signature: __init__(app: ASGIApp, *, origins: Iterable[str], routes: Mapping[str, ExtraOriginRoute], max_age: int = DEFAULT_MAX_AGE) -> None

methods.name: __call__
methods.signature: async __call__(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None

members.name: ExtraOriginRoute
members.doc: What an extra origin may send to one path.

members.name: assert_outside_cors_middleware
members.doc:
Raise :class:`RuntimeError` unless :class:`ExtraOriginCorsMiddleware` wraps every
``CORSMiddleware`` of ``app`` — i.e. was added AFTER it.

Starlette's ``add_middleware`` inserts at the front of ``app.user_middleware`` and the
front is the outermost layer, so this layer's index must be lower than every
``CORSMiddleware``'s. Call it once at the end of ``create_app`` (or in a test).

members.name: parse_extra_origins
members.doc:
A setting's origins as exact origins, in order, each once.

keksdose ``infrastructure/settings.py:631`` ``cors_extra_origin_list``: separated by
commas or whitespace (whitespace is the safe form inside Cloud Build's comma-delimited
``--set-env-vars``); a trailing ``/`` is tolerated; anything that is not
``http(s)://host[:port]`` — a wildcard, a path, a query, a fragment, userinfo — is
DROPPED, as is the app's own origin, so a typo narrows the list instead of widening it.
